def fragment(text, pattern=_RADIOMETER, width=70) -> str:
    """The part of one entry that names the radiometer, rather than its first hundred characters.

    Several of these entries are whole-day visit reports in which the instrument is named once,
    halfway through; truncating from the start shows the drive to the site instead.
    """
    _m = re.search(pattern, str(text), re.I)
    if not _m:
        return str(text)[:2 * width]
    _lo, _hi = max(0, _m.start() - width), min(len(str(text)), _m.end() + width)
    return ('...' if _lo else '') + str(text)[_lo:_hi] + ('...' if _hi < len(str(text)) else '')

3️⃣ The June 2016 calibration change, measured in the data
A calibration error moves the clear-sky envelope but not the overcast ceiling, and it scales the envelope by the same factor at every percentile, which a change in the weather does not do. Both statistics are computed per month and per year over the whole record; yearly values stop at LAST_FULL_YEAR.

# The two statistics, on nighttime records with measured TA. The helpers raise rather than return
# a percentile built from a handful of half-hours.
LW_FINAL = lw_2005_2026[TARGET]
LWNET_NIGHT = net_longwave(LW_FINAL).where(NIGHT)
EMIS_NIGHT = emissivity(LW_FINAL).where(NIGHT)
CLEAR_Q = 0.02          # the clear-sky envelope
OVERCAST_Q = 0.95       # the overcast ceiling
MIN_PER_MONTH = 200


def monthly_q(series: pd.Series, q: float, minrec: int = MIN_PER_MONTH) -> pd.Series:
    """Monthly quantile of `series`, months with fewer than `minrec` records dropped."""
    s = series.dropna()
    v, n = s.resample('MS').quantile(q), s.resample('MS').count()
    out = v[n >= minrec]
    if out.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"no month reaches {minrec} records - the statistic has no support")
    return out


def yearly_q(series: pd.Series, q: float, minrec: int = MIN_PER_MONTH,
             minmonths: int = 10) -> pd.Series:
    """Yearly quantile, taken per calendar month and then averaged over months.

    Month-matched on purpose: this variable has a strong seasonal cycle in both statistics, so a
    year short of a winter must not be compared against one that is not. Years after
    LAST_FULL_YEAR are partial and excluded.
    """
    s = series.dropna()
    s = s[s.index.year <= LAST_FULL_YEAR]
    v = s.groupby([s.index.year, s.index.month]).quantile(q)
    v.index.names = ['year', 'month']
    n = s.groupby([s.index.year, s.index.month]).count()
    v = v[n >= minrec]
    keep = v.groupby(level=0).count()
    out = v.groupby(level=0).mean()
    out.index.name = 'YEAR'
    out = out[keep >= minmonths]
    if out.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"no year reaches {minmonths} months of at least {minrec} records")
    return out


def step_at(series: pd.Series, year: int, span: int = 3) -> float:
    """Percentage change of a yearly statistic across `year`, over `span` years either side.

    The candidate year itself is excluded from both sides: a change inside a year belongs to
    neither era. Returns nan when either side is thin, so a year at the edge of the record cannot
    win a scan by having almost no data behind it.
    """
    pre = series.reindex(range(year - span, year)).dropna()
    post = series.reindex(range(year + 1, year + 1 + span)).dropna()
    if len(pre) < 2 or len(post) < 2:
        return float('nan')
    return 100 * (post.mean() / pre.mean() - 1)


def matched_ratio(monthly: pd.Series, months, years_before, years_after) -> dict:
    """The clear-sky envelope over the same calendar months, before and after a date.

    Month-matched and close in time, which is what makes it a test of a date rather than of a
    decade: the same calendar months are compared, so the seasonal cycle cancels, and the two
    windows are adjacent, so a slow trend has little room to act. A candidate date inside a year
    is tested by splitting that year - the months before it against the same months of earlier
    years, and the months after it against the same months of earlier years.
    """
    a = monthly[monthly.index.month.isin(months) & monthly.index.year.isin(years_before)]
    b = monthly[monthly.index.month.isin(months) & monthly.index.year.isin(years_after)]
    if len(a) < len(months) or len(b) < max(1, int(0.8 * len(months))):
        raise ValueError(f"months {list(months)}: {len(a)} before and {len(b)} after reach the "
                         f"record threshold, too few to compare")
    return {'months compared': f'{len(a)} vs {len(b)}',
            'before (W m-2)': round(float(a.median()), 1),
            'after (W m-2)': round(float(b.median()), 1),
            'ratio': round(float(b.median() / a.median()), 4)}


def placebo_ratios(monthly: pd.Series, months, boundaries, span: int = 3) -> pd.Series:
    """The same statistic at every year of the record, on windows holding no known boundary.

    This is what the boundary values are read against. A year whose window straddles one of
    `boundaries` is dropped, because it would be reporting the very thing being tested.
    """
    out = {}
    for _y in range(int(monthly.index.year.min()) + span, int(monthly.index.year.max()) + 1):
        if any(_y - span <= pd.Timestamp(_b).year <= _y for _b in boundaries):
            continue
        try:
            out[_y] = matched_ratio(monthly, months, range(_y - span, _y), [_y])['ratio']
        except ValueError:
            continue
    if len(out) < 5:
        raise ValueError(f"only {len(out)} quiet years available - the reference distribution "
                         f"would be built on too little to mean anything")
    return pd.Series(out).sort_index()

ImportantThe exported series is not homogeneous across 7 June 2016



Values before that date use a factor 28 % too small and read low, in proportion to how clear the sky was. At the 17 % measured in step 3, that is about 8 W m-2 at the median of nighttime LW_net before the change and up to some 23 W m-2 at its 2nd percentile, a clear, dry night. Later values use the instrument’s own calibration.
This is not corrected. Undoing it means splitting each value into instrument emission and net signal, which needs the radiometer’s body temperature. This product does not read that channel, and its treatment in the processing chain of that era cannot be verified from the available files. Air temperature as a proxy would import an unverified model of that chain into the exported values.
Instead a SOURCE flag names the calibration era, and the size and shape of the offset are recorded here and on the documentation page. Users with the raw voltages or the body temperature can apply the correction; users of this product alone should filter on the flag.





4️⃣ The January 2016 acquisition change did nothing
Two independent results show this. The program installed at the changeover carries the same multiplier as the CR10X programs (step 1). And February to May 2016, new logger with old factor, lies inside the quiet-year range of the statistic that puts July to December 2016 far outside it.
The two dates are five months apart. Placing the break in January puts it in the wrong quarter and wrongly aligns it with the TA break.


5️⃣ The December 2021 boundary
Two candidate causes coincide: the radiometer replacement on 14 December 2021 and the end of the mst screening on 31 December 2021. Unlike 01, there is no external reference, only the same physics.
The median rises from about 316 W m-2 over 2019-2021 to about 326 over 2022-2024. The question is how much of that is weather, and whether the rest is a step at the boundary or a slower change.

That does not make the rest an instrument effect: a warmer atmosphere is also a moister one, and both raise the sky's emissivity. The tests below ask the different question of whether anything happens AT the boundary.




📋 Table: December 2021 against June 2016

# Step two: does anything happen AT the boundary? The same month-matched statistic as at June 2016,
# on the first half of 2022 against the first half of the three preceding years.
SCREENING_YEAR = 2022
_quiet_first = placebo_ratios(ENVELOPE_M, FIRSTHALF, BOUNDARIES)
DEC2021_TEST = matched_ratio(ENVELOPE_M, FIRSTHALF, [2019, 2020, 2021], [SCREENING_YEAR])

       "the same statistic at every year whose window holds neither boundary")

    f'Jan-Jun {SCREENING_YEAR} against {SCREENING_YEAR - 3}-{SCREENING_YEAR - 1}': DEC2021_TEST,
    'Jul-Dec 2016 against 2013-2015': JUN2016_TEST,
}).T

                            f'{_quiet_autumn.min():.3f} - {_quiet_autumn.max():.3f}']

      f"It moves it by about half as much as the calibration change did: "
      f"{100 * (1 - DEC2021_TEST['ratio']):.0f} % against "
      f"{100 * (1 - JUN2016_TEST['ratio']):.0f} %.")

assert DEC2021_TEST['ratio'] > JUN2016_TEST['ratio'], (
    "the December 2021 boundary now moves the clear-sky envelope by more than the June 2016 "
    "calibration change did, which would make it the larger of the two events and would need a "

# Step three: can the change be identified? A conversion factor scales every percentile of the
# tail by one number, as at June 2016. The pinned ceiling, which it cannot move, is shown too.
# Yearly values stop at LAST_FULL_YEAR (see yearly_q).
_QS = (0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)


def era_ratios(before, after):
    return pd.Series({f'p{int(100 * _q):02d}': float(
        yearly_q(LWNET_NIGHT, _q).loc[after[0]:after[1]].mean()
        / yearly_q(LWNET_NIGHT, _q).loc[before[0]:before[1]].mean()) for _q in _QS})


_LAB_2021 = f'across Dec 2021 (2022-{LAST_FULL_YEAR} / 2017-2021)'
_shape = pd.DataFrame({
    'across June 2016 (2017-2021 / 2006-2015)': era_ratios((2006, 2015), (2017, 2021)),
    _LAB_2021: era_ratios((2017, 2021), (2022, LAST_FULL_YEAR)),
    'a quiet interval (2012-2015 / 2007-2011)': era_ratios((2007, 2011), (2012, 2015)),
}).T
_shape['spread across percentiles'] = (_shape[[f'p{int(100 * _q):02d}' for _q in _QS]]
                                       .max(axis=1) - _shape[[f'p{int(100 * _q):02d}' for _q in _QS]]
                                       .min(axis=1)).round(4)
_shape['clear-sky change (%)'] = (100 * (_shape[[f'p{int(100 * _q):02d}' for _q in _QS]]
                                         .mean(axis=1) - 1)).round(2)
_shape['overcast ceiling change (%)'] = [round(step_at(CEILING_Y, 2016), 2),
                                         round(step_at(CEILING_Y, SCREENING_YEAR), 2),
                                         round(step_at(CEILING_Y, 2013), 2)]

       "is confined to the clear-sky end: both real changes move the clear-sky envelope by ten to "
       "twenty times what they move the pinned overcast ceiling. The spread column shows whether "
       "one factor describes the whole clear-sky tail: at June 2016 it does, at December 2021 no "
       "better than in a quiet interval")
display(_shape.round(4))

_spread_2016 = float(_shape.loc['across June 2016 (2017-2021 / 2006-2015)', 'spread across percentiles'])
_spread_2021 = float(_shape.loc[_LAB_2021, 'spread across percentiles'])
print(f"spread across percentiles: June 2016 {_spread_2016:.4f}, December 2021 {_spread_2021:.4f}")
for _row in _shape.index[:2]:
    _clear, _ceil = abs(_shape.loc[_row, 'clear-sky change (%)']), abs(_shape.loc[_row, 'overcast ceiling change (%)'])
    print(f"  {_row}: clear-sky {_clear:.1f} % against overcast ceiling {_ceil:.2f} %, "
          f"a factor of {_clear / _ceil:.0f}")
    assert _clear > 5 * _ceil, (
        f"{_row}: the change is no longer concentrated at the clear-sky end of the distribution, "
        f"which is where a conversion error acts and nowhere else")

    "the December 2021 change is now as cleanly multiplicative as the June 2016 one, which would "
    "make it identifiable as a conversion change and would change what this section concludes")
assert abs(step_at(CEILING_Y, SCREENING_YEAR)) < 1.0, (
    "the overcast ceiling now moves at the December 2021 boundary by as much as an ordinary "
    "change in the clear-sky end. It is pinned by physics, so a change in it would be a change in "
    "the measurement under overcast, which no conversion factor can produce")

      "what keeps both of them inside the part of the signal a conversion error can reach. Only "
      "one of them is described by a single factor.")

Both changes sit at the clear-sky end and barely touch the overcast ceiling, which is what keeps both of them inside the part of the signal a conversion error can reach. Only one of them is described by a single factor.








ImportantDecember 2021: a change this notebook cannot attribute



The record moves across the boundary, by most of the residual left after temperature. Three causes cannot be separated with these data:

the instrument. The CNR4 replaced the CNR1 on 14 December 2021. Its longwave factor is 10.85 µV/W/m², against the 12.83 the CNR1 had from June 2016.
the screening. mst ends on 31 December 2021 and diive begins on 1 January 2022, with no overlap.
the atmosphere. The clear-sky end of the record follows the temperature and humidity of the lower atmosphere. It shrank from 2019 to 2024, the direction a warmer, moister atmosphere would cause, and deepened again through 2025 and the dry year 2026. A gradual change of this kind cannot be separated from a step at the boundary.

At June 2016 one factor scaled the whole clear-sky tail and the fieldbook named it. Here the ratio across the tail is no steadier than in a quiet interval, and the fieldbook records the replacement but no reprocessing.
SW_IN, from the same radiometer, does not step across December 2021 against two independent references (notebook 01). That excludes a common-mode fault in wiring, logger or acquisition, but not a change in the pyrgeometer, a separate detector with its own calibration.
Nothing is corrected: correcting an unattributed change would replace a measurement with a guess, as 01 and 03 conclude for their drifts. The SOURCE flag separates the two instruments.




What this section settles
The four findings listed at the start of this section hold. The break of 7 June 2016 lies mid-record, is larger than anything at either hardware date, and is the main point for users. The series is homogeneous across January 2016, and December 2021 moves it by about half as much as June 2016, for no identifiable cause.
None of these is corrected: June 2016 needs a channel this product lacks, and December 2021 has no known cause. The export carries the measured series and the era flag. The assertions fail the run if the June 2016 step disappears, if a step appears between the two 2016 dates, or if December 2021 becomes the larger event.

title: Download and prepare LW_IN (2005-2026.09)
section: 🏷️ Provenance flag: which instrument and which calibration
text:
🏷️ Provenance flag: which instrument and which calibration
One column name spans two instruments and three calibration factors, so the file names the source of each value, using the dates derived above (two from the fieldbook, one from the logger program it records).
The changeover has its own code. The CNR4 was installed on 14 December 2021, but its constants reached the program only on 7 January 2022, so for three weeks it was read with the old factor. Neither fieldbook nor data can narrow this, so the interval is marked undetermined, as 08 does for its 71-day 2018 transition.

📋 Table: provenance flag by code

FLAGCOL = f'FLAG_{TARGET}_SOURCE'
# Written with inclusive end dates, so the legend reads the way a data user would filter.
_last_cnr1 = (pd.Timestamp(CNR4_INSTALLED) - pd.Timedelta(days=1)).date()
_last_undet = (pd.Timestamp(CNR4_CONSTANTS) - pd.Timedelta(days=1)).date()
_last_old_cal = (pd.Timestamp(CAL_CHANGE) - pd.Timedelta(days=1)).date()
SOURCE_LEGEND = {
    0: f'0 = CNR4 on its own calibration factor (from {CNR4_CONSTANTS})',
    1: f"1 = CNR1 at {SENSITIVITY_NEW} uV/W/m2, the pyrgeometer's own factor ({CAL_CHANGE} to "
       f'{_last_cnr1})',
    2: f'2 = CNR1 at {SENSITIVITY_OLD} uV/W/m2, the PYRANOMETER factor - reads low (to '
       f'{_last_old_cal})',
    3: f'3 = changeover, era undetermined ({CNR4_INSTALLED} to {_last_undet}): CNR4 installed, '
       f'CNR1 constants still in the program',
}

source = pd.Series(0, index=full_index, dtype='int8', name=FLAGCOL)
source.loc[:pd.Timestamp(CAL_CHANGE) - pd.Timedelta(minutes=15)] = 2
source.loc[pd.Timestamp(CAL_CHANGE):pd.Timestamp(CNR4_INSTALLED) - pd.Timedelta(minutes=15)] = 1
source.loc[pd.Timestamp(CNR4_INSTALLED):pd.Timestamp(CNR4_CONSTANTS) - pd.Timedelta(minutes=15)] = 3
# code 0 is what remains, from CNR4_CONSTANTS onwards

tabcap("the exported provenance flag by code. Code 2, the era that reads low, is about half the "
       "record; code 3 is the three weeks the evidence cannot assign to either instrument")
_flagtab = pd.DataFrame({
    'meaning': {c: SOURCE_LEGEND[c] for c in sorted(SOURCE_LEGEND)},
    'records': source.value_counts().reindex(sorted(SOURCE_LEGEND)).astype(int),
    'measured records': source.where(lw_2005_2026[TARGET].notna()).value_counts()
                              .reindex(sorted(SOURCE_LEGEND)).fillna(0).astype(int),
})
_flagtab['share of measured (%)'] = (100 * _flagtab['measured records']
                                     / _flagtab['measured records'].sum()).round(2)
_flagtab.index.name = 'code'
with pd.option_context('display.max_colwidth', 130):
    display(_flagtab)

# The flag covers the whole index once, and its boundaries are the dates derived above.
assert source.notna().all(), "the source flag is not defined everywhere"
assert set(source.unique()) == set(SOURCE_LEGEND), \
    "a code appears in the flag that the legend does not describe, or the other way round"
assert source.loc[:'2016-06-06 23:45'].eq(2).all() and source.loc['2016-06-07 00:15':'2021-12-14 23:45'].eq(1).all(), \
    "the two CNR1 eras no longer meet exactly at the calibration change"
assert int(source.eq(3).sum()) == len(pd.date_range(f'{CNR4_INSTALLED} 00:15',
                                                    pd.Timestamp(CNR4_CONSTANTS) - pd.Timedelta(minutes=15),
                                                    freq='30min')), \
    "the undetermined interval is not the interval between the two December/January dates"

🚫 No gap-filling here
As in notebook 05, the series is exported as measured:

LW_IN_T1_47_1 contains NaN; code assuming a complete series will fail or propagate it.
There is no FLAG_..._ISFILLED column. Non-null means measured.
A complete series, if needed, should be filled and flagged downstream. LW_IN is smooth and tied to air temperature and cloudiness, but a fill must respect the calibration eras the flag names rather than train one model across them.

title: Download and prepare RH (2004-2026.09)
text:
ℹ️ About this notebook
Downloads screened relative humidity RH from InfluxDB, merges the sources, corrects the August 2012 clock shift, removes the three damaged 2012 periods and the two probe half-hours of 2025 and 2026, applies the RH > 100% offset correction, identifies the instrument behind the column and the effect of its probe changes, fills every gap from NABEL and then MeteoSwiss Lägern, and writes the product to the external data folder. Up to the corrections it follows notebooks 01 (SW_IN), 02 (TA) and 03 (PPFD_IN). It reads 02’s product for the vapour pressure of steps 1️⃣1️⃣ and 1️⃣2️⃣, so 02 runs before this notebook.






ImportantThe measured series is not homogeneous across 21 January 2016 or 5 June 2026



RH_T1_47_1 comes from the same probe as TA_T1_47_1: a Rotronic MP101A (analog) until 21 January 2016, a Campbell CS215 (SDI-12) until 5 June 2026, then a Campbell HygroVUE10 (SDI-12). The 2016 change moved TA by about 1.3 °C (notebook 02) and RH by +2.1 to +3.3 percentage points, +3.9 to +4.1 away from the 100 % ceiling, a step attributed to the tower probe in the section Which sensor this is, and what the hardware change did to it. The 2026 change makes the series drier against MeteoSwiss Lägern, by an amount that grows with the humidity. In between, the CS215 heated abnormally in sun from 22 October 2024 (source code 7) and lost its daytime excess when it was handled on 16 May 2025 (code 6); in RH both are effects of the probe temperature (step 1️⃣1️⃣).
RH_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED puts the other probes on the CS215 level: the MP101A era is raised by a humidity-dependent transfer fitted against NABEL (same tower, 49 m) on the three years before the 2016 break and the CS215 record to July 2018, and scored against MeteoSwiss Lägern (step 🔟); the HygroVUE10 era is transferred in vapour pressure and converted back with 02’s homogenised temperature (step 1️⃣2️⃣). The CS215 is unchanged in all its states, codes 6 and 7 included. RH_T1_47_1 keeps every era as measured.
The 2016 correction depends on the reference. Fitted against Lägern instead of NABEL, it would raise the MP101A era by several tenths of a percentage point more on average and by up to about 2.4 percentage points more just below saturation (step 🔟). That difference is the uncertainty of the homogenised column across 2016.
The homogenised column removes the steps, not the drift or the probe heating. Against Lägern the MP101A era drifts downwards and the CS215 era upwards, each by a few tenths of a percentage point a year (computed in step 🔟); neither drift is corrected, so a multi-year trend carries it. Codes 7 and 6 keep their sun-dependent RH errors, and from June 2026 the homogenised RH refers to 02’s homogenised temperature, so in sun it lies above what a CS215 would read.








ImportantWhat this notebook does and does not do



Gaps are reconstructed from another measurement of the same quantity, offset-corrected month by month within the sensor era; nothing is modelled. NABEL at 49 m (same tower, 2004-2018) fills first (flag 3), MeteoSwiss Lägern (2.5 km, 2004-2026) the rest, chiefly after 2018 (flag 4, larger uncertainty). The exported series is complete.


Output columns

RH_T1_47_1: corrected, gap-free series (%), every era as measured
FLAG_RH_T1_47_1_MISSING: 0 measured at 47 m, 3 from NABEL (49 m), 4 from MeteoSwiss Lägern (2.5 km); 1 (never measured) and 2 (removed as faulty) are in FLAG_LEGEND but do not occur
RH_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED: the same series on the CS215 level (%): records before 21 January 2016 raised by the 2016 transfer, records from 5 June 2026 by the vapour pressure transfer relative to 02’s homogenised temperature, the CS215 (codes 0, 6, 7) and the probe half-hours unchanged; drift within each era and the probe heating of codes 6 and 7 are not corrected
FLAG_RH_T1_47_1_SOURCE: probe generation and state, the codes of 02: 0 Campbell CS215, 1 Rotronic MP101A, 2 changeover outage, era undetermined, 3 before the tower record begins, 4 Campbell HygroVUE10, 5 the probe half-hours of 16 May 2025 and 5 June 2026, reconstructed with the era before each, 6 the CS215 after 16 May 2025, 7 the CS215 with excess daytime heating from 22 October 2024

Unlike the ISFILLED flag of 01-03, the provenance codes name no model. Filter FLAG_RH_T1_47_1_MISSING == 0 for genuine 47 m measurements. Use RH_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED for statistics across 2016 or June 2026, and read FLAG_RH_T1_47_1_SOURCE to tell the eras and probe states apart.
InfluxIO needs influxdb-client, installed by uv sync through the diive[db] extra.

📇 Data sources
Series

RH_T1_47_1: ETH, 47 m, the product series. mst 2004-2021, diive 2022-2026. Three probes under one name (Rotronic MP101A, Campbell CS215, Campbell HygroVUE10), see the sensor-identity section.
RH_NABEL_T1_49_1: NABEL, 49 m, same tower, separate acquisition system, 2004-2018; independent until August 2018 (derived below). Reference for the 2012 diagnostics and the sensor-identity section, and first reconstruction source. Not exported.

Captions

# Caption helpers, copied as-is from notebook 03 (its figcap() carries the PlaceHolderLayoutEngine
# fix). Defined above their first use.
def tabcap(text, width=100):
    """Print a table caption, above the table it belongs to."""
    print(textwrap.fill(f"Table - {text}", width) + "\n")


def figcap(fig, text, width=125):
    """Place a caption under a figure. Call after the last axes of that figure is drawn."""
    width = min(width, max(40, int(14.5 * fig.get_size_inches()[0])))
    caption = textwrap.fill(f"Figure - {text}", width)
    # An engine that still lays the figure out at draw time can make room for a caption itself.
    # plt.tight_layout() does NOT leave one: it executes once and leaves a PlaceHolderLayoutEngine
    # that never runs again, so a caption handed to supxlabel there lands on top of the tick
    # labels. Those figures take the manual branch below.
    _engine = fig.get_layout_engine()
    if _engine is not None and type(_engine).__name__ != 'PlaceHolderLayoutEngine':
        fig.supxlabel(caption, fontsize=9, ha='left', x=0.005)
        return
    lines = len(caption.splitlines())
    extra = 0.17 * lines + 0.12          # inches; one caption line is about 0.17 in at fontsize 9
    width_in, height_in = fig.get_size_inches()
    fig.set_size_inches(width_in, height_in + extra)
    keep = height_in / (height_in + extra)
    offset = extra / (height_in + extra)
    for ax in fig.axes:
        pos = ax.get_position()
        ax.set_position([pos.x0, offset + pos.y0 * keep, pos.width, pos.height * keep])
    fig.text(0.005, 0.01, caption, fontsize=9, ha='left', va='bottom')



Helper functions
The shared helpers: the RH > 100% correction, the offset transfer used by both reconstruction passes, and two plotting helpers. The plot helpers of 01 and 03 split a series by a gap-filling flag; these split by provenance. Each builds its own caption from the data it is given.

def remove_rh_offset_by_year(series: pd.Series, showplot: bool = False):
    """Apply diive's `RH > 100%` offset correction within each year that contains a value > 100%.

    The library function derives a daily offset from the records above 100% and interpolates and
    ffill/bfills it over the whole index. One call on the full record would also shift years that
    never exceed 100%: a flat +0.71 % over 2004-2006 (bfilled from 2007) and a flat +0.133 % from
    2016 on (ffilled from 2015). A sensor reading 102 at a true 100 is biased over its whole range,
    so the offset is subtracted from every record of an exceedance year; years without evidence of
    drift come through bit-identical.

    A year is also split at every date of PROBE_STATE_CHANGES (the CS215 changes of 2024-2025 and
    the June 2026 probe change), and each part is corrected only if it holds a value > 100% itself:
    an offset derived from one probe state is never subtracted from another's records. Years
    without such a date are corrected exactly as before.

    The library function renames the series it is given in place, so it gets a copy.

    Returns (corrected series, list of years the correction ran in).
    """
    out = series.copy()
    years = sorted({int(y) for y in series.index.year[series > 100]})
    segment = sum(np.asarray(series.index >= _d, dtype=int) for _d in PROBE_STATE_CHANGES)
    for year in years:
        for part in np.unique(segment):
            locs = (series.index.year == year) & (segment == part)
            if not (series.loc[locs] > 100).any():
                continue
            out.loc[locs] = dv.corrections.remove_relativehumidity_offset(
                series.loc[locs].copy(), showplot=showplot)
    return out, years


def monthly_offset_table(target: pd.Series, reference: pd.Series, era: pd.Series,
                         window_years: int = None, min_samples: int = None) -> pd.Series:
    """Additive offset `target - reference` per (era, year, month), fitted on a local year window.

    The offset varies seasonally (about +3.9 % RH in February, +0.4 % RH in August), drifts over
    the record (annual mean +0.08 % RH in 2006, +5.06 % RH in 2017; a pooled offset would apply
    +3.42 % RH to January 2004 where the local evidence gives +1.35 % RH), and steps by 2 to 4
    percentage points at the January 2016 probe replacement. `era` labels the sensor generation of
    every record and each era is fitted only on its own overlap, so no record is reconstructed
    with a relationship from across the break (the failure notebook 02 documents for gap-filling
    models).

    Within an era, each month of each year is fitted on the overlap within +/- `window_years`
    calendar years. A month with fewer than `min_samples` local records falls back to the era's
    pooled monthly offset, a month absent from the era's overlap to its pooled mean. An era with
    no overlap raises instead of returning a table of NaNs.

    Returns a Series indexed by (era, year, month).
    """
    window_years = OFFSET_WINDOW_YEARS if window_years is None else window_years
    min_samples = OFFSET_MIN_SAMPLES if min_samples is None else min_samples

    years = range(int(target.index.year.min()), int(target.index.year.max()) + 1)
    rows = {}
    for era_code in sorted(pd.unique(era)):
        _in_era = (era == era_code).reindex(target.index).fillna(False)
        overlap = pd.concat([target.where(_in_era).rename('t'), reference.rename('r')],
                            axis=1).dropna()
        if overlap.empty:
            raise ValueError(
                f"sensor era {era_code!r} has no overlap between the two series, so no offset can "
                f"be fitted for it. Reconstructing its records from another era's offset is "
                f"exactly what this split exists to prevent.")
        diff = overlap.t - overlap.r
        pooled_monthly = diff.groupby(diff.index.month).mean()
        pooled_mean = float(diff.mean())
        for year in years:
            near = diff[(diff.index.year >= year - window_years) &
                        (diff.index.year <= year + window_years)]
            grouped = near.groupby(near.index.month)
            local_mean, local_n = grouped.mean(), grouped.size()
            for month in range(1, 13):
                if month in local_mean.index and local_n.get(month, 0) >= min_samples:
                    rows[(era_code, year, month)] = float(local_mean[month])
                elif month in pooled_monthly.index:
                    rows[(era_code, year, month)] = float(pooled_monthly[month])
                else:
                    rows[(era_code, year, month)] = pooled_mean
    return pd.Series(rows).rename('offset')


def reconstruct_from_reference(target: pd.Series, reference: pd.Series, offsets: pd.Series,
                               era: pd.Series):
    """Fill gaps in `target` with offset-corrected `reference` values, clipped to [0, 100].

    Each record takes the offset fitted for **its own** sensor era, so a record on one side of the
    January 2016 probe replacement is never reconstructed with a relationship fitted on the other.

    Only records where `target` is missing AND `reference` has a value are touched; everything
    else comes back untouched. Returns (reconstructed series, boolean mask of what was filled).
    """
    filled = target.isna() & reference.notna()
    keys = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays([era[filled].values,
                                      target.index[filled].year, target.index[filled].month])
    applied = offsets.reindex(keys).values
    if np.isnan(applied).any():
        raise ValueError("no offset available for some records to reconstruct")

    out = target.copy()
    out.loc[filled] = np.clip(reference.loc[filled].values + applied, 0, 100)
    return out, filled


def plot_presence_panels(series, flag, title, ylabel='RH (%)', figsize=(16, 8)):
    """Stacked panels: the exported series, then each provenance class on its own, so a block of
    reconstructed records at the wrong level, or an unexpected gap class, is visible. The caption
    is built from the data the helper is given.
    """
    _plotdf = pd.DataFrame({
        'RH (all values)': series,
        'measured at 47 m': series.where(flag == 0),
        'reconstructed from NABEL (49 m)': series.where(flag == 3),
        'reconstructed from Lägern (2.5 km)': series.where(flag == 4),
        'missing (never measured / removed)': flag.where(flag.isin([1, 2])),
    })
    axs = _plotdf.plot(subplots=True, figsize=figsize, x_compat=True, alpha=.9,
                       title=title, legend=True)
    for ax in axs[:4]:
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    axs[4].set_ylabel('flag')
    plt.tight_layout()
    figcap(axs[0].get_figure(),
           f"{title}. Top: every exported value. Below: each provenance class on its own, where a "
           f"reconstructed block at the wrong level would show: {int((flag == 0).sum()):,} "
           f"measured at 47 m, {int((flag == 3).sum()):,} reconstructed from NABEL at 49 m, "
           f"{int((flag == 4).sum()):,} reconstructed from MeteoSwiss Lägern. The bottom panel is "
           f"empty: no record is left without a value.")
    return axs


def coverage_stats_by_year(series, flag, legend=None):
    """Records per year by provenance class, with a bar chart of the reconstructed ones."""
    legend = legend or FLAG_LEGEND
    _pe = pd.Timestamp(PERIOD_END)
    tab = (pd.crosstab(flag.index.year, flag)
             .rename(columns=lambda f: legend.get(f, f))
             .rename_axis(index='year', columns=None))
    tab.insert(0, 'records', series.groupby(series.index.year).size())
    nonmeasured = tab.drop(columns=['records'] + [c for c in tab.columns
                                                  if str(c).startswith('0 =')], errors='ignore')
    if not nonmeasured.empty and nonmeasured.to_numpy().sum() > 0:
        ax = nonmeasured.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, figsize=(14, 4),
                              title='Non-measured records per year, by provenance')
        ax.set_ylabel('records')
        ax.legend(fontsize=8)
        plt.tight_layout()
        _tot = nonmeasured.sum(axis=1)
        figcap(ax.get_figure(),
               f"reconstructed records per year and source (measured records omitted). The most "
               f"heavily reconstructed year is {int(_tot.idxmax())} with {int(_tot.max()):,} "
               f"records, almost all before the sensor was connected; "
               f"{int((_tot < 100).sum())} of the {len(_tot)} years carry fewer than a hundred "
               f"reconstructed records each. {_pe:%Y} is partial and ends in {_pe:%B}.")
    tabcap(f"records per year and provenance code. Every record carries a code and a value, so the "
           f"rows sum to the half-hours in each year; {_pe:%Y} is partial and ends in {_pe:%B}")
    return tab

text:
✴️ Corrections

Order of the correction steps

Timestamp shift (August 2012). Later windows refer to the corrected axis.
Removal of the three damaged 2012 periods and of the two probe half-hours of May 2025 and June 2026. Some of the 2012 records read above 100%.
RH > 100% offset correction. Its offset is the daily mean of the records above 100%, so the damaged records must be gone first; otherwise they would set the offset subtracted from good data on neighbouring days. Step 2 reports how many removed records exceeded 100%.

The two reconstruction passes (NABEL, then MeteoSwiss Lägern) run last, so that every gap exists and the offsets are fitted on corrected 47 m data. Step 2 creates gaps, so their provenance is recorded before step 3; step 3 is checked not to write into gaps, as the correction in notebook 03 does.


Timestamp shift in August 2012
Info from fieldbook entry 17 Aug 2012: > adjusted the logger date and time. On Servertime (Computer System Time) 17.08.2012 12:31.42 the loggertime was 16.08.2012 08:06:00. Synchronized time at 17.08.2012 11:40:00 servertime. The logger data aquisition on the moxa embedded was restarted
A logger clock error affects every variable on that logger. The correction of notebooks 01-03 is applied to RH_T1_47_1 after a day-by-day lag search against NABEL (August baseline agreement about 2.0 %, see the monthly table further down):

📊 Plot: the August 2012 clock shift, panel by panel

AFFECTED_VARS = [TARGET]
_df = rh_2004_2026.copy()

for av in AFFECTED_VARS:
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(24, 6), dpi=72)
    fig.suptitle(f"{av}")
    gs = gridspec.GridSpec(1, 5)  # rows, cols
    gs.update(wspace=0.5, hspace=1, left=.1, right=.9, top=.85, bottom=.1)
    ax_before = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
    ax_unshifted = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
    ax_shifted = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
    ax_after = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 3])
    ax_corrected = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 4])

    # Show time period around issue, before correction
    _show_locs = (_df.index >= '2012-08-01 00:00') & (_df.index <= '2012-09-01 00:00')
    dv.plotting.HeatmapDateTime(series=_df.loc[_show_locs, av]).plot(
        ax=ax_before, cb_digits_after_comma=0, zlabel='%',
        format_style=dv.plotting.FormatStyle(title="Before correction", title_fontsize=11))

    # Get shifted time period
    _series_corrected = _df.loc[_show_locs, av].copy()
    # Identify shifted time period
    ISSUE_START = '2012-08-09 00:00'
    ISSUE_END = '2012-08-17 00:00'
    _shifted_locs = (_df.index >= ISSUE_START) & (_df.index <= ISSUE_END)
    _series_shifted = _df.loc[_shifted_locs, av].copy()
    _series_shifted = _series_shifted.dropna()
    dv.plotting.HeatmapDateTime(series=_series_shifted).plot(
        ax=ax_unshifted, cb_digits_after_comma=0, zlabel='%',
        format_style=dv.plotting.FormatStyle(title="UNSHIFTED time period", title_fontsize=11))

    # Shift by 15.5 hours during shifted time period, create corrected time series
    _series_shifted.index = _series_shifted.index + pd.Timedelta(hours=15.5)
    dv.plotting.HeatmapDateTime(series=_series_shifted).plot(
        ax=ax_shifted, cb_digits_after_comma=0, zlabel='%',
        format_style=dv.plotting.FormatStyle(title="SHIFTED time period", title_fontsize=11))

    # Delete data between start of issue and the last timestamp of shifted data
    _overwrite_locs = (_df.index >= ISSUE_START) & (_df.index <= _series_shifted.index[-1])
    _df.loc[_overwrite_locs, av] = np.nan
    dv.plotting.HeatmapDateTime(series=_df.loc[_show_locs, av]).plot(
        ax=ax_after, cb_digits_after_comma=0, zlabel='%',
        format_style=dv.plotting.FormatStyle(title="After deletion", title_fontsize=11))

    # Fill in corrected values
    _df.loc[_overwrite_locs, av] = _series_shifted
    dv.plotting.HeatmapDateTime(series=_df.loc[_show_locs, av]).plot(
        ax=ax_corrected, cb_digits_after_comma=0, zlabel='%',
        format_style=dv.plotting.FormatStyle(title="After correction", title_fontsize=11))

    figcap(fig, f"the August 2012 logger clock error in {av} and its repair. Left to right: the "
                f"month as recorded, with the moist night band displaced into the afternoon; the "
                f"affected block; the block shifted by 15.5 hours, with the moist band back at "
                f"night; the month with the block removed; the month with the shifted block "
                f"written back. The shift is the one in the fieldbook entry above and in "
                f"notebooks 01, 02 and 03.")
    print(f"{av}: {len(_series_shifted)} records moved +15.5 h, "
          f"last shifted timestamp {_series_shifted.index[-1]}")

Agreement collapses from 29 October, stays at 12-33 % through 9 November and recovers from 12 November, after the repair visit:

01.11.2012 Checked Forestfloor and Hut for broken sensors due to fallen trees and big branches
06.11.2012 checked all sensor cables. especialy the cables at the forest floor are sometimes strongly stressed. tried to unstress the cables

Both entries name forest floor sensors, not the 47 m instruments, so the link is circumstantial.


Where RH disagrees with the shared windows
The windows are those of SW_IN, TA and PPFD_IN, kept unchanged so that all four products exclude the same periods (notebook 07 combines RH with TA for VPD). Two are wider than the RH evidence requires:

Window 1 starts 29 July; RH is healthy that day (2.31 % against 2.0 %) and degrades from 30 July.
Window 3 starts 28 October; RH is acceptable that day (2.52 % at zero lag) and degrades from 29 October.
Window 2 (the tail after the last shifted value) holds 17 RH records that agree at 1.1 %.

About 113 good records are affected. NABEL covers all three windows, so they are reconstructed (about 3 % uncertainty), not lost. Notebook 02 made the same trade-off for TA.

📊 Plot: 2012 after removing the damaged periods

# Three damaged 2012 periods, documented in the fieldbook and not repairable. Windows are on the
# corrected time axis (after the +15.5 h shift) and identical to notebooks 01, 02 and 03.
BAD_WINDOWS_2012 = [
    ('2012-07-29 00:00', '2012-08-10 15:30'),  # tower power supply failure (fieldbook 09.08.2012)
    ('2012-08-17 15:30', '2012-08-18 00:00'),  # transitional tail after the last shifted value
    ('2012-10-28 00:00', '2012-11-10 00:00'),  # storm damage, stressed cables (fieldbook 01./06.11.2012)
]

# Recorded per record, not just counted: this is what separates flag 2 from flag 1 on export.
removed_here = pd.Series(False, index=rh_2004_2026.index)
_exceeded_and_removed = 0
for _start, _end in BAD_WINDOWS_2012:
    _locs = (rh_2004_2026.index >= _start) & (rh_2004_2026.index <= _end)
    _measured = _locs & rh_2004_2026[TARGET].notna()
    _exceeded_and_removed += int((rh_2004_2026.loc[_measured, TARGET] > 100).sum())
    removed_here |= _measured
    rh_2004_2026.loc[_locs, TARGET] = np.nan

print(f"Removed {int(removed_here.sum())} measured records from {TARGET}.")
print("These become gaps here; the reconstruction section below fills them from NABEL.")
print(f"Of these, {_exceeded_and_removed} read above 100% - they would otherwise have")
print(f"contributed to the offset of the RH>100% correction, which is why that step runs after this one.")

# One heatmap pair per affected period, with the NABEL sensor as the reference.
for _lo, _hi, _label in [('2012-07-15', '2012-09-01', 'July-August'),
                         ('2012-10-20', '2012-11-20', 'October-November')]:
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(ncols=2, figsize=(11, 7), dpi=100, layout="constrained")
    fig.suptitle(f'{_label} 2012 after removing the degraded periods', fontsize=14)
    _show = (rh_2004_2026.index >= _lo) & (rh_2004_2026.index <= _hi)
    dv.plotting.HeatmapDateTime(series=rh_2004_2026.loc[_show, TARGET]).plot(
        ax=axs[0], cb_digits_after_comma=0, zlabel='%',
        format_style=dv.plotting.FormatStyle(title=TARGET, title_fontsize=11))
    dv.plotting.HeatmapDateTime(series=rh_2004_2026.loc[_show, REFERENCE]).plot(
        ax=axs[1], cb_digits_after_comma=0, zlabel='%',
        format_style=dv.plotting.FormatStyle(title=f'{REFERENCE} (reference)', title_fontsize=11))
    figcap(fig, f"{_label} 2012 after removing the damaged records, with the NABEL sensor "
                f"beside it. The removed window is grey on the left and present on the right; the "
                f"records either side carry the reference's diurnal pattern, and the reference "
                f"spans the window apart from a short outage of its own in late August. These "
                f"records are reconstructed below and flagged.")

The probe-handling and probe-swap half-hours
Two half-hours hold a probe being handled and represent no stable state of either probe, so both are removed here and reconstructed with the other gaps (source code 5, as in notebook 02).

16 May 2025, 09:30-10:00 (HANDLING_RECORD). The CS215 was handled between 09:32 and 09:42, when the raw 1-min TA_T1_47_1 jumps while the 35 m sensor does not (02, step 1️⃣1️⃣). It belongs to the period before the handling: its reconstruction offset is fitted on the code 7 era. Step 1️⃣1️⃣ treats this change.
5 June 2026, 11:00-11:30 (SWAP_RECORD). The HygroVUE10 replaced the CS215: the raw 1-min TA_T1_47_1, measured by the same probe call, stops at 11:10 and resumes at 11:31, so the 30MIN value is a mean over at most ten minutes of CS215 output. It belongs to the period before the change: its offset is fitted on the code 6 era, and it receives no HygroVUE10 transfer. Step 1️⃣2️⃣ treats this change.

RH > 100% correction
Values above 100% indicate sensor drift near saturation. dv.corrections.remove_relativehumidity_offset derives a daily offset from the records above 100%, subtracts it from the series and clips what still exceeds 100%.
Scope. The library ffill/bfills the offset over the whole index, so one call on the full record would also shift years without any exceedance: +0.71 % over 2004-2006 and +0.133 % from 2016 to the end of the record. remove_rh_offset_by_year runs it per exceedance year; other years come through bit-identical. A year holding the June 2026 probe change is also split at HV_START, so one probe’s offset is never applied to the other.
Guarantees

RH <= 100 in every year: clipped where the correction runs, true by construction elsewhere. The export check asserts it.
RH >= 0 is not guaranteed, because the lower end is not clipped. With offsets of at most 2.0 % it does not occur here, and the export check asserts it.
A saturated sensor is not repaired: resolution lost near 100% is not recovered.

Gap safety. NaN - x is NaN, so gaps are retained. The cell below checks it, because the analogous correction in notebook 03 turned 7,543 fills into apparent measurements.

title: Download and prepare RH (2004-2026.09)
section: 🔎 Which sensor this is, and what the hardware change did to it
text:
🔎 Which sensor this is, and what the hardware change did to it
RH_T1_47_1 and TA_T1_47_1 come from one instrument, replaced with its logger on 21 January 2016; in TA this required a two-term correction and a homogenised column (notebook 02). The steps below show that RH moved too:

the column holds two probes, a Rotronic MP101A (analog) until January 2016 and a Campbell CS215 (SDI-12) after, each named in the logger programs of its era;
the changeover is a 20-day outage in the data, which dates the boundary;
NABEL stops being independent in August 2018 and is cut there;
the series steps upwards by 2.1 to 3.3 percentage points of RH, and the pairs that move name the tower probe;
the 100 % ceiling hides part of the step, which depends strongly on the humidity;
the step is present at every hour and larger at night, which rules out the shield mechanism of the TA step;
the replaced probe had drifted, on evidence that needs no reference;
there is no step at the December 2021 screening splice, although the median rises across those years;
the maintenance record identifies neither of the first two probes; it files a HygroVUE10 here on 5 June 2026;
a humidity-dependent transfer across 2016 is unstable when fitted on the era means and stable when fitted against NABEL at the break, where it removes the step against Lägern; it depends on the reference, and the drift within the eras remains;
the CS215 changed state in 2024-2025, and in RH the change is one of the probe’s temperature, not of its humidity element;
the HygroVUE10 of June 2026 reads drier than the CS215 in vapour pressure and is transferred onto its level.

The consequences close the section.

Helpers for this section
The logger programs and the fieldbook are read, not quoted, so a re-run re-derives the argument. Both name people and this page is public, so every string taken from them is redacted as in notebooks 01, 02, 03 and 08.

# --- Fieldbook and logger-program redaction ----------------------------------------------------
# Both sources name people and this page is public, so every string taken from either passes
# through redact_people(). Same map and rules as notebooks 01, 02, 03 and 08; the map lives beside
# the export, outside this repository.
REDACT_MAP = Path(FIELDBOOK).with_name('redact_names.csv')
ALLOW_LIST = Path(FIELDBOOK).with_name('redact_allow.csv')


def unmapped_report_path(label: str) -> Path:
    """Where the unmapped-name candidates of one audit are written.

    Per label, because this notebook audits three sources: a single shared file would let a later
    audit overwrite an earlier one's findings.
    """
    _slug = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', label.lower()).strip('_')
    return Path(FIELDBOOK).with_name(f'redact_unmapped_{_slug}.txt')


def load_redactions(path=None) -> dict:
    """Load the name -> pseudonym map.

    Raises if the map is missing. That is the point: carrying on with redaction quietly disabled
    prints real names into a published page and looks exactly like success.
    """
    path = REDACT_MAP if path is None else Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"the redaction map is missing: {path}. Without it the names these files record would "
            f"print unredacted. Restore the file rather than skipping this.")
    tab = pd.read_csv(path, encoding='utf-8')
    missing = {'name', 'pseudonym'}.difference(tab.columns)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: missing column(s) {sorted(missing)}.")
    pairs = {str(n).strip(): str(p).strip()
             for n, p in zip(tab['name'], tab['pseudonym']) if str(n).strip()}
    if not pairs:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: holds no usable name -> pseudonym pairs.")
    return pairs


REDACTIONS = load_redactions()
# Longest surface form first, so a bare surname cannot corrupt a double-barrelled one that starts
# with it. Lookarounds rather than \b, because some forms end in an initial.
_REDACT_RX = re.compile(r'(?<!\w)(' + '|'.join(re.escape(n) for n in
                                               sorted(REDACTIONS, key=len, reverse=True))
                        + r')(?!\w)')


def redact_people(s) -> str:
    """Replace every mapped name with its stable pseudonym."""
    return _REDACT_RX.sub(lambda m: REDACTIONS[m.group(1)], str(s))


def strip_html(text) -> str:
    """Flatten one GIN fieldbook entry to plain text, with the people it names redacted."""
    flat = html.unescape(re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', str(text)))
    return redact_people(re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', flat).strip())


_NAME_TOKEN = r"[A-ZÄÖÜ][\wÄÖÜäöüß'-]{1,20}"
_NAME_UNIT = _NAME_TOKEN + r'(?:\s+' + _NAME_TOKEN + r'){0,2}'
_NAME_SHAPES = (
    re.compile(r'\((' + _NAME_UNIT + r'(?:\s*[,+&]\s*' + _NAME_UNIT + r')*)\s*'
               r'(?:\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}\.\d{4})?\)'),
    re.compile(r'(?:with|by|durch|von|gemaess)\s+(' + _NAME_TOKEN + r'(?:\s+' + _NAME_TOKEN + r')?)'),
)


def audit_unmapped_names(texts, label='fieldbook', write_report: bool = True) -> int:
    """Raise if any name-shaped token survived redaction.

    A newer export can name someone the map has never seen. Candidates are never printed - an
    exception message is stored in a notebook like any other output - so they go to a file beside
    the map and only the count is shown.
    """
    allow = set(pd.read_csv(ALLOW_LIST, encoding='utf-8')['term'].astype(str).str.strip())
    found = {}
    for _t in texts:
        for _rx in _NAME_SHAPES:
            for _m in _rx.finditer(str(_t)):
                for _tok in re.findall(_NAME_TOKEN, _m.group(1)):
                    if _tok.isupper() or any(ch.isdigit() for ch in _tok) or _tok in allow:
                        continue
                    found[_tok] = found.get(_tok, 0) + 1
    if found:
        _report = unmapped_report_path(label)
        if write_report:
            _report.write_text(
                '\n'.join(f'{n}\t{t}' for t, n in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])),
                encoding='utf-8')
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label}: {len(found)} name-shaped token(s) survived redaction. They are deliberately "
            f"NOT shown here - see {_report}. Add the people to redact_names.csv and the "
            f"technical terms to redact_allow.csv, then re-run.")
    print(f"  {label}: no unmapped name-shaped tokens ({len(allow)} allowlisted terms)")
    return 0


def program_excerpt(path, pattern: str, before: int = 6, after: int = 4, expect: int = 1) -> str:
    """The lines of a logger program around `pattern`, redacted.

    Only the matched instruction is returned, never the file header: these programs are signed by
    their authors. Raises unless the pattern matches exactly `expect` times. Both directions
    matter: no match reads as 'the program does not measure this', and an over-broad pattern
    quietly prints the wrong instruction next to the argument it is supposed to support.
    """
    lines = Path(path).read_text(encoding='latin-1').splitlines()
    blocks = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if re.search(pattern, line):
            lo, hi = max(0, i - before), min(len(lines), i + after + 1)
            blocks.append('\n'.join(lines[lo:hi]))
    if len(blocks) != expect:
        raise ValueError(f"{Path(path).name}: {pattern!r} matched {len(blocks)} time(s), expected "
                         f"{expect}. The program layout has changed, the wrong file is configured, "
                         f"or the pattern is not specific enough.")
    return redact_people('\n\n'.join(blocks))


def calibration_constants(excerpt: str) -> dict:
    """The multiplier and offset of one measurement instruction, parsed from its own text.

    The CR10X lists the two numbers as numbered parameters of a `Volt (SE)` instruction; the
    CR1000 passes them as the last two arguments of a `VoltSe(...)` or `VoltDiff(...)` call. Both
    shapes are matched on their own terms.

    Raises if either number cannot be found. That failure path is not a defect here, it is the
    argument: the CR1000 reads this sensor over **SDI-12**, which returns finished engineering
    units, so its instruction carries no multiplier and no offset at all and this function raises
    on it. A version that returned an empty result instead would let the two eras be compared by
    having nothing to disagree about.
    """
    if 'Mult' in excerpt:                                    # CR10X parameter listing
        _m = re.search(r'^\s*\d+:\s*([\d.]+)\s+Mult', excerpt, re.M)
        _o = re.search(r'^\s*\d+:\s*([\d.]+)\s+Offset', excerpt, re.M)
        tokens = [_m.group(1) if _m else None, _o.group(1) if _o else None]
    else:                                                    # CR1000 VoltSe/VoltDiff call
        _call = re.search(r'Volt(?:Se|Diff)\s*\(([^)]*)\)', excerpt)
        _args = [a.strip() for a in _call.group(1).split(',')] if _call else []
        tokens = _args[-2:] if len(_args) >= 2 else [None, None]
    values = []
    for _tok in tokens:
        if _tok is None:
            raise ValueError("could not parse a multiplier and an offset from the instruction - "
                             "the program language or the layout has changed, or the measurement "
                             "is not an analog voltage at all")
        values.append(float(_tok))
    return {'multiplier': values[0], 'offset': values[1]}


Negative controls
Each helper is fed input it must refuse, before it is trusted.

# Every failure path is exercised before anything is read.
try:
    program_excerpt(PROGRAM_CR1000, r'ThisPatternIsNotInAnyLoggerProgram')
except ValueError as _exc:
    print(f"OK, program_excerpt raised on a pattern that does not occur: {_exc}")
else:
    raise AssertionError("(!) program_excerpt accepted a pattern that does not occur.")

4️⃣ Reading the three series against each other
A response change at one of the three series (tower, NABEL at 49 m, MeteoSwiss Lägern at 2.5 km) moves every pairwise comparison it appears in and no other, as in notebook 02 for TA and RADIATION_SENSOR_CONTINUITY.ipynb for the radiation sensors. NABEL has its own logger and housing, and nothing at this tower can move MeteoSwiss. A comparison says two sensors separated, never which of them left; the pattern of pairs names it.
Yearly levels use full years up to LAST_FULL_YEAR, so the partial 2026 is not compared with full years.

# RH is bounded and its errors are additive, so every comparison is a DIFFERENCE, in percentage
# points of RH (the ratio machinery of notebooks 01 and 03 is for radiation). Controls in the helper:
#   Season: the difference has a seasonal cycle (about +3.9 % RH in February, +0.4 % RH in August),
#     so medians are taken per calendar month and then averaged over months.
#   Sample size: a month with fewer than MIN_RECORDS half-hours is dropped; a pair with no
#     populated month raises.
#   Partial year: only years up to LAST_FULL_YEAR enter, so January-September 2026 is not
#     compared with full years.
MIN_RECORDS = 100
SATURATED = 95.0        # % RH; above this the ceiling starts to clip a step
QUIET_YEARS = (2007, 2015)

PAIRS = [(TOWER_L, NABEL_L), (TOWER_L, MS_L), (NABEL_L, MS_L)]
PAIR_LABELS = [f'{_a} - {_b}' for _a, _b in PAIRS]
TOWER_PAIRS = [_l for _l in PAIR_LABELS if TOWER_L in _l]
REF_PAIR = f'{NABEL_L} - {MS_L}'


def diff_by_year(a: str, b: str, mask: pd.Series = None, min_records: int = MIN_RECORDS
                 ) -> pd.Series:
    """Month-matched yearly mean of `a - b`, in percentage points of RH."""
    _j = rh3.loc[rh3.index.year <= LAST_FULL_YEAR, [a, b]].dropna()
    if mask is not None:
        _j = _j[mask.reindex(_j.index).fillna(False)]
    _d = _j[a] - _j[b]
    _m = _d.groupby([_d.index.year, _d.index.month]).median()
    _n = _d.groupby([_d.index.year, _d.index.month]).count()
    _m = _m[_n >= min_records]
    if _m.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"{a} - {b}: no calendar month reaches {min_records} records, so a yearly "
                         f"level cannot be built from this selection")
    return _m.groupby(level=0).mean()


def levels_and_changes(mask=None):
    """Yearly level of every pair, and the change from one year to the next."""
    _lvl = pd.DataFrame({f'{_a} - {_b}': diff_by_year(_a, _b, mask) for _a, _b in PAIRS})
    _lvl.index.name = 'YEAR'
    return _lvl, _lvl.diff()

def step_at(series: pd.Series, year: int, span: int = 3) -> float:
    """Change of a yearly level across `year`, over `span` years either side.

    The candidate year itself is excluded from both sides: a change inside a year belongs to
    neither era. Returns nan when either side is thin, so a year at the edge of the record cannot
    win by having almost no data behind it.
    """
    _pre = series.reindex(range(year - span, year)).dropna()
    _post = series.reindex(range(year + 1, year + 1 + span)).dropna()
    if len(_pre) < 2 or len(_post) < 2:
        return float('nan')
    return float(_post.mean() - _pre.mean())

def fragment(text, pattern=rf'{PROBE_RX}|{LOC_RX}', width=70) -> str:
    """The part of one entry that names the sensor or its logger, not its first characters.

    Several of these are whole-day visit reports in which the sensor is named once, halfway
    through; truncating from the start shows the drive to the site instead.
    """
    _m = re.search(pattern, str(text), re.I)
    if not _m:
        return str(text)[:2 * width]
    _lo, _hi = max(0, _m.start() - width), min(len(str(text)), _m.end() + width)
    return ('...' if _lo else '') + str(text)[_lo:_hi] + ('...' if _hi < len(str(text)) else '')

🔟 A transfer across 2016: fitted on the era means it does not hold, fitted at the break it does
For a step that is not one number, the homogenisation is a transfer that varies with the humidity: per humidity bin, the difference between the eras, added to the earlier era. This step first fits it against MeteoSwiss Lägern on the era means (2005-2015 against 2017 to CS215_LAST_NORMAL_YEAR, the last full year before the CS215 changed state, step 1️⃣1️⃣) and shows that this estimate is not stable, because both eras drift. It then fits the transfer against NABEL at the break, on the three years before it and the CS215 record up to the end of NABEL’s independent period, shows that this estimate depends little on the window, and scores it against Lägern, which entered no fit. This is the arrangement notebook 02 uses for TA. RH_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED uses the transfer fitted at the break: it removes the step at the break and leaves the drift within each era.
Every fit uses measured records only, binned on the reference humidity; binning on the tower’s reading would produce a slope from regression to the mean.

📋 Table: correction curve per reference humidity bin

HOM_EDGES = np.array([20, 30, 40, 50, 55, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85, 88, 91, 94, 96, 98, 100.0001])
HOM_MID = [(HOM_EDGES[i] + HOM_EDGES[i + 1]) / 2 for i in range(len(HOM_EDGES) - 1)]

# The normal CS215 only: its states of 2024-2025 (step 11) and the HygroVUE10 are left out.
_m = pd.concat([rh_2004_2026[TARGET].rename('tower'), lae.rename('ref')], axis=1).dropna()

PRE_YEARS = list(range(2005, BREAK.year))
POST_YEARS = list(range(BREAK.year + 1, CS215_LAST_NORMAL_YEAR + 1))   # full years only
print(f"measured overlapping records: {len(_m):,}   "
      f"pre {PRE_YEARS[0]}-{PRE_YEARS[-1]}, post {POST_YEARS[0]}-{POST_YEARS[-1]}")


def transfer_curve(frame, pre_years, post_years, min_n=1500):
    """The correction a level-dependent homogenisation would apply, per humidity bin.

    Returns each era's mean tower-minus-reference difference and their difference, which is what
    would have to be ADDED to the earlier era to put it on the later era's level. Bins holding
    fewer than `min_n` records in either era are dropped rather than reported as noise.
    """
    def _binned(sel):
        _b = pd.cut(sel['ref'], bins=HOM_EDGES, labels=HOM_MID, include_lowest=True, right=False)
        _g = (sel['tower'] - sel['ref']).groupby(_b, observed=False)
        return _g.mean(), _g.count()

    _mp, _npre = _binned(frame[frame.index.year.isin(pre_years)])
    _mq, _npost = _binned(frame[frame.index.year.isin(post_years)])
    _t = pd.DataFrame({'pre_diff': _mp, 'post_diff': _mq, 'delta': _mq - _mp,
                       'n_pre': _npre, 'n_post': _npost})
    return _t[(_t.n_pre >= min_n) & (_t.n_post >= min_n)]

# Why the estimates disagree: both eras are moving. The mid-humidity band is where the step is
# largest and where the 100 % ceiling does not compress it.
# The normal CS215 lasts to the last record before EXCESS_START (_m stops there), so its last year
# is partial. Every year of both eras is restricted to the calendar months that year covers in
# full, January to the month before EXCESS_START, so no year's mean is shifted by the seasonal
# cycle of the difference through months that are missing from it.
DRIFT_MONTHS = list(range(1, EXCESS_START.month))
DRIFT_POST_YEARS = list(range(BREAK.year + 1, EXCESS_START.year + 1))   # the CS215 years, 2016 left out
assert _m.index.max() < EXCESS_START and len(DRIFT_MONTHS) >= 6
_band = _m[(_m['ref'] >= 60) & (_m['ref'] < 80) & _m.index.month.isin(DRIFT_MONTHS)]
_res = (_band['tower'] - _band['ref'])
DRIFT = _res.groupby(_res.index.year).agg(['mean', 'count'])
DRIFT = DRIFT[DRIFT['count'] > 1500]
assert EXCESS_START.year in DRIFT.index, "the last year of the normal CS215 is missing from the drift table"

tabcap(f"tower-minus-MeteoSwiss difference per year over the mid-humidity band, where the step is "
       f"largest, on the months {DRIFT_MONTHS[0]}-{DRIFT_MONTHS[-1]} of every year: the normal CS215 "
       f"runs to {EXCESS_START:%d %B %Y}, and its last year covers these months in full. Each era "
       f"travels rather than holding one level")
display(DRIFT.round(2))

_pre = DRIFT.loc[DRIFT.index.isin(PRE_YEARS), 'mean']
_post = DRIFT.loc[DRIFT.index.isin(DRIFT_POST_YEARS), 'mean']
STEP_PP = float(_post.mean() - _pre.mean())
_tr_pre = float(np.polyfit(_pre.index.values.astype(float), _pre.values, 1)[0])
_tr_post = float(np.polyfit(_post.index.values.astype(float), _post.values, 1)[0])
_span_pre, _span_post = _tr_pre * (len(_pre) - 1), _tr_post * (len(_post) - 1)
DRIFT_TOTAL = abs(_span_pre) + abs(_span_post)
DRIFT_PRE_PER_YR, DRIFT_POST_PER_YR = _tr_pre, _tr_post   # reported, not corrected
_ordinary = float(_pre.diff().abs().median())
_jump = float(DRIFT.loc[BREAK.year + 1, 'mean'] - DRIFT.loc[BREAK.year - 1, 'mean'])

print(f"step between era means:        {STEP_PP:+.2f} pp")
print(f"jump {BREAK.year - 1} -> {BREAK.year + 1}:              {_jump:+.2f} pp   "
      f"(median ordinary year-to-year change within the earlier era: {_ordinary:.2f} pp)")
print(f"drift within the earlier era:  {_tr_pre:+.3f} pp/yr = {_span_pre:+.2f} pp end to end")
print(f"drift within the later era:    {_tr_post:+.3f} pp/yr = {_span_post:+.2f} pp end to end")
print(f"total within-era drift:        {DRIFT_TOTAL:.2f} pp, against a step of {abs(STEP_PP):.2f} pp")

# The step is real (asserted first, so this section is not read as a retraction of step 4).
assert _jump > 5 * _ordinary, (
    "the 2016 jump is no longer large against an ordinary year - has a reference changed?")

# But a transfer fitted on the era means cannot remove it, and these two are the reasons; they
# are why the homogenised column uses a transfer fitted at the break (below).
assert DRIFT_TOTAL > abs(STEP_PP), (
    "the within-era drift no longer exceeds the step; an era-mean transfer may now be stable and "
    "the choice of a transfer fitted at the break should be revisited")
assert STAB['difference'].abs().max() > 0.5 * abs(STEP_PP), (
    "the two half-era estimates of the era-mean transfer now agree; revisit the choice of a "
    "transfer fitted at the break")
print("\nAsserted: the step is real, and the drift within the eras is larger than it. The drift is "
      "not corrected by the homogenised column.")

The transfer at the break, fitted against NABEL
NABEL measures at 49 m on the same tower with its own logger and housing, so it sees the same air as the 47 m probe; MeteoSwiss Lägern is 2.5 km away. The transfer is fitted on tower minus NABEL with the binning of transfer_curve(): the MP101A over the three full years before the break (LOCAL_PRE_YEARS), the CS215 from the first full month after it (LOCAL_POST_START) to the end of NABEL’s independent period (LOCAL_POST_END, step 3️⃣). Close to the break the drift has had little time to act. Each bin’s correction is attached to the MP101A’s own reading in that bin (tower_reading), interpolated between bins and held constant beyond the outer bins, so it can be applied to an MP101A value. Near saturation, where both probes sit at the ceiling, the fitted step is close to zero; the top bin keeps its own small correction, and the result is capped to [0, 100], so a saturated MP101A record stays at 100 %.
Three checks follow: the transfer must come out the same from shorter windows; applied to the MP101A era, it must remove the step against Lägern, which entered no fit (fit against one reference, score against another); and the same transfer fitted against Lägern is printed beside it, because the difference between the two is the reference dependence of this correction.


📋 Table: the 2016 transfer per NABEL humidity bin

# The 2016 transfer, fitted at the break against NABEL (same tower, 49 m, independent until
# NABEL_UNTIL, step 3) and scored against MeteoSwiss Lägern below, as notebook 02 does for TA.
LOCAL_PRE_YEARS = [BREAK.year - 3, BREAK.year - 2, BREAK.year - 1]   # MP101A, 2013-2015
LOCAL_POST_START = pd.Timestamp(f'{BREAK.year}-02-01')   # first full month of the CS215 record
LOCAL_POST_END = NABEL_UNTIL                              # exclusive: NABEL stops being independent
LOCAL_MIN_N = 300   # records per bin and window; lets the shorter windows below fill most bins
assert BREAK < LOCAL_POST_START < LOCAL_POST_END and max(LOCAL_PRE_YEARS) < BREAK.year

# Measured records only: nothing is reconstructed yet.
_nm = pd.concat([rh_2004_2026[TARGET].rename('tower'), NABEL_REF.rename('ref')], axis=1).dropna()
_lm = pd.concat([rh_2004_2026[TARGET].rename('tower'), lae.rename('ref')], axis=1).dropna()


def pre_window(frame, years=None):
    """The MP101A window: full calendar years before the break."""
    return frame[frame.index.year.isin(LOCAL_PRE_YEARS if years is None else years)]


def post_window(frame, start=None, end=None):
    """The CS215 window: from `start` to before `end`."""
    start = LOCAL_POST_START if start is None else start
    end = LOCAL_POST_END if end is None else end
    return frame[(frame.index >= start) & (frame.index < end)]


def binned_transfer(pre: pd.DataFrame, post: pd.DataFrame, min_n: int = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The binning of transfer_curve() on two explicit windows of a (tower, ref) frame.

    Per reference-humidity bin: each window's mean tower - reference difference, their difference
    `delta` (what is added to the earlier era), the record counts, and `tower_reading`, the
    earlier era's own reading in that bin. Bins holding fewer than `min_n` records in either window
    are dropped; raises if none is left.
    """
    min_n = LOCAL_MIN_N if min_n is None else min_n

    def _binned(sel):
        _b = pd.cut(sel['ref'], bins=HOM_EDGES, labels=HOM_MID, include_lowest=True, right=False)
        _g = (sel['tower'] - sel['ref']).groupby(_b, observed=False)
        return _g.mean(), _g.count()

    (_a, _na), (_p, _np) = _binned(pre), _binned(post)
    _t = pd.DataFrame({'pre_diff': _a, 'post_diff': _p, 'delta': _p - _a, 'n_pre': _na, 'n_post': _np})
    _t = _t[(_t.n_pre >= min_n) & (_t.n_post >= min_n)]
    if _t.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"no humidity bin holds {min_n} records in both windows")
    _t['tower_reading'] = _t.index.to_series().astype(float) + _t['pre_diff']
    return _t


try:
    binned_transfer(_nm.iloc[:48], _nm.iloc[-48:])
except ValueError as _exc:
    print(f"OK, binned_transfer raised on a single day per window: {_exc}")
else:
    raise AssertionError("(!) binned_transfer accepted windows of a single day.")

LOCAL_CURVE = binned_transfer(pre_window(_nm), post_window(_nm))

# The ordinary year-to-year change of the same binned difference within each era: consecutive
# calendar years before the break, consecutive year-long blocks after it. It is the noise level of
# a binned correction, used for the near-zero bins here and for the window tolerance below.
_blocks_pre = [pre_window(_nm, [_y]) for _y in LOCAL_PRE_YEARS]
_blocks_post = [post_window(_nm, LOCAL_POST_START + pd.DateOffset(years=_k),
                            LOCAL_POST_START + pd.DateOffset(years=_k + 1)) for _k in range(2)]
_yy = pd.concat([binned_transfer(_x, _y, min_n=1)['delta'] for _x, _y in
                 [(_blocks_pre[0], _blocks_pre[1]), (_blocks_pre[1], _blocks_pre[2]),
                  (_blocks_post[0], _blocks_post[1])]], axis=1, ignore_index=True)
YEAR_TO_YEAR = float(_yy[_yy.index.astype(float) >= 40].abs().stack().median())

# Where both probes sit at the ceiling the step is zero, and the fitted delta may come out a few
# hundredths below it. Such a bin is applied as zero, so the transfer never lowers a reading; a
# negative delta larger than the year-to-year noise would be a real step and fails here.
LOCAL_CURVE['correction'] = LOCAL_CURVE['delta'].clip(lower=0.0)
_neg = LOCAL_CURVE['delta'] < 0
assert (LOCAL_CURVE.loc[_neg, 'delta'].abs() < YEAR_TO_YEAR).all(), (
    "a bin of the 2016 transfer is negative by more than the year-to-year noise: the MP101A would "
    "read wetter than the CS215 there, which this section does not describe")
tabcap(f"the 2016 transfer per NABEL humidity bin: each window's mean difference from NABEL "
       f"(MP101A {LOCAL_PRE_YEARS[0]}-{LOCAL_PRE_YEARS[-1]}, CS215 {LOCAL_POST_START:%b %Y} to "
       f"{(LOCAL_POST_END - pd.Timedelta('1D')):%b %Y}), the fitted delta, the correction applied "
       f"(delta, with {int(_neg.sum())} near-zero negative bin(s) set to zero) and the MP101A reading "
       f"it attaches to")
display(LOCAL_CURVE.round(2))


def mp101a_to_cs215(rh_mp, curve=None):
    """CS215 equivalent of an MP101A reading, from the 2016 transfer of step 10.

    The correction is interpolated on the MP101A reading between the bins and held constant beyond
    the outer bins (np.interp). The result is capped to [0, 100]; NaN stays NaN.
    """
    curve = LOCAL_CURVE if curve is None else curve
    _v = np.asarray(rh_mp, dtype=float)
    _c = curve['correction'] if 'correction' in curve else curve['delta']
    _out = np.clip(_v + np.interp(_v, curve['tower_reading'].values, _c.values), 0.0, 100.0)
    _out = np.where(np.isnan(_v), np.nan, _out)
    if isinstance(rh_mp, pd.Series):
        return pd.Series(_out, index=rh_mp.index, name=rh_mp.name)
    return _out


# What the transfer does, asserted. It is applied on the MP101A reading, so that axis must be
# ordered; it raises every reading in the drier half of the range (below 85 %, the boundary of
# step 5's dry bins), lowers none, keeps the order of the readings, leaves 100 % at 100 % and
# never fills a gap.
_fine = np.linspace(0.0, 100.0, 2001)
_mapped = mp101a_to_cs215(_fine)
assert LOCAL_CURVE['tower_reading'].is_monotonic_increasing, (

assert (_mapped >= _fine).all() and _mapped.max() <= 100.0, "the transfer lowers a reading or leaves [0, 100]"
assert mp101a_to_cs215(np.array([100.0]))[0] == 100.0, "a saturated MP101A record no longer stays at 100 %"
assert np.isnan(mp101a_to_cs215(np.array([np.nan]))[0]), "the transfer filled a gap"

      f"top bin {LOCAL_CURVE['correction'].iloc[-1]:+.2f} % RH; median one-year change of the binned "
      f"difference {YEAR_TO_YEAR:.2f} % RH")

# Score against MeteoSwiss Lägern, which entered neither the transfer nor its windows: the
# tower-minus-Lägern step across the break, binned on the Lägern humidity, over the windows of the
# fit, before and after the MP101A era is raised. Measured records only.
def step_across(pre: pd.DataFrame, post: pd.DataFrame):
    """Per reference bin the post-minus-pre mean of tower - reference, and its mean over the bins."""
    _s = binned_transfer(pre, post)['delta']
    return _s, float(_s.mean())


_lae_pre, _lae_post = pre_window(_lm), post_window(_lm)

_lae_after, LAE_STEP_AFTER = step_across(_lae_pre_hom, _lae_post)

# Tolerance, two parts. (1) Lägern's own year-to-year scatter of this statistic: the same step
# between consecutive year-long blocks within one era, on the homogenised values. (2) The drift
# the windows contain: against Lägern each era drifts (step 10), and the window centres lie
# away from the break, so a step measured between them holds the drift over those distances.
_hom = lambda d: d.assign(tower=mp101a_to_cs215(d['tower']))

What step 🔟 settles
Fitted on the era means, the transfer is not stable. Estimates from the first and second halves of each era differ by up to the size of the correction, and summer and winter by about as much again. The drift figure shows why: each era travels further over its own length than the step between them, the two in opposite directions, so a transfer fitted on the era means is correct for no particular year.
Fitted at the break against NABEL, it is. Shorter windows change it by less than the year-to-year noise of each bin plus a year of drift, and applied to the MP101A era it removes most of the step against Lägern, which entered no fit, to within Lägern’s own year-to-year change plus the drift the windows contain. RH_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED raises the MP101A era by this transfer. The shorter windows give a smaller correction in every bin from 40 to 85 % (asserted), so part of what the fitted windows attribute to the probes may be drift.
The correction depends on the reference. Fitted against Lägern over the same windows, it raises the MP101A records by several tenths of a percentage point more on average and by up to about 2.4 percentage points more just below saturation, where NABEL finds almost no step and Lägern a large one (table above). That difference is the uncertainty of the homogenised column across 2016, and it is largest in humid conditions.
The drift is not corrected. It is unattributed, and after mid-2018 no third series exists to attribute it (NABEL stops, then repeats the tower). Fitting the tower onto MeteoSwiss would replace the measurement with the reference, which 01 and 03 decline for an unattributed drift. The homogenised column is therefore free of the step at the break and not homogeneous over decades: against Lägern the MP101A era drifts by DRIFT_PRE_PER_YR and the CS215 era by DRIFT_POST_PER_YR (printed above, in percentage points a year, from January to September of each year so that the partial year 2024 compares with the others), in opposite directions, and a trend computed from either column carries that drift.



1️⃣1️⃣ The CS215 change of May 2025
Notebook 02 (its step 1️⃣1️⃣) finds two states of the CS215 that depart from its normal behaviour. From EXCESS_START (22 October 2024) the probe heats abnormally in sunlight (source code 7). On 16 May 2025 it was handled between 09:32 and 09:42, and from RESET_START the daytime excess is gone (code 6). The dates are those of 02, declared again in the settings; the source flags of the two products are compared in Sensor era of every record.
The CS215 reports RH relative to its own temperature, so a probe that is too warm in sun reads a lower RH for the same amount of water vapour. Whether the May 2025 change in RH is of that kind or a change of the humidity element is decided here in vapour pressure e, computed from each sensor’s own RH and TA: a temperature error moves RH and leaves e in place. Tower TA is 02’s measured TA_T1_47_1_gfXG (measured records only); Lägern e follows from RH_LAE_MS and TA_LAE_MS. Saturation vapour pressure over water is the Magnus form that diive’s calc_vpd_from_ta_rh uses, so notebook 07’s VPD rests on the same formula.
The comparison is season-matched: the 30 days before the handling and the 30 days after it in 2025, against the same calendar dates of the normal CS215 summers HV_CS215_YEARS.

def es_hpa(ta):
    """Saturation vapour pressure over water (hPa) at air temperature `ta` (degC).

    Magnus form with the coefficients of diive's calc_vpd_from_ta_rh (6.1078 hPa, 17.08085,
    234.175 degC), the formula notebook 07 computes VPD with.
    """
    _t = np.asarray(ta, dtype=float)
    _out = 6.1078 * np.exp(17.08085 * _t / (234.175 + _t))
    return pd.Series(_out, index=ta.index) if isinstance(ta, pd.Series) else _out
