text:
🔍 Outlier detection
Run a test → inspect its preview → commit with mscr.addflag(). Only the committed flag of the most recent test is added. Skip any test a variable does not need.
What is committed here: the December 2025 logger-artefact minutes (manual removal), the April 2024 SDI-12 decode garbage (absolute limits), and the missing-values flag. Why the rest are off:

Never split day and night. Soil temperature does have a diurnal cycle, but at this depth it is damped and lagged relative to the surface, so a solar-geometry split does not line up with it — it would only halve the sample behind every threshold. Every test below runs with separate_daytime_nighttime=False.
Distribution-wide tests measure the season, not a fault. A z-score over the whole record asks how far a value sits from the multi-year mean; January at 2 °C and July at 19 °C are both correct.
Differencing-based tests are degenerate on this record. The 10MIN era (to March 2021) is back-filled onto the 1MIN grid by diive, so nine of every ten increments are zero by construction; the 1MIN era is quantised to exactly 0.05 °C and the soil moves a few tenths of a kelvin a day, so ~97 % of minute-to-minute increments are genuinely zero. The rolling MAD a Hampel filter scales its band by is then zero, and raising n_sigma cannot help.


mscr.start_outlier_detection()

  > Starting step-wise outlier detection for variable TS_FF1_0.5_1 ...



Plot the current cleaned data at any point during detection:

for key, val in mscr.outlier_detection.items():
    val.showplot_cleaned(interactive=False)









Manual removal
Flag specific timestamps or time ranges for removal - known sensor failures, maintenance windows, logger artefacts. Give [start, stop] pairs and/or single timestamps.
Why this variable needs one. On 18-19 December 2025 two remote logger-program uploads corrupted the SDI-12 scale: in seven individual minutes all eleven SDI-12 channels of the profile depart from their own local median at once, by exactly the same factor — 0.00 × on four minutes and 0.50 × on three — while the two analogue Campbell 109 thermistors on a different port read a steady 4.8-5.7 °C throughout. Eleven probes between 5 and 60 cm cannot go to zero, or halve, in the same minute for any physical reason. No automatic test reaches them: 0.00 °C and 3.10 °C are both plausible December soil temperatures at 0.5 m, so absolute limits cannot see them, and the differencing tests are degenerate here.

The windows are written as [T − 1 min, T], and that is deliberate — see Timestamp convention. ManualRemoval matches against TIMESTAMP_MID, so the closed interval ['2025-12-19 10:38:00', '2025-12-19 10:39:00'] selects exactly the one record whose TIMESTAMP_END is 10:39:00, and a bare timestamp would select nothing. Asserted below.


⚠️ These windows are a bus event, not a property of this probe. They are shared with every SDI-12 channel — which is why they appear identically in the _1 notebook. Verify them on the preview plot rather than trusting the copy: REMOVE_DATES belongs to a sensor.

    ['2025-12-19 09:48:00', '2025-12-19 09:49:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 09:50:00', '2025-12-19 09:51:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 09:56:00', '2025-12-19 09:57:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
    ['2025-12-19 10:30:00', '2025-12-19 10:31:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
    ['2025-12-19 10:35:00', '2025-12-19 10:36:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 10:38:00', '2025-12-19 10:39:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
]

# A window that brackets no middle stamp removes nothing at all, silently - so check the shape.
for _w in REMOVE_DATES:

    assert _e - _s == pd.Timedelta('1min'), (
        f'(!) window {_w} is not the one-minute bracket the TIMESTAMP_MID convention needs')

    mscr.flag_manualremoval_test(remove_dates=REMOVE_DATES, showplot=True, verbose=True)

🔧 Corrections
Applied to the high-res, QCF-filtered data. None of them apply to soil temperature, and every call below stays commented out. The corrections diive offers are offset removals for radiation and relative humidity, threshold clipping, and setting ranges to a constant - every one of them writes a value the sensor did not measure.

⚠️ Do not set the exact value 0 to missing. correction_set_exact_value_to_missing(values=[0]) looks like the obvious way to catch the failed SDI-12 reads, and it is wrong twice over: it would delete every genuine 0.00 °C reading this soil ever produces, and it would miss the half-scale minutes entirely, because those are not a fixed value at all. That is why those minutes are handled by named manual removal instead.


mscr.showplot_cleaned()








Inspect the most frequent values first (read-only, safe to run). At 0.5 m this list is expected to be short and top-heavy, and that is not a fault. The 1MIN era is quantised to 0.05 °C while the daily signal is about 0.10 K — two steps — so this channel spends hours, and in winter sometimes days, reporting a single value. Over the whole record it can only produce about 280 distinct values (a 4-17 °C span at a 0.05 °C step), and the 10MIN era is additionally back-filled across ten 1MIN slots.

⚠️ Do not read a dominant value as a stuck sensor here, and never enable a flat-run or stuck-value test at this depth — it would fire on the entire winter. The shallow notebooks say the opposite because at 0.05 m a dominant value would be suspicious; that guidance does not survive the trip down the profile. What would be a genuine fault at this depth is a value appearing outside the seasonal band it belongs to.

⬆️ Upload data to database
Re-uploading overwrites the same variant - safe to re-run. With delete_from_db_before_upload=True (below), the upload first deletes, then writes. The delete is scoped to the exact match _measurement + varname + data_version (meteoscreening_diive) over the uploaded time range, so re-screening a period replaces only its previous screened result. It never touches the raw data (different data_version, and a different _raw bucket), other variables, or other data versions. The delete-first step (rather than a plain overwrite) matters because InfluxDB keys a point by its full tag set: if a tag changed between runs (e.g. units, gain, offset), a plain write would leave the old point as a duplicate - the delete removes it regardless of tags.

📝 Notes for this variable

Mean, not sum. RESAMPLING_AGG = 'mean' - soil temperature is a state, not a flux.
Units are °C, filegroup 12_meteo_forestfloor.
Sensor identity. The temperature channel of a METER TEROS 21 water-potential sensor installed 19 Mar 2020 at 0.5 m, first logged 2020-04-10 15:00. Not an MPS-2 (that family is 0.05/0.1/0.6 m only) and not a TEROS 12 (that is TS_FF1_0.5_2).
Coverage 2 505 423 records, 99.06 % over 2020-2025 — the five shared power and logger outages only. No fault of its own.
Raw range 0.00 … 17.15 °C, and the upper end is real soil, not decode garbage. Only 0.00 is an artefact — the failed-read sentinel, which sits inside the physical limits and is caught by the manual removal rather than by the limits test. Its same-depth partner reaches 277 °C, so the two channels’ limits reports will not resemble each other.
The diurnal diagnostics are dead at this depth, and reporting them anyway would be misleading. Median daily amplitude is 0.10 K — exactly two steps of the 0.05 °C quantiser. A rolling correlation of daily increments against anything measures rounding, not soil: on the channels at this depth it runs at a median of 0.41-0.58 with several hundred days below 0.5, spread evenly across every season rather than clustered on any fault. A future reader who takes that at face value would delete several hundred good days. Do not compute it here, and do not carry the 0.05 m version of the diagnostic down.
What still works is the seasonal signal. The annual wave at 0.5 m has an amplitude of several kelvin — two orders of magnitude above the quantiser — and lags the surface by weeks. Its amplitude and phase are the diagnostics that discriminate at this depth, and they belong in 30_PRODUCTS/ on the 30MIN data. The diurnal maximum, for the record, arrives around 4 a.m. here: a solar-geometry day/night split would be actively wrong, which is why screening never uses one.
Long runs of identical values are correct behaviour, not a stuck sensor. With a daily signal of two quantiser steps, this channel spends hours — sometimes days in winter — reporting one value. Over the whole record it can only ever produce about 280 distinct values (a 4-17 °C span at a 0.05 °C step). Never enable a flat-run or stuck-value test at this depth; it would fire on the entire winter.
Two raw time resolutions, 10MIN until the March 2021 logger rebuild and 1MIN after; diive upsamples the coarser era onto the finest grid before screening.
A failed sensor read is a number, not a gap — a failed SDI-12 read arrives as the true value times a wrong scale factor (0 × or 0.5 ×), so notna() does not mean “measured”.
Deferred to 30_PRODUCTS/, on the 30MIN data: the comparison against the rest of the FF1 profile and against air temperature, the placement and offset questions, and any gap handling. This notebook exports gaps where the station was down and does not fill them.



♻️ Sibling notebooks
Its same-depth partner is TS_FF1_0.5_2, the TEROS 12 — a different make of sensor in the same soil at the same nominal depth. That comparison belongs in 30_PRODUCTS/ on the 30MIN data, and at this depth it must be made on the seasonal signal: the diurnal diagnostics are quantisation noise here.
Structurally this is a near-copy of TS_FF1_0.3_1_2020-2025.ipynb — same make, same bus, same windows, limits as a backstop. What is new at 0.5 m is that the daily signal has shrunk to two quantiser steps, which kills the diurnal diagnostics outright rather than merely blunting them.
The standing rule for all of them: REMOVE_DATES belongs to a sensor, not to a variable. These notebooks are copies of each other with a few settings changed, and carrying a window across a copy deletes good data under a justification written about a different probe.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.3_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
ℹ️ About this notebook
Download raw soil temperature from the InfluxDB database, remove the worst outliers on the high-resolution data, resample to 30MIN, and upload the result back to the database. Screening uses StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb from diive (diive/preprocessing/qaqc/meteoscreening.py); download and upload use diive’s in-house InfluxDB engine (InfluxIO, in diive/core/io/db/influx).
Flow: download (InfluxIO) → screen on high-res data (diive) → resample to 30MIN → upload.
Scope is deliberately narrow. The raw record is millions of rows, so anything done here is expensive. This notebook only takes out what is unambiguously wrong at high resolution — the April 2024 SDI-12 decode garbage (absolute limits) and the seven December 2025 logger-artefact minutes (manual removal) — and hands over a clean 30MIN series. Everything else (sensor comparisons, level/offset questions, gap handling, homogenisation across sensor generations) is settled later in 30_PRODUCTS/, on the half-hourly data, where it costs a fraction as much.
Outlier detection is stepwise: run a test, inspect its preview plot, then commit it with mscr.addflag(). Re-run with different parameters as often as you like before committing. Run only the tests a variable actually needs. At the end all committed flags are aggregated into one overall quality flag QCF.

Which sensor this is. In this profile the replicate suffix names the sensor family, not the depth: _1 = the water-potential sensors of the 19 Mar 2020 install (MPS-2 at 0.05/0.1/0.6 m, TEROS 21 at 0.2/0.3/0.5 m), _2 = the TEROS 12 probes that also report SWC_FF1_<depth>_1, _3/_4 = Campbell 109 thermistors added at the March 2021 logger rebuild. This one is a METER TEROS 21 water-potential sensor, temperature channel.


Database access needs the influxdb-client package, which this project pulls in via the diive[db] extra (declared in pyproject.toml). diive also ships a db dependency group, but dependency groups are local to the project that declares them — uv sync --group db only works inside the diive repo, not from here.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.3_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
⏱️ Timestamp convention (important)
The database stores every timestamp in UTC and as TIMESTAMP_END (the stamp marks the end of the averaging interval). Getting this right is the one thing that must not go wrong: the value written back to the database depends on it, and so does every window in REMOVE_DATES.
The single knob is TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS (set in User settings). It is applied identically on download and on upload:









Stage
Timezone
Convention
Done by




Database
UTC
TIMESTAMP_END
InfluxDB


After dbc.download(..., timezone_offset_to_utc_hours=N)
local (UTC+N)
TIMESTAMP_END
InfluxIO


During screening
local
TIMESTAMP_MIDDLE (converted internally)
StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb


After mscr.resample()
local
back to TIMESTAMP_END
diive


After dbc.upload_singlevar(..., timezone_offset_to_utc_hours=N)

TIMESTAMP_END
InfluxIO



One place where this bites. REMOVE_DATES is matched against TIMESTAMP_MID, not TIMESTAMP_END: StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb hands the series to ManualRemoval after the internal conversion, so the record whose TIMESTAMP_END is 10:39:00 carries the label 10:38:30 inside the test. A bare '2025-12-19 10:39:00' would therefore match nothing and the removal would silently do nothing. It only matters when removing individual records: a window spanning days has edges far larger than the half-record offset.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.3_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
✏️ User settings (please adjust)
Adjust these before running. What each setting means:
Site - SITE, SITE_LAT, SITE_LON: site ID and coordinates. The coordinates set the day/night split used during screening — not used here, see Outlier detection.
Variable to screen - PROFILE, DEPTH, REPL: the sensor’s position tags. FIELD is assembled from them and is the InfluxDB _field. REPL changes the sensor family, not just the probe. - MEASUREMENT: exactly one measurement grouping the variables — TS for soil temperature.
Time range to screen - START: first timestamp to screen — is included. - STOP: upper bound — is not included.
Data settings - TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS: the critical timestamp knob — see Timestamp convention. Must match how the raw data was logged (1 for CET winter time) and must be the same value everywhere. - DATA_VERSION: the source data version in the database (raw). - DIRCONF: local folder holding the database connection config.
Resampling - RESAMPLING_FREQ / RESAMPLING_AGG: soil temperature is a state, so 'mean' — never 'sum'.
Physical range - TS_MIN, TS_MAX: the absolute-limits test, justified from this sensor’s own measured extremes.
Parameter help - SHOW_PARAM_HELP: True prints the full docstring of each screening method right before it runs.

# --- Site ---
SITE = 'ch-lae'
SITE_LAT = 47.478333  # CH-LAE
SITE_LON = 8.364389  # CH-LAE

# --- Variable to screen ---
# (!) REPL, not DEPTH, is what names the sensor family in this profile:
#       _1  the water-potential sensors of the 19 Mar 2020 install - MPS-2 at 0.05/0.1/0.6 m,
#           TEROS 21 at 0.2/0.3/0.5 m. Six channels.
#       _2  METER TEROS 12, the same probes that report SWC_FF1_<depth>_1. Five channels.
#       _3/_4  Campbell 109 thermistors at 0.05 m, added at the March 2021 logger rebuild.
# This notebook screens: METER TEROS 21 water-potential sensor, temperature channel.
PROFILE = 'FF1'  # horizontal position (soil profile)
DEPTH = '0.3'
REPL = '1'  # <-- the sensor family, see above
FIELD = f'TS_{PROFILE}_{DEPTH}_{REPL}'
FIELDS = [FIELD]  # StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb expects a list
MEASUREMENT = 'TS'

# --- Time range to screen ---
# Raw resolution is 10MIN until the March 2021 logger rebuild and 1MIN after, so this
# range is ~2.5 million records. The record starts 2020-04-10 15:00; asking for
# 2020-01-01 simply starts at the first record.
START = '2020-01-01 00:00:01'  # included
STOP = '2026-01-01 00:00:01'  # not included

# --- Data settings ---
DATA_VERSION = 'raw'
TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS = 1  # UTC+01:00 (CET, winter time). Must match how the raw data was logged.
DIRCONF = r'<LOCAL>\poet\configs'
# DIRCONF = r'P:\Flux\RDS_calculations\_scripts\_configs\configs'

# --- Resampling ---
RESAMPLING_FREQ = '30min'  # screened high-res data is resampled to this frequency
RESAMPLING_AGG = 'mean'  # (!) soil temperature is a state variable, never summed

# --- Physical range of soil temperature at this site, in degC ---
# (!) On THIS channel the limits test is a backstop that will almost certainly flag nothing,
# and that is worth knowing before you read its report as a failure.
# Measured over 2020-2025 the raw record spans 0.00 to 18.40 degC. Unlike every channel above
# it, the upper end is NOT decode garbage - 18.40 degC is a real August soil temperature. This
# probe kept measuring cleanly through the April 2024 bus failure that filled its neighbours
# with 40-300 degC nonsense, which is one of the four measurements that establish which sensor
# family is which. The lower end, 0.00, is the failed-SDI-12-read sentinel and sits INSIDE the
# limits, so this test cannot catch it either - the manual removal below is what does.
# At 0.3 m the seasonal swing is narrower still (median daily amplitude 0.20 K), roughly
# 3-18 degC, so the limits below cannot fire on a measurement.
TS_MIN, TS_MAX = -5, 30

# --- Parameter help ---
SHOW_PARAM_HELP = False

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.3_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
🔍 Outlier detection
Run a test → inspect its preview → commit with mscr.addflag(). Only the committed flag of the most recent test is added. Skip any test a variable does not need.
What is committed here: the December 2025 logger-artefact minutes (manual removal), the April 2024 SDI-12 decode garbage (absolute limits), and the missing-values flag. Why the rest are off:

Never split day and night. Soil temperature does have a diurnal cycle, but at this depth it is damped and lagged relative to the surface, so a solar-geometry split does not line up with it — it would only halve the sample behind every threshold. Every test below runs with separate_daytime_nighttime=False.
Distribution-wide tests measure the season, not a fault. A z-score over the whole record asks how far a value sits from the multi-year mean; January at 2 °C and July at 19 °C are both correct.
Differencing-based tests are degenerate on this record. The 10MIN era (to March 2021) is back-filled onto the 1MIN grid by diive, so nine of every ten increments are zero by construction; the 1MIN era is quantised to exactly 0.05 °C and the soil moves a few tenths of a kelvin a day, so ~97 % of minute-to-minute increments are genuinely zero. The rolling MAD a Hampel filter scales its band by is then zero, and raising n_sigma cannot help.


mscr.start_outlier_detection()

  > Starting step-wise outlier detection for variable TS_FF1_0.3_1 ...



Plot the current cleaned data at any point during detection:

for key, val in mscr.outlier_detection.items():
    val.showplot_cleaned(interactive=False)









Manual removal
Flag specific timestamps or time ranges for removal - known sensor failures, maintenance windows, logger artefacts. Give [start, stop] pairs and/or single timestamps.
Why this variable needs one. On 18-19 December 2025 two remote logger-program uploads corrupted the SDI-12 scale: in seven individual minutes all eleven SDI-12 channels of the profile depart from their own local median at once, by exactly the same factor — 0.00 × on four minutes and 0.50 × on three — while the two analogue Campbell 109 thermistors on a different port read a steady 4.8-5.7 °C throughout. Eleven probes between 5 and 60 cm cannot go to zero, or halve, in the same minute for any physical reason. No automatic test reaches them: 0.00 °C and 3.10 °C are both plausible December soil temperatures at 0.3 m, so absolute limits cannot see them, and the differencing tests are degenerate here.

The windows are written as [T − 1 min, T], and that is deliberate — see Timestamp convention. ManualRemoval matches against TIMESTAMP_MID, so the closed interval ['2025-12-19 10:38:00', '2025-12-19 10:39:00'] selects exactly the one record whose TIMESTAMP_END is 10:39:00, and a bare timestamp would select nothing. Asserted below.


⚠️ These windows are a bus event, not a property of this probe. They are shared with every SDI-12 channel — which is why they appear identically in the _1 notebook. Verify them on the preview plot rather than trusting the copy: REMOVE_DATES belongs to a sensor.

    ['2025-12-19 09:50:00', '2025-12-19 09:51:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 09:56:00', '2025-12-19 09:57:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
    ['2025-12-19 10:30:00', '2025-12-19 10:31:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
    ['2025-12-19 10:35:00', '2025-12-19 10:36:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 10:38:00', '2025-12-19 10:39:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
]

# A window that brackets no middle stamp removes nothing at all, silently - so check the shape.

This is the workhorse test for this channel: the only artefact that is not the December 2025 logger trouble is the April 2024 SDI-12 decode garbage, and every one of those records lands far outside anything the soil can do — this channel’s raw maximum is 80.00 °C.

⬆️ Upload data to database
Re-uploading overwrites the same variant - safe to re-run. With delete_from_db_before_upload=True (below), the upload first deletes, then writes. The delete is scoped to the exact match _measurement + varname + data_version (meteoscreening_diive) over the uploaded time range, so re-screening a period replaces only its previous screened result. It never touches the raw data (different data_version, and a different _raw bucket), other variables, or other data versions. The delete-first step (rather than a plain overwrite) matters because InfluxDB keys a point by its full tag set: if a tag changed between runs (e.g. units, gain, offset), a plain write would leave the old point as a duplicate - the delete removes it regardless of tags.

📝 Notes for this variable

Mean, not sum. RESAMPLING_AGG = 'mean' - soil temperature is a state, not a flux.
Units are °C, filegroup 12_meteo_forestfloor.
Sensor identity. The temperature channel of a METER TEROS 21 water-potential sensor installed 19 Mar 2020 at 0.3 m, first logged 2020-04-10 15:00. Not an MPS-2 (that family is 0.05/0.1/0.6 m only) and not a TEROS 12 (that is TS_FF1_0.3_2).
This channel is one of the four measurements that establish the _1/_2 mapping, and the decisive one. The 0.3 m TEROS 12 failed in April 2024 and was not replaced until March 2025, leaving TS_FF1_0.3_2 with a 326-day hole — while this channel carries only the 12-day April 2024 bus outage and keeps measuring right through. The probe with the hole is the TEROS 12. That is why the suffix mapping is not a guess.
Coverage 2 505 757 records, 99.07 % over 2020-2025 — the five shared power and logger outages only.
Raw range 0.00 … 18.40 °C, and unlike the channels above it the upper end is real soil, not decode garbage: this probe measured cleanly through the April 2024 bus failure that filled its neighbours with 40-300 °C nonsense. Only the lower end, 0.00, is an artefact — the failed-read sentinel, which sits inside the physical limits and is caught by the manual removal rather than by the limits test.
Median daily amplitude 0.20 K (2023). At this depth the amplitude diagnostic stops discriminating: against a 0.05 °C storage step, 0.20 K is four steps, and below 0.3 m the resolution rather than the soil sets the number. Do not use amplitude to separate 0.3, 0.5 and 0.6 m.
Two raw time resolutions, 10MIN until the March 2021 logger rebuild and 1MIN after; diive upsamples the coarser era onto the finest grid before screening.
Values are quantised to 0.05 °C in the 1MIN era — at this depth that quantisation is a substantial fraction of the whole daily signal.
A failed sensor read is a number, not a gap — a failed SDI-12 read arrives as the true value times a wrong scale factor (0 × or 0.5 ×), so notna() does not mean “measured”.
Deferred to 30_PRODUCTS/, on the 30MIN data: the comparison against the rest of the FF1 profile and against air temperature, the placement and offset questions, and any gap handling. This notebook exports gaps where the station was down and does not fill them.



♻️ Sibling notebooks
Its same-depth partner is TS_FF1_0.3_2, the TEROS 12 — but that channel is two probes under one name with a 326-day hole between them, so it is not a drop-in reference. This channel is the one that measured continuously across that hole, which makes it the reference for adjudicating its partner, not the other way round.
Structurally this is a near-copy of TS_FF1_0.2_1_2020-2025.ipynb — same make (TEROS 21), same bus, same windows. What changes at this depth is that the limits test has nothing to catch and the amplitude diagnostic stops discriminating; both are stated in the notes.
The standing rule for all of them: REMOVE_DATES belongs to a sensor, not to a variable. These notebooks are copies of each other with a few settings changed, and carrying a window across a copy deletes good data under a justification written about a different probe.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.2_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
ℹ️ About this notebook
Download raw soil temperature from the InfluxDB database, remove the worst outliers on the high-resolution data, resample to 30MIN, and upload the result back to the database. Screening uses StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb from diive (diive/preprocessing/qaqc/meteoscreening.py); download and upload use diive’s in-house InfluxDB engine (InfluxIO, in diive/core/io/db/influx).
Flow: download (InfluxIO) → screen on high-res data (diive) → resample to 30MIN → upload.
Scope is deliberately narrow. The raw record is millions of rows, so anything done here is expensive. This notebook only takes out what is unambiguously wrong at high resolution — the April 2024 SDI-12 decode garbage (absolute limits) and the seven December 2025 logger-artefact minutes (manual removal) — and hands over a clean 30MIN series. Everything else (sensor comparisons, level/offset questions, gap handling, homogenisation across sensor generations) is settled later in 30_PRODUCTS/, on the half-hourly data, where it costs a fraction as much.
Outlier detection is stepwise: run a test, inspect its preview plot, then commit it with mscr.addflag(). Re-run with different parameters as often as you like before committing. Run only the tests a variable actually needs. At the end all committed flags are aggregated into one overall quality flag QCF.

Which sensor this is. In this profile the replicate suffix names the sensor family, not the depth: _1 = the water-potential sensors of the 19 Mar 2020 install (MPS-2 at 0.05/0.1/0.6 m, TEROS 21 at 0.2/0.3/0.5 m), _2 = the TEROS 12 probes that also report SWC_FF1_<depth>_1, _3/_4 = Campbell 109 thermistors added at the March 2021 logger rebuild. This one is a METER TEROS 21 water-potential sensor, temperature channel.


Database access needs the influxdb-client package, which this project pulls in via the diive[db] extra (declared in pyproject.toml). diive also ships a db dependency group, but dependency groups are local to the project that declares them — uv sync --group db only works inside the diive repo, not from here.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.2_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
⏱️ Timestamp convention (important)
The database stores every timestamp in UTC and as TIMESTAMP_END (the stamp marks the end of the averaging interval). Getting this right is the one thing that must not go wrong: the value written back to the database depends on it, and so does every window in REMOVE_DATES.
The single knob is TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS (set in User settings). It is applied identically on download and on upload:









Stage
Timezone

local

One place where this bites. REMOVE_DATES is matched against TIMESTAMP_MID, not TIMESTAMP_END: StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb hands the series to ManualRemoval after the internal conversion, so the record whose TIMESTAMP_END is 10:39:00 carries the label 10:38:30 inside the test. A bare '2025-12-19 10:39:00' would therefore match nothing and the removal would silently do nothing. It only matters when removing individual records: a window spanning days has edges far larger than the half-record offset.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.2_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
✏️ User settings (please adjust)
Adjust these before running. What each setting means:
Site - SITE, SITE_LAT, SITE_LON: site ID and coordinates. The coordinates set the day/night split used during screening — not used here, see Outlier detection.
Variable to screen - PROFILE, DEPTH, REPL: the sensor’s position tags. FIELD is assembled from them and is the InfluxDB _field. REPL changes the sensor family, not just the probe. - MEASUREMENT: exactly one measurement grouping the variables — TS for soil temperature.
Time range to screen - START: first timestamp to screen — is included. - STOP: upper bound — is not included.
Data settings - TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS: the critical timestamp knob — see Timestamp convention. Must match how the raw data was logged (1 for CET winter time) and must be the same value everywhere. - DATA_VERSION: the source data version in the database (raw). - DIRCONF: local folder holding the database connection config.
Resampling - RESAMPLING_FREQ / RESAMPLING_AGG: soil temperature is a state, so 'mean' — never 'sum'.
Physical range - TS_MIN, TS_MAX: the absolute-limits test, justified from this sensor’s own measured extremes.
Parameter help - SHOW_PARAM_HELP: True prints the full docstring of each screening method right before it runs.

# --- Site ---
SITE = 'ch-lae'
SITE_LAT = 47.478333  # CH-LAE
SITE_LON = 8.364389  # CH-LAE

# --- Variable to screen ---
# (!) REPL, not DEPTH, is what names the sensor family in this profile:
#       _1  the water-potential sensors of the 19 Mar 2020 install - MPS-2 at 0.05/0.1/0.6 m,
#           TEROS 21 at 0.2/0.3/0.5 m. Six channels.
#       _2  METER TEROS 12, the same probes that report SWC_FF1_<depth>_1. Five channels.
#       _3/_4  Campbell 109 thermistors at 0.05 m, added at the March 2021 logger rebuild.
# This notebook screens: METER TEROS 21 water-potential sensor, temperature channel.
PROFILE = 'FF1'  # horizontal position (soil profile)
DEPTH = '0.2'
REPL = '1'  # <-- the sensor family, see above
FIELD = f'TS_{PROFILE}_{DEPTH}_{REPL}'
FIELDS = [FIELD]  # StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb expects a list
MEASUREMENT = 'TS'

# --- Time range to screen ---
# Raw resolution is 10MIN until the March 2021 logger rebuild and 1MIN after, so this
# range is ~2.5 million records. The record starts 2020-04-10 15:00; asking for
# 2020-01-01 simply starts at the first record.
START = '2020-01-01 00:00:01'  # included
STOP = '2026-01-01 00:00:01'  # not included

# --- Data settings ---
DATA_VERSION = 'raw'
TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS = 1  # UTC+01:00 (CET, winter time). Must match how the raw data was logged.
DIRCONF = r'<LOCAL>\poet\configs'
# DIRCONF = r'P:\Flux\RDS_calculations\_scripts\_configs\configs'

# --- Resampling ---
RESAMPLING_FREQ = '30min'  # screened high-res data is resampled to this frequency
RESAMPLING_AGG = 'mean'  # (!) soil temperature is a state variable, never summed

# --- Physical range of soil temperature at this site, in degC ---
# Measured on this channel over 2020-2025 the raw record spans 0.00 to 53.35 degC - but both
# ends are artefacts, not soil: 0.00 is the failed-SDI-12-read sentinel and 53.35 is April 2024
# decode garbage. At 0.2 m the soil signal is damped further than at the depths above it (median
# daily amplitude 0.20 K, against 0.30 K at 0.1 m and 0.40 K at 0.05 m on this sensor family),
# so the seasonal swing is narrower still - roughly 2-19 degC. The limits below cannot fire on a
# measurement and do catch every decode record.
# (!) Verify against this channel's own extremes on the first run rather than trusting the line
#     above: the plot and the value counts below both show them.
TS_MIN, TS_MAX = -5, 30

# --- Parameter help ---
SHOW_PARAM_HELP = False

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.2_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
🔍 Outlier detection
Run a test → inspect its preview → commit with mscr.addflag(). Only the committed flag of the most recent test is added. Skip any test a variable does not need.
What is committed here: the December 2025 logger-artefact minutes (manual removal), the April 2024 SDI-12 decode garbage (absolute limits), and the missing-values flag. Why the rest are off:

Never split day and night. Soil temperature does have a diurnal cycle, but at this depth it is damped and lagged relative to the surface, so a solar-geometry split does not line up with it — it would only halve the sample behind every threshold. Every test below runs with separate_daytime_nighttime=False.
Distribution-wide tests measure the season, not a fault. A z-score over the whole record asks how far a value sits from the multi-year mean; January at 2 °C and July at 19 °C are both correct.
Differencing-based tests are degenerate on this record. The 10MIN era (to March 2021) is back-filled onto the 1MIN grid by diive, so nine of every ten increments are zero by construction; the 1MIN era is quantised to exactly 0.05 °C and the soil moves a few tenths of a kelvin a day, so ~97 % of minute-to-minute increments are genuinely zero. The rolling MAD a Hampel filter scales its band by is then zero, and raising n_sigma cannot help.


mscr.start_outlier_detection()

  > Starting step-wise outlier detection for variable TS_FF1_0.2_1 ...



Plot the current cleaned data at any point during detection:

for key, val in mscr.outlier_detection.items():
    val.showplot_cleaned(interactive=False)









Manual removal
Flag specific timestamps or time ranges for removal - known sensor failures, maintenance windows, logger artefacts. Give [start, stop] pairs and/or single timestamps.
Why this variable needs one. On 18-19 December 2025 two remote logger-program uploads corrupted the SDI-12 scale: in seven individual minutes all eleven SDI-12 channels of the profile depart from their own local median at once, by exactly the same factor — 0.00 × on four minutes and 0.50 × on three — while the two analogue Campbell 109 thermistors on a different port read a steady 4.8-5.7 °C throughout. Eleven probes between 5 and 60 cm cannot go to zero, or halve, in the same minute for any physical reason. No automatic test reaches them: 0.00 °C and 3.10 °C are both plausible December soil temperatures at 0.2 m, so absolute limits cannot see them, and the differencing tests are degenerate here.

The windows are written as [T − 1 min, T], and that is deliberate — see Timestamp convention. ManualRemoval matches against TIMESTAMP_MID, so the closed interval ['2025-12-19 10:38:00', '2025-12-19 10:39:00'] selects exactly the one record whose TIMESTAMP_END is 10:39:00, and a bare timestamp would select nothing. Asserted below.


⚠️ These windows are a bus event, not a property of this probe. They are shared with every SDI-12 channel — which is why they appear identically in the _1 notebook. Verify them on the preview plot rather than trusting the copy: REMOVE_DATES belongs to a sensor.


if SHOW_PARAM_HELP:
    help(dv.outliers.ManualRemoval)


REMOVE_DATES = [
    ['2025-12-18 17:44:00', '2025-12-18 17:45:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
    ['2025-12-19 09:48:00', '2025-12-19 09:49:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 09:50:00', '2025-12-19 09:51:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 09:56:00', '2025-12-19 09:57:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
    ['2025-12-19 10:30:00', '2025-12-19 10:31:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
    ['2025-12-19 10:35:00', '2025-12-19 10:36:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 10:38:00', '2025-12-19 10:39:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
]

# A window that brackets no middle stamp removes nothing at all, silently - so check the shape.
for _w in REMOVE_DATES:
    _s, _e = pd.Timestamp(_w[0]), pd.Timestamp(_w[1])
    assert _e - _s == pd.Timedelta('1min'), (
        f'(!) window {_w} is not the one-minute bracket the TIMESTAMP_MID convention needs')

if REMOVE_DATES:
    mscr.flag_manualremoval_test(remove_dates=REMOVE_DATES, showplot=True, verbose=True)
else:
    print('No manual removal windows for this sensor - skip the addflag cell below.')

  > running ManualRemoval ...











if REMOVE_DATES:
    mscr.addflag()

  > ++Added flag column FLAG_TS_FF1_0.2_1_OUTLIER_MANUAL_TEST to flag data





Absolute limits
Flags values outside a fixed physical range [minval, maxval]. This is the workhorse test for this channel: the only artefact that is not the December 2025 logger trouble is the April 2024 SDI-12 decode garbage, and every one of those records lands far outside anything the soil can do — this channel’s raw maximum is 80.00 °C.

⚠️ Do not clip instead. correction_setto_max_threshold(threshold=30) would turn an 80 °C decode error into a fabricated 30 °C - a value inside the physical range that nothing downstream could ever identify as fake. A removed value is honest; a clipped one is not.


if SHOW_PARAM_HELP:
    help(dv.outliers.AbsoluteLimits)


mscr.flag_outliers_abslim_test(minval=TS_MIN, maxval=TS_MAX, showplot=True, verbose=True)

  > running AbsoluteLimits ...











mscr.addflag()

  > ++Added flag column FLAG_TS_FF1_0.2_1_OUTLIER_ABSLIM_TEST to flag data





Other tests (all off)
Left switched off for the reasons given at the top of Outlier detection. If you do enable one, report its flagged count per era (10MIN before the March 2021 rebuild, 1MIN after) rather than as a total — the two eras behave completely differently. Note also that differencing-based tests compute their differences after dropping missing records, so the records flanking every gap are compared across the gap and look like spikes; this record has a 13-day gap in April 2024 and a 10-day one in September 2022.

# Optional, all off by default - read the note above before enabling any of these.
# mscr.flag_outliers_hampel_test(window_length=60 * 24, n_sigma=8, use_differencing=False,
#                                separate_daytime_nighttime=False,
#                                repeat=False, showplot=True, verbose=3)
# mscr.flag_outliers_zscore_test(thres_zscore=4.5, separate_daytime_nighttime=False,
#                                repeat=True, showplot=True, verbose=True)
# mscr.flag_outliers_zscore_rolling_test(thres_zscore=4.5, winsize=60 * 24 * 7,
#                                        repeat=True, showplot=True, verbose=True)
# mscr.flag_outliers_localsd_test(n_sd=7, winsize=60 * 24 * 7, constant_sd=False,
#                                 separate_daytime_nighttime=False,
#                                 repeat=False, showplot=True, verbose=True)
# mscr.flag_outliers_increments_zcore_test(thres_zscore=40, repeat=True, showplot=True, verbose=True)
# mscr.addflag()



Missing values
Not an outlier test - flags missing records so they are counted in the overall QCF.

mscr.flag_missingvals_test(verbose=True)

  > running MissingValues ...



  > MISSING VALUES TEST: Generated new flag variable FLAG_TS_FF1_0.2_1_MISSING_TEST, newly 
calculated from variable TS_FF1_0.2_1, with flag 0 (good values) where TS_FF1_0.2_1 is available, 
flag 2 (bad values) where TS_FF1_0.2_1 is missing.





Overall quality flag QCF
Aggregate all committed test flags into one overall flag QCF (0 = good, 1 = marginal, 2 = bad) and filter the series. Required before corrections and resampling.

mscr.finalize_outlier_detection()

text:
🔧 Corrections
Applied to the high-res, QCF-filtered data. None of them apply to soil temperature, and every call below stays commented out. The corrections diive offers are offset removals for radiation and relative humidity, threshold clipping, and setting ranges to a constant - every one of them writes a value the sensor did not measure.

⚠️ Do not set the exact value 0 to missing. correction_set_exact_value_to_missing(values=[0]) looks like the obvious way to catch the failed SDI-12 reads, and it is wrong twice over: it would delete every genuine 0.00 °C reading this soil ever produces, and it would miss the half-scale minutes entirely, because those are not a fixed value at all. That is why those minutes are handled by named manual removal instead.


mscr.showplot_cleaned()








Inspect the most frequent values first (read-only, safe to run). This channel is expected to show heavily repeated values: the 1MIN era is quantised to 0.05 °C, so a few hundred distinct values carry millions of records, and the 10MIN era is back-filled across ten 1MIN slots. What would be a fault is a single value appearing far more often than its neighbours in the seasonal distribution - that is a stuck sensor rather than a coarse one.

for ff in mscr.fields:
    vc = mscr.series_hires_cleaned[ff].value_counts()
    print(f'--- {ff} (top 20 of {mscr.series_hires_cleaned[ff].count():,} records, '
          f'{mscr.series_hires_cleaned[ff].nunique():,} distinct) ---')
    print(vc.head(20))

🔁 Resampling

Resample to 30MIN
Resample the screened high-res series to RESAMPLING_FREQ. The output timestamp is TIMESTAMP_END again (see Timestamp convention), ready for upload. This is the handover point: everything downstream of here works on the half-hourly series.

# mincounts_perc stays at the template default of .25, i.e. 7.5 of the 30 records a full
# half hour holds in the 1MIN era. A 30MIN *mean* of a smooth state variable is well
# estimated from a quarter of the records - this series moves a few hundredths of a kelvin
# in half an hour. (A *sum* would be the opposite case and is why the precipitation
# notebook chose differently.)
mscr.resample(to_freqstr=RESAMPLING_FREQ, agg=RESAMPLING_AGG, mincounts_perc=.25)
mscr.showplot_resampled()

Check the resampled time resolution

for v in mscr.resampled_detailed.keys():
    freq = dv.times.DetectFrequency(index=mscr.resampled_detailed[v].index, verbose=True).get()
    status = 'PASSED' if freq == RESAMPLING_FREQ else '(!) FAILED'

PASSED - TS_FF1_0.2_1: 30min




📉 The 2025 intermittent period, and why nothing is removed for it
This is the only channel in the FF1 profile with a fault of its own rather than a shared one. Between 2025-06-26 and 2025-07-06 it logged as few as 18-138 records/day against a normal 1 440 — an intermittent SDI-12 read failure, not a clean outage. It is why this channel’s coverage is 98.50 %, the lowest of the eleven SDI-12 channels.
No REMOVE_DATES window is drawn for it, and the reason is arithmetic rather than leniency. What that period produced is missing records, and a gap is already missing. Whether the records that did arrive are trustworthy is a separate question this notebook cannot answer at 1MIN resolution — but it largely does not have to, because the resampling coverage rule answers it first: a 30MIN mean needs 8 of 30 records (mincounts_perc=.25), and 138 records/day is under 3 per half hour on average. Most half hours in the window therefore never produce a value at all.
The cell below reports what actually survived, so the claim is measured rather than asserted. If half hours do survive in that window, treat them as suspect and settle them in 30_PRODUCTS/ against TS_FF1_0.2_2 — the TEROS 12 in the same soil at the same depth, which logged normally throughout. That comparison is cheap on 30MIN data and expensive here.

# What survived the coverage rule inside the 2025 intermittent period. Reporting only -
# nothing is removed here, and this cell makes no assertion because the honest answer is
# 'look at it', not 'it passed'.
_FAULT = ('2025-06-26', '2025-07-06')
_res = mscr.resampled_detailed[FIELD][FIELD]
_raw = data_detailed[FIELD][FIELD].dropna()

_raw_win = _raw.loc[_FAULT[0]:_FAULT[1]]
_res_win = _res.loc[_FAULT[0]:_FAULT[1]]
_perday = _raw_win.resample('D').count()

print(f'raw records/day in {_FAULT[0]} .. {_FAULT[1]} (normal is 1440):')
for _d, _n in _perday.items():
    print(f'   {_d:%Y-%m-%d}  {_n:5d}')
print(f'\n30MIN periods in the window:            {len(_res_win)}')
print(f'   with a value (survived the 25% rule): {int(_res_win.notna().sum())}')
print(f'   empty:                                {int(_res_win.isna().sum())}')
if int(_res_win.notna().sum()):
    print(f'   surviving values span {_res_win.min():.2f} .. {_res_win.max():.2f} degC')
    print('   -> check these against TS_FF1_0.2_2 in 30_PRODUCTS before trusting them')
else:
    print('   -> the coverage rule emptied the whole window; nothing to adjudicate')

text:
⬆️ Upload data to database
Re-uploading overwrites the same variant - safe to re-run. With delete_from_db_before_upload=True (below), the upload first deletes, then writes. The delete is scoped to the exact match _measurement + varname + data_version (meteoscreening_diive) over the uploaded time range, so re-screening a period replaces only its previous screened result. It never touches the raw data (different data_version, and a different _raw bucket), other variables, or other data versions. The delete-first step (rather than a plain overwrite) matters because InfluxDB keys a point by its full tag set: if a tag changed between runs (e.g. units, gain, offset), a plain write would leave the old point as a duplicate - the delete removes it regardless of tags.

print(f'Uploading to bucket {BUCKET_PROCESSED}')
for v in mscr.resampled_detailed.keys():
    dbc.upload_singlevar(
        to_bucket=BUCKET_PROCESSED,
        to_measurement=assigned_measurements[v],
        var_df=mscr.resampled_detailed[v],
        timezone_offset_to_utc_hours=TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS,
        delete_from_db_before_upload=True,
    )

📝 Notes for this variable

Mean, not sum. RESAMPLING_AGG = 'mean' - soil temperature is a state, not a flux.
Units are °C, filegroup 12_meteo_forestfloor.
Sensor identity. The temperature channel of a METER TEROS 21 water-potential sensor installed 19 Mar 2020 at 0.2 m, first logged 2020-04-10 15:00. Not an MPS-2 — that family covers only 0.05, 0.1 and 0.6 m; from 0.2 m down the _1 channels are TEROS 21. And not a TEROS 12, which is TS_FF1_0.2_2. Three sensor makes share this profile and the suffix names the family, not the depth.
Coverage 2 491 244 records, 98.50 % — the lowest of the eleven SDI-12 channels, and the shortfall is this channel’s own: the 2025-06-26 … 07-06 intermittent period on top of the five shared outages. See the dedicated section above.
Raw range 0.00 … 53.35 °C, both ends artefacts: 0.00 is the failed-SDI-12-read sentinel, 53.35 is April 2024 decode garbage.
Median daily amplitude 0.20 K (2023), against 0.30 K at 0.1 m and 0.20 K at 0.3 m on the same family. The damping is monotone but the depths below 0.3 m can no longer be separated this way: at a 0.05 °C storage step a 0.20 K amplitude is four steps, and the resolution starts to set the number rather than the soil.
Two raw time resolutions, 10MIN until the March 2021 logger rebuild and 1MIN after; diive upsamples the coarser era onto the finest grid before screening. Report any test’s flagged count per era, never as a total.
Values are quantised to 0.05 °C in the 1MIN era — see the amplitude note above for why that matters more at this depth than at 0.05 m.
A failed sensor read is a number, not a gap — a failed SDI-12 read arrives as the true value times a wrong scale factor (0 × or 0.5 ×), so notna() does not mean “measured”.
Deferred to 30_PRODUCTS/, on the 30MIN data: the comparison against the rest of the FF1 profile and against air temperature, the placement and offset questions, and any gap handling. This notebook exports gaps where the station was down and does not fill them.



♻️ Sibling notebooks
Its same-depth partner is TS_FF1_0.2_2, the TEROS 12 — a different make of sensor in the same soil at the same nominal depth, and the reference against which the 2025 intermittent period should be settled in 30_PRODUCTS/.
This notebook is a near-copy of TS_FF1_0.1_1_2020-2025.ipynb in structure, but the sensor is not the same make: 0.05 and 0.1 m carry MPS-2 probes, 0.2 m and below carry TEROS 21. Do not carry the instrument name across when copying further down the profile.
The standing rule for all of them: REMOVE_DATES belongs to a sensor, not to a variable. These notebooks are copies of each other with a few settings changed, and carrying a window across a copy deletes good data under a justification written about a different probe.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.1_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
ℹ️ About this notebook
Download raw soil temperature from the InfluxDB database, remove the worst outliers on the high-resolution data, resample to 30MIN, and upload the result back to the database. Screening uses StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb from diive (diive/preprocessing/qaqc/meteoscreening.py); download and upload use diive’s in-house InfluxDB engine (InfluxIO, in diive/core/io/db/influx).
Flow: download (InfluxIO) → screen on high-res data (diive) → resample to 30MIN → upload.
Scope is deliberately narrow. The raw record is millions of rows, so anything done here is expensive. This notebook only takes out what is unambiguously wrong at high resolution — the April 2024 SDI-12 decode garbage (absolute limits) and the seven December 2025 logger-artefact minutes (manual removal) — and hands over a clean 30MIN series. Everything else (sensor comparisons, level/offset questions, gap handling, homogenisation across sensor generations) is settled later in 30_PRODUCTS/, on the half-hourly data, where it costs a fraction as much.
Outlier detection is stepwise: run a test, inspect its preview plot, then commit it with mscr.addflag(). Re-run with different parameters as often as you like before committing. Run only the tests a variable actually needs. At the end all committed flags are aggregated into one overall quality flag QCF.

Which sensor this is. In this profile the replicate suffix names the sensor family, not the depth: _1 = the water-potential sensors of the 19 Mar 2020 install (MPS-2 at 0.05/0.1/0.6 m, TEROS 21 at 0.2/0.3/0.5 m), _2 = the TEROS 12 probes that also report SWC_FF1_<depth>_1, _3/_4 = Campbell 109 thermistors added at the March 2021 logger rebuild. This one is a METER MPS-2 water-potential sensor, temperature channel.


Database access needs the influxdb-client package, which this project pulls in via the diive[db] extra (declared in pyproject.toml). diive also ships a db dependency group, but dependency groups are local to the project that declares them — uv sync --group db only works inside the diive repo, not from here.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.1_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
⏱️ Timestamp convention (important)
The database stores every timestamp in UTC and as TIMESTAMP_END (the stamp marks the end of the averaging interval). Getting this right is the one thing that must not go wrong: the value written back to the database depends on it, and so does every window in REMOVE_DATES.
The single knob is TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS (set in User settings). It is applied identically on download and on upload:









Stage
Timezone
Convention
Done by




Database
UTC
TIMESTAMP_END
InfluxDB


After dbc.download(..., timezone_offset_to_utc_hours=N)
local (UTC+N)
TIMESTAMP_END
InfluxIO


During screening
local
TIMESTAMP_MIDDLE (converted internally)
StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb


After mscr.resample()
local
back to TIMESTAMP_END
diive


After dbc.upload_singlevar(..., timezone_offset_to_utc_hours=N)
UTC
TIMESTAMP_END
InfluxIO



One place where this bites. REMOVE_DATES is matched against TIMESTAMP_MID, not TIMESTAMP_END: StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb hands the series to ManualRemoval after the internal conversion, so the record whose TIMESTAMP_END is 10:39:00 carries the label 10:38:30 inside the test. A bare '2025-12-19 10:39:00' would therefore match nothing and the removal would silently do nothing. It only matters when removing individual records: a window spanning days has edges far larger than the half-record offset.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.1_1 (2020-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
✏️ User settings (please adjust)
Adjust these before running. What each setting means:
Site - SITE, SITE_LAT, SITE_LON: site ID and coordinates. The coordinates set the day/night split used during screening — not used here, see Outlier detection.
Variable to screen - PROFILE, DEPTH, REPL: the sensor’s position tags. FIELD is assembled from them and is the InfluxDB _field. REPL changes the sensor family, not just the probe. - MEASUREMENT: exactly one measurement grouping the variables — TS for soil temperature.
Time range to screen - START: first timestamp to screen — is included. - STOP: upper bound — is not included.
Data settings - TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS: the critical timestamp knob — see Timestamp convention. Must match how the raw data was logged (1 for CET winter time) and must be the same value everywhere. - DATA_VERSION: the source data version in the database (raw). - DIRCONF: local folder holding the database connection config.
Resampling - RESAMPLING_FREQ / RESAMPLING_AGG: soil temperature is a state, so 'mean' — never 'sum'.
Physical range - TS_MIN, TS_MAX: the absolute-limits test, justified from this sensor’s own measured extremes.
Parameter help - SHOW_PARAM_HELP: True prints the full docstring of each screening method right before it runs.

# --- Site ---
SITE = 'ch-lae'
SITE_LAT = 47.478333  # CH-LAE
SITE_LON = 8.364389  # CH-LAE

# --- Variable to screen ---
# (!) REPL, not DEPTH, is what names the sensor family in this profile:
#       _1  the water-potential sensors of the 19 Mar 2020 install - MPS-2 at 0.05/0.1/0.6 m,
#           TEROS 21 at 0.2/0.3/0.5 m. Six channels.
#       _2  METER TEROS 12, the same probes that report SWC_FF1_<depth>_1. Five channels.
#       _3/_4  Campbell 109 thermistors at 0.05 m, added at the March 2021 logger rebuild.
# This notebook screens: METER MPS-2 water-potential sensor, temperature channel.
PROFILE = 'FF1'  # horizontal position (soil profile)
DEPTH = '0.1'
REPL = '1'  # <-- the sensor family, see above
FIELD = f'TS_{PROFILE}_{DEPTH}_{REPL}'
FIELDS = [FIELD]  # StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb expects a list
MEASUREMENT = 'TS'

# --- Time range to screen ---
# Raw resolution is 10MIN until the March 2021 logger rebuild and 1MIN after, so this
# range is ~2.5 million records. The record starts 2020-04-10 15:00; asking for
# 2020-01-01 simply starts at the first record.
START = '2020-01-01 00:00:01'  # included
STOP = '2026-01-01 00:00:01'  # not included

# --- Data settings ---
DATA_VERSION = 'raw'
TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS = 1  # UTC+01:00 (CET, winter time). Must match how the raw data was logged.
DIRCONF = r'<LOCAL>\poet\configs'
# DIRCONF = r'P:\Flux\RDS_calculations\_scripts\_configs\configs'

# --- Resampling ---
RESAMPLING_FREQ = '30min'  # screened high-res data is resampled to this frequency
RESAMPLING_AGG = 'mean'  # (!) soil temperature is a state variable, never summed

# --- Physical range of soil temperature at this site, in degC ---
# Measured on this channel over 2020-2025 the raw record spans 0.00 to 40.60 degC - but both
# ends are artefacts, not soil: 0.00 is the failed-SDI-12-read sentinel and 40.60 is April 2024
# decode garbage. The soil signal at 0.1 m is *damped relative to 0.05 m* (median daily amplitude
# 0.30 K against 0.40 K on the same sensor family), so it cannot reach further than the shallower
# channel does - and that one spans 1.70 to 19.60 degC. The limits below therefore sit several
# kelvin outside anything this depth can produce, and do catch every decode record.
# (!) Verify against this channel's own extremes on the first run rather than trusting the line
#     above: the plot and the value counts below both show them.
TS_MIN, TS_MAX = -5, 30

# --- Parameter help ---
SHOW_PARAM_HELP = False

text:
🔍 Outlier detection
Run a test → inspect its preview → commit with mscr.addflag(). Only the committed flag of the most recent test is added. Skip any test a variable does not need.
What is committed here: the December 2025 logger-artefact minutes (manual removal), the April 2024 SDI-12 decode garbage (absolute limits), and the missing-values flag. Why the rest are off:

Never split day and night. Soil temperature does have a diurnal cycle, but at this depth it is damped and lagged relative to the surface, so a solar-geometry split does not line up with it — it would only halve the sample behind every threshold. Every test below runs with separate_daytime_nighttime=False.
Distribution-wide tests measure the season, not a fault. A z-score over the whole record asks how far a value sits from the multi-year mean; January at 2 °C and July at 19 °C are both correct.
Differencing-based tests are degenerate on this record. The 10MIN era (to March 2021) is back-filled onto the 1MIN grid by diive, so nine of every ten increments are zero by construction; the 1MIN era is quantised to exactly 0.05 °C and the soil moves a few tenths of a kelvin a day, so ~97 % of minute-to-minute increments are genuinely zero. The rolling MAD a Hampel filter scales its band by is then zero, and raising n_sigma cannot help.


mscr.start_outlier_detection()

  > Starting step-wise outlier detection for variable TS_FF1_0.1_1 ...



Plot the current cleaned data at any point during detection:

for key, val in mscr.outlier_detection.items():
    val.showplot_cleaned(interactive=False)









Manual removal
Flag specific timestamps or time ranges for removal - known sensor failures, maintenance windows, logger artefacts. Give [start, stop] pairs and/or single timestamps.
Why this variable needs one. On 18-19 December 2025 two remote logger-program uploads corrupted the SDI-12 scale: in seven individual minutes all eleven SDI-12 channels of the profile depart from their own local median at once, by exactly the same factor — 0.00 × on four minutes and 0.50 × on three — while the two analogue Campbell 109 thermistors on a different port read a steady 4.8-5.7 °C throughout. Eleven probes between 5 and 60 cm cannot go to zero, or halve, in the same minute for any physical reason. No automatic test reaches them: 0.00 °C and 3.10 °C are both plausible December soil temperatures at 0.1 m, so absolute limits cannot see them, and the differencing tests are degenerate here.

The windows are written as [T − 1 min, T], and that is deliberate — see Timestamp convention. ManualRemoval matches against TIMESTAMP_MID, so the closed interval ['2025-12-19 10:38:00', '2025-12-19 10:39:00'] selects exactly the one record whose TIMESTAMP_END is 10:39:00, and a bare timestamp would select nothing. Asserted below.


⚠️ These windows are a bus event, not a property of this probe. They are shared with every SDI-12 channel — which is why they appear identically in the _1 notebook. Verify them on the preview plot rather than trusting the copy: REMOVE_DATES belongs to a sensor.

    ['2025-12-19 09:48:00', '2025-12-19 09:49:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 09:50:00', '2025-12-19 09:51:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 09:56:00', '2025-12-19 09:57:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
    ['2025-12-19 10:30:00', '2025-12-19 10:31:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
    ['2025-12-19 10:35:00', '2025-12-19 10:36:00'],  # reads exactly half the true value
    ['2025-12-19 10:38:00', '2025-12-19 10:39:00'],  # reads 0.00 on all eleven SDI-12 channels
]

# A window that brackets no middle stamp removes nothing at all, silently - so check the shape.
for _w in REMOVE_DATES:

⬆️ Upload data to database
Re-uploading overwrites the same variant - safe to re-run. With delete_from_db_before_upload=True (below), the upload first deletes, then writes. The delete is scoped to the exact match _measurement + varname + data_version (meteoscreening_diive) over the uploaded time range, so re-screening a period replaces only its previous screened result. It never touches the raw data (different data_version, and a different _raw bucket), other variables, or other data versions. The delete-first step (rather than a plain overwrite) matters because InfluxDB keys a point by its full tag set: if a tag changed between runs (e.g. units, gain, offset), a plain write would leave the old point as a duplicate - the delete removes it regardless of tags.

📝 Notes for this variable

Mean, not sum. RESAMPLING_AGG = 'mean' - soil temperature is a state, not a flux.
Units are °C, filegroup 12_meteo_forestfloor.
Sensor identity. The temperature channel of a METER MPS-2 water-potential sensor installed 19 Mar 2020 at 0.1 m, first logged 2020-04-10 15:00. It is not a TEROS 12 - that is TS_FF1_0.1_2, the same physical probe that reports SWC_FF1_0.1_1. The replicate suffix names the sensor family, and the mapping is the opposite of the obvious guess.
Coverage 2 506 841 records, 99.12 % over 2020-2025 - the most complete channel in the FF1 profile. Its gaps are the five shared power and logger outages, not sensor events.
Raw range 0.00 … 40.60 °C, both ends artefacts: 0.00 is the failed-SDI-12-read sentinel, 40.60 is April 2024 decode garbage.
Median daily amplitude 0.30 K (2023), against 0.40 K for the same sensor family at 0.05 m and 0.20 K at 0.2 m. The damping with depth is monotone, which is the cheapest check that this channel is where it claims to be.
Two raw time resolutions, 10MIN until the March 2021 logger rebuild and 1MIN after. diive drops any resolution group holding <0.2 % of records and upsamples the coarser era onto the finest grid before screening. Report any test’s flagged count per era, never as a total.
Values are quantised to 0.05 °C in the 1MIN era. At an 0.30 K daily amplitude that is six steps - still resolvable, but do not read fine structure into it, and do not expect a differencing-based test to work.
A failed sensor read is a number, not a gap. The CR1000 firmware predates SDI-12 NaN support and the update was declined on 2020-04-10, so a failed read arrives as the true value times a wrong scale factor (0 × or 0.5 ×). notna() does not mean “measured”, and neither does “inside the physical range”.
Deferred to 30_PRODUCTS/, on the 30MIN data: the comparison against the rest of the FF1 profile and against air temperature, the placement and offset questions, and any gap handling. This notebook exports gaps where the station was down and does not fill them.



♻️ Sibling notebooks
Its same-depth partner is TS_FF1_0.1_2, the TEROS 12 — a different make of sensor in the same soil at the same nominal depth, which makes it the sharpest available check on whether a change is in the sensor or in the soil. That comparison belongs in 30_PRODUCTS/, on the 30MIN data, not here.
This notebook is a near-copy of TS_FF1_0.05_1_2020-2025.ipynb: both are MPS-2 channels on the SDI-12 bus, so the seven removal windows and the quantisation argument carry across unchanged. The 0.05_3/0.05_4 notebooks are not copies in that sense — those are analogue thermistors and three of the arguments invert.
The standing rule for all of them: REMOVE_DATES belongs to a sensor, not to a variable. These notebooks are copies of each other with a few settings changed, and carrying a window across a copy deletes good data under a justification written about a different probe.

text:
ℹ️ About this notebook
Download raw soil temperature from the InfluxDB database, remove the worst outliers on the high-resolution data, resample to 30MIN, and upload the result back to the database. Screening uses StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb from diive (diive/preprocessing/qaqc/meteoscreening.py); download and upload use diive’s in-house InfluxDB engine (InfluxIO, in diive/core/io/db/influx).
Flow: download (InfluxIO) → screen on high-res data (diive) → resample to 30MIN → upload.
Scope is deliberately narrow. The raw record is millions of rows, so anything done here is expensive. This notebook only takes out what is unambiguously wrong at high resolution — nothing, as it turns out — and hands over a clean 30MIN series. Everything else (sensor comparisons, level/offset questions, gap handling, homogenisation across sensor generations) is settled later in 30_PRODUCTS/, on the half-hourly data, where it costs a fraction as much.
Outlier detection is stepwise: run a test, inspect its preview plot, then commit it with mscr.addflag(). Re-run with different parameters as often as you like before committing. Run only the tests a variable actually needs. At the end all committed flags are aggregated into one overall quality flag QCF.

Which sensor this is. In this profile the replicate suffix names the sensor family, not the depth: _1 = the water-potential sensors of the 19 Mar 2020 install (MPS-2 at 0.05/0.1/0.6 m, TEROS 21 at 0.2/0.3/0.5 m), _2 = the TEROS 12 probes that also report SWC_FF1_<depth>_1, _3/_4 = Campbell 109 thermistors added at the March 2021 logger rebuild. This one is a Campbell 109 thermistor (analogue, not on the SDI-12 bus). Being analogue rather than SDI-12 is what makes this notebook differ from its _1/_2 siblings, in three places marked below.


Database access needs the influxdb-client package, which this project pulls in via the diive[db] extra (declared in pyproject.toml). diive also ships a db dependency group, but dependency groups are local to the project that declares them — uv sync --group db only works inside the diive repo, not from here.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.05_3 (2021-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
⏱️ Timestamp convention (important)
The database stores every timestamp in UTC and as TIMESTAMP_END (the stamp marks the end of the averaging interval). Getting this right is the one thing that must not go wrong: the value written back to the database depends on it, and so does every window in REMOVE_DATES.
The single knob is TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS (set in User settings). It is applied identically on download and on upload:

One place where this bites. REMOVE_DATES is matched against TIMESTAMP_MID, not TIMESTAMP_END: StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb hands the series to ManualRemoval after the internal conversion, so the record whose TIMESTAMP_END is 10:39:00 carries the label 10:38:30 inside the test. A bare '2025-12-19 10:39:00' would therefore match nothing and the removal would silently do nothing. It only matters when removing individual records: a window spanning days has edges far larger than the half-record offset.

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.05_3 (2021-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
✏️ User settings (please adjust)
Adjust these before running. What each setting means:
Site - SITE, SITE_LAT, SITE_LON: site ID and coordinates. The coordinates set the day/night split used during screening — not used here, see Outlier detection.
Variable to screen - PROFILE, DEPTH, REPL: the sensor’s position tags. FIELD is assembled from them and is the InfluxDB _field. REPL changes the sensor family, not just the probe. - MEASUREMENT: exactly one measurement grouping the variables — TS for soil temperature.
Time range to screen - START: first timestamp to screen — is included. - STOP: upper bound — is not included.
Data settings - TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS: the critical timestamp knob — see Timestamp convention. Must match how the raw data was logged (1 for CET winter time) and must be the same value everywhere. - DATA_VERSION: the source data version in the database (raw). - DIRCONF: local folder holding the database connection config.
Resampling - RESAMPLING_FREQ / RESAMPLING_AGG: soil temperature is a state, so 'mean' — never 'sum'.
Physical range - TS_MIN, TS_MAX: the absolute-limits test, justified from this sensor’s own measured extremes.
Parameter help - SHOW_PARAM_HELP: True prints the full docstring of each screening method right before it runs.

# --- Site ---
SITE = 'ch-lae'
SITE_LAT = 47.478333  # CH-LAE
SITE_LON = 8.364389  # CH-LAE

# --- Variable to screen ---
# (!) REPL, not DEPTH, is what names the sensor family in this profile:
#       _1  the water-potential sensors of the 19 Mar 2020 install - MPS-2 at 0.05/0.1/0.6 m,
#           TEROS 21 at 0.2/0.3/0.5 m. Six channels.
#       _2  METER TEROS 12, the same probes that report SWC_FF1_<depth>_1. Five channels.
#       _3/_4  Campbell 109 thermistors at 0.05 m, added at the March 2021 logger rebuild.
# This notebook screens: Campbell 109 thermistor (analogue, not on the SDI-12 bus).
PROFILE = 'FF1'  # horizontal position (soil profile)
DEPTH = '0.05'
REPL = '3'  # <-- the sensor family, see above
FIELD = f'TS_{PROFILE}_{DEPTH}_{REPL}'
FIELDS = [FIELD]  # StepwiseMeteoScreeningDb expects a list
MEASUREMENT = 'TS'

# --- Time range to screen ---
# This channel was added at the March 2021 logger rebuild and first logged on
# 2021-03-26 15:22, so it has a SINGLE resolution era: 1MIN throughout. Asking for
# 2021-01-01 simply starts at the first record. Nothing before 2021-03-26 belongs to
# this series - the Campbell 107 thermistors it replaced live under different names.
START = '2021-01-01 00:00:01'  # included
STOP = '2026-01-01 00:00:01'  # not included

# --- Data settings ---
DATA_VERSION = 'raw'
TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS = 1  # UTC+01:00 (CET, winter time). Must match how the raw data was logged.
DIRCONF = r'<LOCAL>\poet\configs'
# DIRCONF = r'P:\Flux\RDS_calculations\_scripts\_configs\configs'

# --- Resampling ---
RESAMPLING_FREQ = '30min'  # screened high-res data is resampled to this frequency
RESAMPLING_AGG = 'mean'  # (!) soil temperature is a state variable, never summed

# --- Physical range of soil temperature at this site, in degC ---
# Measured on this channel over 2021-2025: 1.04 to 20.05 degC, with no artefact of any kind -
# this is the cleanest channel in the profile. The limits below therefore sit ~6 K below the
# coldest and ~10 K above the warmest value it has produced, and act purely as a backstop
# against an open-circuit thermistor (which rails, rather than returning a plausible number).
TS_MIN, TS_MAX = -5, 30

# --- Parameter help ---
SHOW_PARAM_HELP = False

title: MeteoScreening TS_FF1_0.05_3 (2021-2025) from database (influxdb)
text:
🔍 Outlier detection
Run a test → inspect its preview → commit with mscr.addflag(). Only the committed flag of the most recent test is added. Skip any test a variable does not need.
What is committed here: a physical-range backstop (absolute limits) and the missing-values flag. Why the rest are off:

Never split day and night. Soil temperature does have a diurnal cycle, but at this depth it is damped and lagged relative to the surface, so a solar-geometry split does not line up with it — it would only halve the sample behind every threshold. Every test below runs with separate_daytime_nighttime=False.
Distribution-wide tests measure the season, not a fault. A z-score over the whole record asks how far a value sits from the multi-year mean; January at 2 °C and July at 19 °C are both correct.
Differencing-based tests would actually work here — and are still not committed. This is the one place where this notebook differs from its _1/_2 siblings on a point of arithmetic rather than taste. Those channels are SDI-12 and quantised to a 0.05 °C grid, which collapses the rolling MAD a Hampel filter scales its band by to exactly zero. This one is an analogue thermistor: its values are continuous (only 0.007 % land on that grid, i.e. at chance) and it has a single 1MIN resolution era with no back-filling. So a spike test has a real scale to work with. It is left off because there is nothing for it to find, not because it would misbehave — see Other tests below. If any channel in this family ever justifies one, it is this one.


mscr.start_outlier_detection()

  > Starting step-wise outlier detection for variable TS_FF1_0.05_3 ...



Plot the current cleaned data at any point during detection:

for key, val in mscr.outlier_detection.items():
    val.showplot_cleaned(interactive=False)









Manual removal
Flag specific timestamps or time ranges for removal - known sensor failures, maintenance windows, logger artefacts. Give [start, stop] pairs and/or single timestamps.
This channel needs none, and the empty list is the finding. Two reasons, both specific to it:

It is not on the SDI-12 bus. The seven artefact minutes of 18-19 December 2025 that the _1 and _2 notebooks remove are a bus event: eleven SDI-12 channels going to 0 × or 0.5 × their true value in the same minute. This analogue thermistor read a steady 4.8-5.7 °C straight through all seven, which is part of how the artefact was identified as a bus fault in the first place. The same applies to the April 2024 SDI-12 bus failure — this channel logged 1 440 records/day right through the outage that emptied the rest of the profile.
It has no fault of its own. Over 2021-2025 it never leaves 1.04-20.05 °C, with no episode of the kind its twin 0.05_4 shows in 2022.

The cells below are guarded on REMOVE_DATES and skip themselves when it is empty, so a Run All is safe.

⚠️ Do not copy windows in from a sibling notebook. A removal window belongs to a sensor. The _1/_2 windows describe a bus this sensor is not attached to, and the _4 window describes a probe that left the soil — neither is a statement about this one.


if SHOW_PARAM_HELP:
    help(dv.outliers.ManualRemoval)


# This channel is NOT on the SDI-12 bus, so the seven December 2025 artefact minutes that the
# _1 and _2 notebooks remove do not exist here - this thermistor read normally straight through
# them, which is part of how they were identified in the first place. Nothing else in the record
# needs a hand-drawn window: measured over 2021-2025 this channel never leaves 1.04-20.05 degC.
# (!) Do not copy windows in from a sibling notebook. A removal window belongs to a sensor.
REMOVE_DATES = []

if REMOVE_DATES:
    mscr.flag_manualremoval_test(remove_dates=REMOVE_DATES, showplot=True, verbose=True)
else:
    print('No manual removal windows for this sensor - skip the addflag cell below.')

No manual removal windows for this sensor - skip the addflag cell below.



if REMOVE_DATES:
    mscr.addflag()



Absolute limits
Flags values outside a fixed physical range [minval, maxval]. On this channel it is a backstop, not a workhorse: being analogue, it never saw the SDI-12 decode garbage that this test exists to catch on the _1/_2 channels. What it guards against is an open-circuit or shorted thermistor, which rails rather than returning a plausible number. Expect it to flag nothing, and treat it flagging anything as news.

⚠️ Do not clip instead. correction_setto_max_threshold would turn a railed reading into a fabricated in-range value that nothing downstream could identify as fake. A removed value is honest; a clipped one is not.


if SHOW_PARAM_HELP:
    help(dv.outliers.AbsoluteLimits)


mscr.flag_outliers_abslim_test(minval=TS_MIN, maxval=TS_MAX, showplot=True, verbose=True)

  > running AbsoluteLimits ...











mscr.addflag()

  > ++Added flag column FLAG_TS_FF1_0.05_3_OUTLIER_ABSLIM_TEST to flag data





Other tests (all off)
Left switched off — but for a different reason than in the _1/_2 notebooks, and the difference matters if you ever reach for one.
There, differencing-based tests are broken: quantisation collapses their scale estimate to zero. Here they are merely unnecessary. This channel is analogue and continuous, on a single 1MIN grid, so a Hampel filter has a real MAD to work with and would behave sensibly. The reason not to commit one is that there is nothing left for it to find once the manual removal has run — and a spike test on a 1MIN soil record mostly rediscovers the fact that soil temperature is smooth.
If you do enable one: there is no per-era split to worry about on this channel (single resolution era), but differencing-based tests still compute their differences after dropping missing records, so the records flanking every gap are compared across the gap and look like spikes. Check what it flags against the gap list before believing it.

text:
🔧 Corrections
Applied to the high-res, QCF-filtered data. None of them apply to soil temperature, and every call below stays commented out. The corrections diive offers are offset removals for radiation and relative humidity, threshold clipping, and setting ranges to a constant - every one of them writes a value the sensor did not measure.

text:
⬆️ Upload data to database
Re-uploading overwrites the same variant - safe to re-run. With delete_from_db_before_upload=True (below), the upload first deletes, then writes. The delete is scoped to the exact match _measurement + varname + data_version (meteoscreening_diive) over the uploaded time range, so re-screening a period replaces only its previous screened result. It never touches the raw data (different data_version, and a different _raw bucket), other variables, or other data versions. The delete-first step (rather than a plain overwrite) matters because InfluxDB keys a point by its full tag set: if a tag changed between runs (e.g. units, gain, offset), a plain write would leave the old point as a duplicate - the delete removes it regardless of tags.

Mean, not sum. RESAMPLING_AGG = 'mean' - soil temperature is a state, not a flux.
Units are °C, filegroup 12_meteo_forestfloor.
Sensor identity. Campbell 109 thermistor, analogue, added at the March 2021 logger rebuild and first logged 2021-03-26 15:22 — 350 days after the rest of the profile.
