title: Download and prepare PPFD_IN (2004-2026.09)
section: 🔎 Which sensor this is, and what the hardware changes did to it
text:
🔎 Which sensor this is, and what the hardware changes did to it
The tower logger was replaced on 21 January 2016, and TA_T1_47_1 steps by about 1.3 °C there (notebook 02). The fieldbook also records a Kipp & Zonen PAR sensor installed on 8 January 2016, so the question is whether the column is the same instrument across that month.
It is. The steps below show that:

the exported column is the Delta-T sunshine sensor, not the Kipp & Zonen PAR LITE;
the record begins after that sensor replaced a different probe at the same storage location;
the PAR LITE has its own column, which starts at the changeover;
there is no step at January 2016;
the 2011 and 2013 changes are not this sensor;
there is no step at the December 2021 screening splice;
the fieldbook records no replacement or calibration of this sensor;
the sensor’s response fell between the 2022 and 2024 seasons and has not recovered; the fall has not continued since 2024. This is the only finding that is not a negative result, and a limitation of the product.

RADIATION_SENSOR_CONTINUITY.ipynb makes the full attribution, with the NABEL pyranometer at 49 m as a fourth witness, and places the decline on this sensor. This section carries what bears on this product and the assertions that keep it true.

Helpers for this section
The logger programs and the fieldbook are read, not quoted, so a re-run re-derives the argument. Both name people and this notebook is published, so every extracted string is redacted as in notebooks 01, 02 and 08.

# --- Fieldbook and logger-program redaction ----------------------------------------------------
# The GIN export and the logger programs both name people and this notebook renders to a public
# page, so every extracted string passes through redact_people() where it is flattened. Same map
# and rules as notebooks 01, 02 and 08; the map lives beside the export, OUTSIDE this repository.
REDACT_MAP = Path(FIELDBOOK).with_name('redact_names.csv')
ALLOW_LIST = Path(FIELDBOOK).with_name('redact_allow.csv')


def unmapped_report_path(label: str) -> Path:
    """Where the unmapped-name candidates of one audit are written.

    Per label, because this notebook audits two sources: a single shared file would let the
    second audit overwrite the first one's findings.
    """
    _slug = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', label.lower()).strip('_')
    return Path(FIELDBOOK).with_name(f'redact_unmapped_{_slug}.txt')


def load_redactions(path=None) -> dict:
    """Load the name -> pseudonym map.

    Raises if the map is missing. That is the point: carrying on with redaction quietly disabled
    prints real names into a published page and looks exactly like success.
    """
    path = REDACT_MAP if path is None else Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"the redaction map is missing: {path}. Without it the names these files record would "
            f"print unredacted. Restore the file rather than skipping this.")
    tab = pd.read_csv(path, encoding='utf-8')
    missing = {'name', 'pseudonym'}.difference(tab.columns)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: missing column(s) {sorted(missing)}.")
    pairs = {str(n).strip(): str(p).strip()
             for n, p in zip(tab['name'], tab['pseudonym']) if str(n).strip()}
    if not pairs:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: holds no usable name -> pseudonym pairs.")
    return pairs


REDACTIONS = load_redactions()
# Longest surface form first, so a bare surname cannot corrupt a double-barrelled one that starts
# with it. Lookarounds rather than \b, because some forms end in an initial.
_REDACT_RX = re.compile(r'(?<!\w)(' + '|'.join(re.escape(n) for n in
                                               sorted(REDACTIONS, key=len, reverse=True))
                        + r')(?!\w)')


def redact_people(s) -> str:
    """Replace every mapped name with its stable pseudonym."""
    return _REDACT_RX.sub(lambda m: REDACTIONS[m.group(1)], str(s))


def strip_html(text) -> str:
    """Flatten one GIN fieldbook entry to plain text, with the people it names redacted."""
    flat = html.unescape(re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', str(text)))
    return redact_people(re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', flat).strip())


_NAME_TOKEN = r"[A-ZÄÖÜ][\wÄÖÜäöüß'-]{1,20}"
_NAME_UNIT = _NAME_TOKEN + r'(?:\s+' + _NAME_TOKEN + r'){0,2}'
_NAME_SHAPES = (
    re.compile(r'\((' + _NAME_UNIT + r'(?:\s*[,+&]\s*' + _NAME_UNIT + r')*)\s*'
               r'(?:\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}\.\d{4})?\)'),
    re.compile(r'(?:with|by|durch|von|gemaess)\s+(' + _NAME_TOKEN + r'(?:\s+' + _NAME_TOKEN + r')?)'),
)


def audit_unmapped_names(texts, label='fieldbook', write_report: bool = True) -> int:
    """Raise if any name-shaped token survived redaction.

    A newer export can name someone the map has never seen. Candidates are never printed - an
    exception message is stored in a notebook like any other output - so they go to a file beside
    the map and only the count is shown.
    """
    allow = set(pd.read_csv(ALLOW_LIST, encoding='utf-8')['term'].astype(str).str.strip())
    found = {}
    for _t in texts:
        for _rx in _NAME_SHAPES:
            for _m in _rx.finditer(str(_t)):
                for _tok in re.findall(_NAME_TOKEN, _m.group(1)):
                    if _tok.isupper() or any(ch.isdigit() for ch in _tok) or _tok in allow:
                        continue
                    found[_tok] = found.get(_tok, 0) + 1
    if found:
        _report = unmapped_report_path(label)
        if write_report:
            _report.write_text(
                '\n'.join(f'{n}\t{t}' for t, n in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])),
                encoding='utf-8')
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label}: {len(found)} name-shaped token(s) survived redaction. They are deliberately "
            f"NOT shown here - see {_report}. Add the people to redact_names.csv and the "
            f"technical terms to redact_allow.csv, then re-run.")
    print(f"  {label}: no unmapped name-shaped tokens ({len(allow)} allowlisted terms)")
    return 0


def program_excerpt(path, pattern: str, before: int = 6, after: int = 4, expect: int = 1) -> str:
    """The lines of a logger program around `pattern`, redacted.

    Only the matched instruction is returned, never the file header: these programs are signed by
    their authors. Raises unless the pattern matches exactly `expect` times. Both directions
    matter: no match reads as 'the program does not measure this', and an over-broad pattern
    quietly prints the wrong instruction next to the argument it is supposed to support.
    """
    lines = Path(path).read_text(encoding='latin-1').splitlines()
    blocks = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if re.search(pattern, line):
            lo, hi = max(0, i - before), min(len(lines), i + after + 1)
            blocks.append('\n'.join(lines[lo:hi]))
    if len(blocks) != expect:
        raise ValueError(f"{Path(path).name}: {pattern!r} matched {len(blocks)} time(s), expected "
                         f"{expect}. The program layout has changed, the wrong file is configured, "
                         f"or the pattern is not specific enough.")
    return redact_people('\n\n'.join(blocks))


_ARITHMETIC = re.compile(r'^[0-9.\s()*/+-]+$')


def program_constants(path) -> dict:
    """Every `Const <name> = <expression>` declared in a CR1000 program, evaluated.

    The CR1000 program writes the PPFD multipliers as arithmetic on the calibration certificate
    (`1/5.65*1000` for 5.65 uV per umol m-2 s-1) and names the result in the measurement
    instruction, so the declarations must be parsed to obtain a number.

    Only digits, spaces, brackets and the four arithmetic operators are evaluated, so a program
    cannot make this cell run code. Raises if no constant is declared, rather than returning an
    empty dict that would make a later lookup fail less informatively.
    """
    text = Path(path).read_text(encoding='latin-1')
    out = {}
    for _name, _expr in re.findall(r'^\s*Const\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*([^\'\r\n]+)', text, re.M):
        _expr = _expr.strip()
        if not _ARITHMETIC.match(_expr):
            continue
        try:
            out[_name] = float(eval(_expr, {'__builtins__': {}}, {}))
        except (SyntaxError, ZeroDivisionError, TypeError):
            continue
    if not out:
        raise ValueError(f"{Path(path).name}: no numeric `Const` declaration found. This program "
                         f"language does not declare constants, or the layout has changed.")
    return out


def calibration_constants(excerpt: str, consts: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """The multiplier and offset of one measurement instruction, parsed from its own text.

    The CR10X lists both numbers as numbered parameters; the CR1000 passes them as the last two
    arguments of `VoltSe(...)` or `VoltDiff(...)`, possibly as the *name* of a declared constant,
    which `consts` resolves.

    Raises if either number is missing or a name cannot be resolved: an empty result would let the
    comparison below pass with nothing to disagree about.
    """
    if 'Mult' in excerpt:                                    # CR10X parameter listing
        _m = re.search(r'^\s*\d+:\s*([\d.]+)\s+Mult', excerpt, re.M)
        _o = re.search(r'^\s*\d+:\s*([\d.]+)\s+Offset', excerpt, re.M)
        tokens = [_m.group(1) if _m else None, _o.group(1) if _o else None]
    else:                                                    # CR1000 VoltSe/VoltDiff call
        _call = re.search(r'Volt(?:Se|Diff)\s*\(([^)]*)\)', excerpt)
        _args = [a.strip() for a in _call.group(1).split(',')] if _call else []
        tokens = _args[-2:] if len(_args) >= 2 else [None, None]

    values = []
    for _tok in tokens:
        if _tok is None:
            raise ValueError("could not parse a multiplier and an offset from the instruction - "
                             "the program language or the layout has changed")
        try:
            values.append(float(_tok))
        except ValueError:
            if not consts or _tok not in consts:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"the instruction gives its constant as the name {_tok!r}, which is not among "
                    f"the declarations passed in. Parse the program's `Const` block and pass it as "
                    f"`consts`, rather than reporting a constant this notebook cannot read.")
            values.append(consts[_tok])
    return {'multiplier': values[0], 'offset': values[1]}


# Negative controls: every failure path of the helpers is exercised before anything is read.
try:
    program_excerpt(PROGRAM_AFTER, r'ThisPatternIsNotInAnyLoggerProgram')
except ValueError as _exc:
    print(f"OK, program_excerpt raised on a pattern that does not occur: {_exc}")
else:
    raise AssertionError("(!) program_excerpt accepted a pattern that does not occur.")

# 'Ada Lovelace' is an invented name for this control. It writes no report, so the real one is
# not overwritten.
try:
    audit_unmapped_names(['12.05.2019 (Ada Lovelace) replaced the logger battery'],
                         'positive control', write_report=False)
except ValueError:
    print("OK, the unknown-name net fired on a name that is not in the map")
else:
    raise AssertionError("(!) the unknown-name net did not fire on an unmapped name.")

# The constant parser must refuse an instruction it cannot read at all ...
try:
    calibration_constants("18:  Volt (Diff) (P2) ;Messung von Kin\n 1: 1        Reps")
except ValueError as _exc:
    print(f"OK, calibration_constants raised on an instruction with no constants: {_exc}")
else:
    raise AssertionError("(!) calibration_constants accepted an instruction carrying no constants.")

# ... and one whose constant is a NAME it has no value for. This path is new relative to 01: the
# CR1000 names its PPFD multipliers, and a literal-only parser would miss or misread them.
try:
    calibration_constants("VoltDiff(PPFD_IN_T1_47_2,1,mV25,1,True,0,_50Hz,PPFD_IN_T1_47_2_mult,0)",
                          consts={})
except ValueError as _exc:
    print(f"OK, calibration_constants raised on an unresolved named constant: {_exc}")
else:
    raise AssertionError("(!) calibration_constants accepted a constant it could not resolve.")

# The declaration parser must refuse a program without declarations instead of returning an
# empty mapping.
try:
    program_constants(PROGRAMS_BF2[0])
except ValueError as _exc:
    print(f"OK, program_constants raised on a program that declares no constants: {_exc}")
else:
    raise AssertionError("(!) program_constants accepted a program with no `Const` declarations.")

# Radiation errors are multiplicative, so every comparison is a RATIO and every change a percentage.
# Three controls are built into the helper, because each could manufacture a change:
#   season: medians per calendar month, averaged over months, April-September only (snow, rime and
#     low-sun horizon differences read as response changes);
#   illumination: POTENTIAL radiation above WELL_LIT, which cannot drift, and both members above
#     MIN_IRRADIANCE (selecting on a measured series biases the ratio towards it);
#   sunniness: a ratio of two sensors is immune; a clear-sky index is not, and is not used here.
WELL_LIT = 300.0        # W m-2 of POTENTIAL radiation
MIN_IRRADIANCE = 50.0   # measured; W m-2 for the two shortwave series, umol m-2 s-1 for PPFD
SUMMER_MONTHS = [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9]
# The record covers April-September of its last year in full, so the partial year 2026 enters
# these yearly ratios like any other year. If PERIOD_END moves earlier, cap them at LAST_FULL_YEAR.
_season_end = (pd.Timestamp(pd.Timestamp(PERIOD_END).year, max(SUMMER_MONTHS), 1)
               + pd.offsets.MonthEnd(1) + pd.Timedelta(hours=23, minutes=45))
assert pd.Timestamp(PERIOD_END) >= _season_end, (
    f"the record ends at {PERIOD_END}, inside the April-September window of its last year, so that "
    f"year would enter the ratios with part of a season")

      f"{int(USABLE.sum()):,} of {len(rad):,}")


def ratio_by_year(num: str, den: str, min_records: int = 100) -> pd.Series:
    """Month-matched yearly median of `num`/`den` over usable half-hours.

    Monthly medians first, then the mean over calendar months, so a year short of one month is not
    compared against one that is not. Raises rather than returning a thin result: a ratio built
    from a handful of half-hours reads exactly like one built from a thousand.
    """
    _j = rad.loc[USABLE, [num, den]].dropna()
    _j = _j[(_j[num] > MIN_IRRADIANCE) & (_j[den] > MIN_IRRADIANCE)]
    if len(_j) < min_records * 12:
        raise ValueError(f"{num} / {den}: only {len(_j)} usable half-hours, too few to build "
                         f"monthly medians from")
    _r = _j[num] / _j[den]
    _m = _r.groupby([_r.index.year, _r.index.month]).median()
    _m.index.names = ['year', 'month']
    _n = _r.groupby([_r.index.year, _r.index.month]).count()
    _m = _m[_n >= min_records]
    if _m.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"{num} / {den}: no calendar month reaches {min_records} records")
    return _m.groupby(level=0).mean()


def step_at(series: pd.Series, year: int, span: int = 3) -> float:
    """Percentage change of a yearly ratio across `year`, over `span` years either side.

    The candidate year itself is excluded from both sides: a change inside a year belongs to
    neither era, and including it would halve the step it is meant to measure. Returns nan rather
    than a number when either side is thin, so a year at the edge of the record cannot win a scan
    by having almost no data behind it.
    """
    _pre = series.reindex(range(year - span, year)).dropna()
    _post = series.reindex(range(year + 1, year + 1 + span)).dropna()
    if len(_pre) < 2 or len(_post) < 2:
        return float('nan')
    return 100 * (_post.mean() / _pre.mean() - 1)


RATIOS = {f'{PPFD_47} / {SW_47}': ratio_by_year(PPFD_47, SW_47),
          f'{PPFD_47} / {MS_SW}': ratio_by_year(PPFD_47, MS_SW),
          f'{SW_47} / {MS_SW}': ratio_by_year(SW_47, MS_SW)}
PPFD_PAIRS = [_l for _l in RATIOS if _l.startswith(PPFD_47)]

SCREENING_YEAR = 2022   # the first year screened by diive; mst ends on 31 Dec 2021

# A three-year window straddling a drift reports the drift. Two comparisons separate a step from
# a drift, both against a year where nothing happened to this sensor rather than against zero:
#   neighbour test: the same three-year statistic at 2023. A step makes the boundary window the
#     larger; a drift makes the later one larger, because it accumulates.
#   adjacent-year test: the change from the last season before the boundary to the first after
#     it, and the same one year later. A step lands entirely in the first; a drift does not.
tabcap(f"the change across the {SCREENING_YEAR - 1}/{SCREENING_YEAR} screening boundary and the "
       f"same statistic one year later, where nothing happened to this sensor. The last column is "
       f"the ordinary year-to-year change over the rest of the record, for scale")

    _rel = 100 * (_s / _s.loc[BASELINE_YEARS[0]:BASELINE_YEARS[1]].mean() - 1)
    _adjacent = _rel.diff()
    _rows.append({

        f'the same at {SCREENING_YEAR + 1} (%)': step_at(_s, SCREENING_YEAR + 1),
        f'one-year change across the boundary (%)': _adjacent.get(SCREENING_YEAR, float('nan')),

_dev = fb[['Device Name', 'Device Model']].astype(str).agg(' '.join, axis=1)
DELTA_T = r'\bBF2\b|\bBF3\b'
_by_device = _dev.str.contains(DELTA_T + r'|PAR ?LITE', case=False, regex=True, na=False)
_by_text = fb['text'].str.contains(DELTA_T + r'|Kipp ?& ?Zonen par|PAR ?LITE', case=False,
                                   regex=True, na=False)

      f"({int(_by_device.sum())} by device column, {int(_by_text.sum())} by free text)")

def fragment(text, pattern=DELTA_T + r'|PAR ?LITE|Kipp ?& ?Zonen par', width=45) -> str:
    """The part of one entry that names a sensor, rather than its first 100 characters.

    Several of these entries are whole-day visit reports in which the sensor is named once,
    halfway through; truncating from the start shows the drive to the site instead.
    """
    _m = re.search(pattern, str(text), re.I)
    if not _m:
        return str(text)[:2 * width]
    _lo, _hi = max(0, _m.start() - width), min(len(str(text)), _m.end() + width)
    return ('...' if _lo else '') + str(text)[_lo:_hi] + ('...' if _hi < len(str(text)) else '')

PPFD_IN_T1_47_1 declines relative to both radiation references, by several per cent between the 2022 and 2024 seasons. The 2022 season is not yet below 2021, so the decline first appears in 2023; it is measured from the 2021 level. It has not continued since 2024: 2025 and 2026 stay within the ordinary one-year change of the 2024 level. The replacement of the tower box on 13 June 2023 does not explain it, since April and May 2023 already read low. This is a property of the exported product, not of the gap-filling.
RADIATION_SENSOR_CONTINUITY.ipynb attributes it with four sensors: the two ratios containing this sensor move, the ratio of the other two does not. This step reproduces the size of the decline on this notebook’s data and asserts it.
MeteoSwiss Lägern is another institution’s instrument 2.5 km away. The tower SW_IN shares the mast, logger and maintenance, but not the optics or calibration, where a response drift lives. A decline against both is a change at this sensor.

WarningKnown limitation of this product



PPFD_IN_T1_47_1 is exported as measured, without correcting the decline. The decline has no date at which to apply a correction, and no maintenance record names a cause, so a correction would be a rescaling towards a reference rather than the repair of a known fault.

A trend over the last years of the record, or across 2021, contains the sensor’s decline as well as any change in the light (size in the table above).
Comparisons within a year, and the relation of PPFD_IN to other radiation variables at a given time, are unaffected.
Gap-filled records inherit the sensor’s state at the time, because the model is trained on the surrounding measurements; they neither add nor remove the bias.

The likeliest cause, after more than twenty years in the field, is soiling or ageing of the diffuser and detectors. A calibration or replacement would settle it.




What this section settles
PPFD_IN_T1_47_1 is one instrument over the whole record: the Delta-T sunshine sensor, at 47 m since August 2004 and never replaced, read through the same conversion by both acquisition systems. It is homogeneous across the January 2016 changeover and the December 2021 splice, so no _HOMOGENIZED column is exported; the assertions above keep that claim true. The decline is real, on this sensor, uncorrected, and the first thing the variable’s documentation page states.

title: Download and prepare PPFD_IN (2004-2026.09)
text:
🟥 Gap-filling

Method
diive has no PPFD_IN gap-filling class, so this uses XGBoostTS with an explicit FeatureEngineer, as notebook 02 does for TA, with two radiation-specific settings:

below_zero='zero': negative predictions are clipped.
Nighttime gaps are set to zero after modelling and flagged 3, as SWINGapFillerXGBoost does in notebook 01; a modelled value at night would be noise around a known answer.

As in 02: no lag features (a lag of a gappy driver demotes records to the timestamp-only fallback), SW_IN_POT excluded from the rolling and EMA stages (it is deterministic), SHAP capped at 10,000 rows, and short daytime gaps interpolated and flagged 4.

SHAP_MAX_ROWS = 10_000


def short_gap_mask(missing: pd.Series, limit: int) -> pd.Series:
    """True where `missing` is set AND its whole run is at most `limit` records long.

    Takes a boolean gap mask rather than the series itself, so the caller can pass the
    mask from before the nighttime offset correction.
    """
    run_length = missing.groupby((~missing).cumsum()).transform('sum')
    return missing & (run_length <= limit)


def gapfill_ppfd(target: pd.Series,
                 drivers: pd.DataFrame,
                 swinpot: pd.Series,
                 original_gaps: pd.Series,
                 interpolate_limit: int = 2,
                 reduce_features: bool = True,
                 verbose: int = 1):
    """Gap-fill PPFD with XGBoost, force nighttime to zero, interpolate short daytime gaps.

    `original_gaps` must be the gap mask from BEFORE the nighttime offset correction:
    that correction zeroes every nighttime record including the missing ones, so
    `target.isna()` here would report no nighttime gaps at all and label them as measured.

    Returns (model, gapfilled, flag).
    """
    daytime = swinpot >= NIGHTTIME_THRESHOLD

    input_df = pd.concat([target, drivers], axis=1)
    engineer = dv.gapfilling.FeatureEngineer(
        target_col=target.name,
        features_lag=[],
        features_rolling=[4, 8, 24, 48],
        features_rolling_stats=['median'],
        features_rolling_exclude_cols=['SW_IN_POT'],
        features_ema=[6, 24],
        features_ema_exclude_cols=['SW_IN_POT'],
        vectorize_timestamps=True,
        add_continuous_record_number=True,
        verbose=0,
    )
    features_df = engineer.fit_transform(input_df)
    print(f"Features: {features_df.shape[1] - 1} over {len(features_df):,} records")

    model = dv.gapfilling.XGBoostTS(
        input_df=features_df, target_col=target.name, verbose=verbose,
        below_zero='zero',           # photon flux cannot be negative
        shap_max_rows=SHAP_MAX_ROWS,
        n_estimators=3000, max_depth=6, early_stopping_rounds=20,
        random_state=42, n_jobs=-1,
    )
    model.trainmodel(showplot_scores=False, showplot_importance=False)
    if reduce_features:
        model.reduce_features()
        model.trainmodel(showplot_scores=False, showplot_importance=False)
    model.fillgaps(showplot_scores=False, showplot_importance=False)

    gapfilled = model.results.gapfilled.copy()
    flag = model.results.flag.copy()

    # Physics beats the model at night: no incoming PAR after sunset.
    night_gaps = original_gaps & ~daytime
    gapfilled[night_gaps] = 0.0
    flag[night_gaps] = 3
    print(f"Nighttime gaps set to 0: {int(night_gaps.sum()):,}")

    # Short DAYTIME gaps only - a night is already handled above. The run-length search
    # uses the pre-correction mask for the same reason as above.
    if interpolate_limit:
        short = short_gap_mask(original_gaps, interpolate_limit) & daytime
        interp = target.interpolate(method='time', limit_area='inside')
        fill_locs = short & interp.notna()
        gapfilled[fill_locs] = interp[fill_locs]
        flag[fill_locs] = 4
        print(f"Short-gap interpolation: {int(fill_locs.sum())} records")

    gapfilled = gapfilled.rename(f"{target.name}_gfXG")
    flag = flag.rename(f"FLAG_{target.name}_ISFILLED")
    return model, gapfilled, flag



Run gap-filling

%%time

gf_ppfd, gapfilled_ppfd, flag_ppfd = gapfill_ppfd(
    target=ppfd_2004_2026[TARGET],
    drivers=drivers,
    swinpot=drivers['SW_IN_POT'],
    original_gaps=PPFD_ORIGINAL_GAPS,  # from BEFORE the offset correction, see there
)

title: Download and prepare PA (2005-2026.09)
text:
ℹ️ About this notebook
Downloads screened atmospheric pressure PA from InfluxDB, harmonises the units of the two sources, merges them, applies the 2012 corrections and writes the product to the external data folder. It also identifies the barometer from the logger programs, checks the absolute level against the barometric formula, and tests the two hardware boundaries in the record.
Differences from notebooks 01-03:

The sources are stored in different units (kPa, Pa) and are harmonised to kPa before anything else.
No gap-filling. The record is almost complete and is exported as measured.
The record starts 2005-09-02, when the archive begins. Nothing earlier is invented, so the index does not begin at 2004-01-01.

Output column: PA_T1_47_1, pressure in kPa, measured and corrected, gaps left as NaN. There is no FLAG_..._ISFILLED column: every non-null record is a measurement.






ImportantKnown limitation: a level step at the January 2016 acquisition change



The record before the tower logger replacement of January 2016 sits about 0.09 kPa above the record after it. The step is on the tower barometer, since the two references do not move against each other. Averaged over 2016 to 2025, the later era agrees with the barometric formula to within 0.03 kPa against both references. Year by year, its departure from the formula against Lägern grows from +0.017 kPa in 2016 to -0.061 kPa in 2025 and -0.074 kPa in January to September 2026. The formula is computed from Lägern’s own pressure, so it cannot say whether the tower or Lägern drifts.
The series is exported as measured, without a homogenised column: the step is one part in a thousand, and a second column would change this product and the merged one. To obtain one absolute level, lower the records before 2016-01-21 by the step. Comparisons within a year and air density for flux processing are not affected at this size.


InfluxIO needs influxdb-client, which uv sync installs through the diive[db] extra.

title: Download and prepare PA (2005-2026.09)
text:
📇 Data sources

PA_T1_47_1: exported variable, tower 1, 47 m. mst (2005-2021) and diive (2022-2026), not overlapping.
PA_NABEL_H1_2_1: hut barometer, 2 m, on the NABEL acquisition system, independent of the tower logger. Diagnostic only. Nominally to the end of 2018, but from July 2018 it repeats the tower series and is trimmed there.
PA_LAE_MS: MeteoSwiss Lägern station pressure (2.5 km, 845 m), 2004-2026, from REFPATH. Diagnostic only; it covers the years after NABEL stops. hPa, divided by 10. TA_LAE_MS and VP_LAE_MS from the same file feed the barometric formula.
PA_H1_0_1 (2017-2019, kPa) is not used: short, and it overlaps a period in which PA_T1_47_1 is essentially complete.
Logger programs: six CR10X programs (2004-2006) and the CR1000 program of January 2016. They name the barometer and its conversion, which the fieldbook does not.
GIN fieldbook: the site maintenance record, read and filtered in the notebook.

Screening: mst is ETH data screened with the deprecated MeteoscreeningTool; diive is ETH and NABEL data screened with diive. MeteoSwiss open data come from 10_REFERENCE.

title: Download and prepare PA (2005-2026.09)
section: ⚠️ The unit break, and why it is handled first
text:
⚠️ The unit break, and why it is handled first
meteoscreening_mst (2005-09-02 to 2021-12-31) stores PA_T1_47_1 in kPa, meteoscreening_diive (from 2022-01-01) in Pa: exactly a factor of 1000, with no overlap. The counts and medians are tabulated under Before harmonisation; the medians are not exactly 1000 apart only because they cover different years. Merged as stored, every statistic across the break would be meaningless and still look like a number.
The harmonisation therefore runs before the merge and ignores the calendar:

The unit is decided per source from the median. Surface pressure here (~690 m a.s.l.) is about 93 kPa = 930 hPa = 93,000 Pa, so the magnitude is unambiguous.
The verdict must match the database unit tag (kPa for mst, Pa for diive, hPa for NABEL), or the notebook raises.
The full converted range of every source must lie in the plausible band, or the notebook raises.

Output unit is kPa: the FLUXNET convention, the unit diive’s FLUXNET formatter documents (PA (kPa)), the one notebook x-99 declares for EddyPro’s Pa_1_1_1, and that of the 11_METEO6 product.

title: Download and prepare PA (2005-2026.09)
text:
⏱️ Timestamp convention
The database stores UTC TIMESTAMP_END. InfluxIO shifts it by TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS to local time, and TimestampSanitizer(output_middle_timestamp=True) converts it to TIMESTAMP_MID, which the rest of the notebook uses. START and STOP are local time.

# Captions. Copied as-is from notebook 03, whose figcap carries the PlaceHolderLayoutEngine fix.
def tabcap(text, width=100):
    """Print a table caption, above the table it belongs to."""
    print(textwrap.fill(f"Table - {text}", width) + "\n")


def figcap(fig, text, width=125):
    """Place a caption under a figure. Call after the last axes of that figure is drawn."""
    width = min(width, max(40, int(14.5 * fig.get_size_inches()[0])))
    caption = textwrap.fill(f"Figure - {text}", width)
    # An engine that still lays the figure out at draw time can make room for a caption itself.
    # plt.tight_layout() does NOT leave one: it executes once and leaves a PlaceHolderLayoutEngine
    # that never runs again, so a caption handed to supxlabel there lands on top of the tick
    # labels. Those figures take the manual branch below.
    _engine = fig.get_layout_engine()
    if _engine is not None and type(_engine).__name__ != 'PlaceHolderLayoutEngine':
        fig.supxlabel(caption, fontsize=9, ha='left', x=0.005)
        return
    lines = len(caption.splitlines())
    extra = 0.17 * lines + 0.12          # inches; one caption line is about 0.17 in at fontsize 9
    width_in, height_in = fig.get_size_inches()
    fig.set_size_inches(width_in, height_in + extra)
    keep = height_in / (height_in + extra)
    offset = extra / (height_in + extra)
    for ax in fig.axes:
        pos = ax.get_position()
        ax.set_position([pos.x0, offset + pos.y0 * keep, pos.width, pos.height * keep])
    fig.text(0.005, 0.01, caption, fontsize=9, ha='left', va='bottom')



🧭 Unit harmonisation helper
harmonise_to_kpa() converts only what it can identify with certainty and never looks at the date. PA_PLAUSIBLE_KPA (85-100 kPa) is deliberately wide: recorded extremes here are 89.4-95.5 kPa, and the band only has to separate kPa, hPa and Pa.

# Plausible surface pressure at CH-LAE (~690 m a.s.l.). Wide enough to accept any real weather,
# far too narrow to accept a value that is off by a factor of 10 or 1000.
PA_PLAUSIBLE_KPA = (85.0, 100.0)

UNIT_FACTORS_TO_KPA = {'kPa': 1.0, 'hPa': 0.1, 'Pa': 0.001}


def harmonise_to_kpa(series: pd.Series, source: str, declared_unit: str | None = None) -> pd.Series:
    """Convert a pressure series to kPa, identifying its unit from the data itself.

    The unit is decided by magnitude, NOT by date: the median is multiplied by each candidate
    factor and exactly one result must land inside `PA_PLAUSIBLE_KPA`. `declared_unit` is the
    unit tag stored alongside the series in the database; when given it must agree with the
    magnitude verdict.

    Raises ValueError if the unit is ambiguous, if the declared and detected units disagree, or
    if any converted value falls outside the plausible band. Silently returning a series that is
    off by a factor of 1000 is the one outcome that must never happen.
    """
    s = series.dropna()
    if s.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"{source}: no data, cannot determine unit.")

    lo, hi = PA_PLAUSIBLE_KPA
    median = float(s.median())
    matches = [u for u, f in UNIT_FACTORS_TO_KPA.items() if lo <= median * f <= hi]
    if len(matches) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{source}: median {median:,.2f} is consistent with {matches or 'no'} unit(s), "
            f"expected exactly one. Surface pressure here is ~93 kPa / ~930 hPa / ~93,000 Pa.")
    detected = matches[0]

    if declared_unit is not None and declared_unit != detected:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{source}: the database declares '{declared_unit}' but the magnitude says "
            f"'{detected}' (median {median:,.2f}). Refusing to guess - check the source.")

    factor = UNIT_FACTORS_TO_KPA[detected]
    out = series * factor

    converted = out.dropna()
    if not (lo <= converted.min() and converted.max() <= hi):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{source}: after converting {detected} -> kPa the range is "
            f"{converted.min():.2f}..{converted.max():.2f} kPa, outside the plausible "
            f"{lo}..{hi} kPa. Not exporting this.")

    print(f"  {source:<26} {detected:>3} -> kPa (x{factor:g})   n={len(converted):>7,}   "
          f"median {float(converted.median()):7.3f}   "
          f"range {converted.min():.2f}..{converted.max():.2f}")
    return out

The NABEL reference stops being independent
From July 2018 the values stored under PA_NABEL_H1_2_1 reproduce PA_T1_47_1 to the fifth decimal, which two barometers 45 m apart never do: the NABEL barometer had stopped and its slot was back-filled with the tower series. A copied reference makes every comparison circular while looking like perfect agreement. The test is a run of consecutive records agreeing to better than 0.0001 kPa; the reference is cut where the first run begins. MeteoSwiss Lägern covers the years after.

def independent_until(target: pd.Series, reference: pd.Series, tol: float = 1e-4,
                      min_run: int = 48) -> pd.Timestamp | None:
    """The first timestamp from which `reference` merely repeats `target`, or None.

    Two barometers separated by 45 m of air agree to a few hundredths of a kPa and never to five
    decimal places, so a run of `min_run` consecutive records inside `tol` is not agreement, it is
    the same numbers twice. Returns None when no such run exists, which is the answer for a
    reference that is doing its job.
    """
    both = pd.concat([target.rename('t'), reference.rename('r')], axis=1, sort=False).dropna()
    if both.empty:
        raise ValueError("target and reference never overlap - there is nothing to test.")
    same = (both['t'] - both['r']).abs() < tol
    run = same.groupby((~same).cumsum()).transform('sum').where(same, 0)
    return both.index[run >= min_run][0] if (run >= min_run).any() else None

The reference series, and why they make these diagnostics possible
Neither reference is on the tower logger, which is what judging a tower-logger fault requires. PA_NABEL_H1_2_1 (hut, 2 m) runs from 2005 to mid-2018 and covers the 2012 faults. The tower barometer, 45 m higher, reads a near-constant amount lower; adding that offset, computed here and checked against the barometric formula later, turns NABEL into a predicted tower pressure. Undisturbed, the residual is a few hundredths of a kPa. After 2018, MeteoSwiss Lägern is the second reference.

Timestamp shift in August 2012
Info from fieldbook entry 17 Aug 2012: > adjusted the logger date and time. On Servertime (Computer System Time) 17.08.2012 12:31.42 the loggertime was 16.08.2012 08:06:00. Synchronized time at 17.08.2012 11:40:00 servertime. The logger data aquisition on the moxa embedded was restarted

ImportantWhy the lag diagnostic works for pressure



Pressure has almost no diurnal cycle (the semidiurnal tide is ~1-2 hPa against synoptic swings of tens of hPa). The lag search works on the synoptic signal instead: pressure wanders by 1-3 kPa over a few days, so a 15.5 h shift against an independent barometer leaves a large residual. Without PA_NABEL_H1_2_1, which is not on the faulty logger, the test would be underpowered.

_rows = []
for _day in pd.date_range('2012-08-09', '2012-08-18', freq='D'):
    _d = _day.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')

    def _rmse(series):
        _x, _y = series.loc[_d], reference.loc[_d]
        _ok = _x.notna() & _y.notna()
        return float(np.sqrt(((_x[_ok] - _y[_ok]) ** 2).mean())) if _ok.sum() >= 12 else np.nan

    _rows.append((_d, _rmse(_before), _rmse(_df[TARGET])))

_check = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=['date', 'RMSE_before_kPa', 'RMSE_after_kPa']).set_index('date')
_check['improvement'] = (_check.RMSE_before_kPa - _check.RMSE_after_kPa).round(3)

       "so an 'after' value near that means the correction landed")
display(_check.round(3))
print("Undisturbed agreement is about 0.04 kPa, so 'after' values near 0.05 kPa mean the "
      "correction landed.")

NoteNo zero-offset correction here



01 and 03 remove a nighttime zero-offset because radiation is known to be zero at night. Pressure has no such reference value, so no equivalent step is applied. Notebook 03’s trap, a correction writing into gaps and relabelling fills as measurements, cannot occur here: the clock shift moves records and the 2012 windows only set NaN.





🌍 MeteoSwiss Lägern: an independent check across the whole record
Lägern (2.5 km, 845 m) covers the years after NABEL stops in 2018. With a constant altitude offset removed, tower and Lägern correlate at ~0.99. Lägern (hPa, divided by 10) sits about 110 m above the tower barometer and reads lower; the offset is fitted from the overlap (mean of tower - Lägern) and added to Lägern. Diagnostic only. Two checks follow: the alignment guard of 01-03, which proves the TIMESTAMP_END -> TIMESTAMP_MID conversion, and the residual before and after 2018, where a shift or fault missed after NABEL ended would show.

# Pressure, and also the temperature and vapour pressure of the air column, which the
# barometric check below needs. All three come from the same station and the same file.
_lae = pd.read_parquet(REFPATH)[[REFCOL, REFCOL_TA, REFCOL_VP]].copy()
_lae.index = _lae.index - pd.Timedelta(minutes=15)  # TIMESTAMP_END -> TIMESTAMP_MID
_lae.index.name = pa_2005_2026.index.name
_lae = _lae.reindex(pa_2005_2026.index)
pa_lae = _lae[REFCOL] / 10.0   # hPa -> kPa, onto the product index
ta_lae = _lae[REFCOL_TA]       # deg C
vp_lae = _lae[REFCOL_VP]       # hPa

# Hydrostatic offset, fitted from the overlap rather than guessed: Laegern (845 m) reads lower than
# the tower barometer (~690 m). Add it to Laegern so both sit on the tower's pressure level.
_both = pd.concat([pa_2005_2026[TARGET].rename('tower'), pa_lae.rename('lae')],
                  axis=1, sort=False).dropna()
LAE_OFFSET = float((_both['tower'] - _both['lae']).mean())
lae_adjusted = pa_lae + LAE_OFFSET
print(f"fitted tower - Laegern offset: {LAE_OFFSET:+.4f} kPa "
      f"(mean over {len(_both):,} overlapping records; Laegern reads lower, sitting higher)")

# Alignment guard (as in notebooks 01-03): correlate the measured tower PA against Laegern-adjusted
# at -1/0/+1 half-hour offsets. Offset 0 must win, which proves the TIMESTAMP_MID conversion.
# Pressure is spatially coherent, so the correlation is ~0.99 and the zero-lag peak is clear.
_meas = pa_2005_2026[TARGET]
_scores = {}
for _off in (-1, 0, 1):
    _j = pd.concat([_meas.rename('t'), lae_adjusted.shift(_off).rename('r')],
                   axis=1, sort=False).dropna()
    _scores[_off] = _j['t'].corr(_j['r'])
    print(f"  offset {_off:+d} x 30min: corr {_scores[_off]:.5f}")
assert max(_scores, key=_scores.get) == 0, f"reference is mis-aligned: {_scores}"
print("OK: offset 0 wins, the TIMESTAMP_MID conversion is correct.")

_res_lae = (pa_2005_2026[TARGET] - lae_adjusted)

title: Download and prepare PA (2005-2026.09)
section: 🔎 Which sensor this is, and what the hardware changes did to it
text:
🔎 Which sensor this is, and what the hardware changes did to it
PA_T1_47_1 names a variable, not an instrument. This section asks which hardware stands behind it, what the two boundaries in the record did to it, and whether its absolute level is right, which for pressure can be checked against physics. It establishes:

one barometer and one conversion: a Vaisala PTB101B at multiplier 0.184 and offset 600 in all seven surviving logger programs;
the record begins long after the last change to this channel;
the absolute level agrees with the barometric formula, without a fitted parameter, to within a few hundredths of a kPa, including the seasonal shape of the difference;
three barometers give three pairwise differences, whose pattern names the instrument that moved;
the tower barometer steps at the January 2016 acquisition change, by about 0.09 kPa;
nothing steps at the December 2021 screening splice;
the maintenance record has never named this barometer in twenty-one years.


Helpers for this section
The logger programs and the fieldbook are read, not quoted, so a re-run re-derives the argument. Both name people, so every string taken from them is redacted as in 01, 02, 03 and 08.

# --- Fieldbook and logger-program redaction ----------------------------------------------------
# The GIN export and the logger programs both name people and this page is public, so every
# string taken from either passes through redact_people() where it is flattened. Same map and rules
# as notebooks 01, 02, 03 and 08; the map lives beside the export, outside this repository.
REDACT_MAP = Path(FIELDBOOK).with_name('redact_names.csv')
ALLOW_LIST = Path(FIELDBOOK).with_name('redact_allow.csv')


def unmapped_report_path(label: str) -> Path:
    """Where the unmapped-name candidates of one audit are written.

    Per label, because this notebook audits two sources: a single shared file would let the
    second audit overwrite the first one's findings.
    """
    _slug = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', label.lower()).strip('_')
    return Path(FIELDBOOK).with_name(f'redact_unmapped_{_slug}.txt')


def load_redactions(path=None) -> dict:
    """Load the name -> pseudonym map.

    Raises if the map is missing. That is the point: carrying on with redaction quietly disabled
    prints real names into a published page and looks exactly like success.
    """
    path = REDACT_MAP if path is None else Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"the redaction map is missing: {path}. Without it the names these files record would "
            f"print unredacted. Restore the file rather than skipping this.")
    tab = pd.read_csv(path, encoding='utf-8')
    missing = {'name', 'pseudonym'}.difference(tab.columns)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: missing column(s) {sorted(missing)}.")
    pairs = {str(n).strip(): str(p).strip()
             for n, p in zip(tab['name'], tab['pseudonym']) if str(n).strip()}
    if not pairs:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: holds no usable name -> pseudonym pairs.")
    return pairs


REDACTIONS = load_redactions()
# Longest surface form first, so a bare surname cannot corrupt a double-barrelled one that starts
# with it. Lookarounds rather than \b, because some forms end in an initial.
_REDACT_RX = re.compile(r'(?<!\w)(' + '|'.join(re.escape(n) for n in
                                               sorted(REDACTIONS, key=len, reverse=True))
                        + r')(?!\w)')


def redact_people(s) -> str:
    """Replace every mapped name with its stable pseudonym."""
    return _REDACT_RX.sub(lambda m: REDACTIONS[m.group(1)], str(s))


def strip_html(text) -> str:
    """Flatten one GIN fieldbook entry to plain text, with the people it names redacted."""
    flat = html.unescape(re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', str(text)))
    return redact_people(re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', flat).strip())


_NAME_TOKEN = r"[A-ZÄÖÜ][\wÄÖÜäöüß'-]{1,20}"
_NAME_UNIT = _NAME_TOKEN + r'(?:\s+' + _NAME_TOKEN + r'){0,2}'
_NAME_SHAPES = (
    re.compile(r'\((' + _NAME_UNIT + r'(?:\s*[,+&]\s*' + _NAME_UNIT + r')*)\s*'
               r'(?:\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}\.\d{4})?\)'),
    re.compile(r'(?:with|by|durch|von|gemaess)\s+(' + _NAME_TOKEN + r'(?:\s+' + _NAME_TOKEN + r')?)'),
)


def audit_unmapped_names(texts, label='fieldbook', write_report: bool = True) -> int:
    """Raise if any name-shaped token survived redaction.

    A newer export can name someone the map has never seen. Candidates are never printed - an
    exception message is stored in a notebook like any other output - so they go to a file beside
    the map and only the count is shown.
    """
    allow = set(pd.read_csv(ALLOW_LIST, encoding='utf-8')['term'].astype(str).str.strip())
    found = {}
    for _t in texts:
        for _rx in _NAME_SHAPES:
            for _m in _rx.finditer(str(_t)):
                for _tok in re.findall(_NAME_TOKEN, _m.group(1)):
                    if _tok.isupper() or any(ch.isdigit() for ch in _tok) or _tok in allow:
                        continue
                    found[_tok] = found.get(_tok, 0) + 1
    if found:
        _report = unmapped_report_path(label)
        if write_report:
            _report.write_text(
                '\n'.join(f'{n}\t{t}' for t, n in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])),
                encoding='utf-8')
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label}: {len(found)} name-shaped token(s) survived redaction. They are deliberately "
            f"NOT shown here - see {_report}. Add the people to redact_names.csv and the "
            f"technical terms to redact_allow.csv, then re-run.")
    print(f"  {label}: no unmapped name-shaped tokens ({len(allow)} allowlisted terms)")
    return 0


def program_excerpt(path, pattern: str, before: int = 6, after: int = 4, expect: int = 1) -> str:
    """The lines of a logger program around `pattern`, redacted.

    Only the matched instruction is returned, never the file header: these programs are signed by
    their authors. Raises unless the pattern matches exactly `expect` times. Both directions
    matter: no match reads as 'the program does not measure this', and an over-broad pattern
    quietly prints the wrong instruction next to the argument it is supposed to support.
    """
    lines = Path(path).read_text(encoding='latin-1').splitlines()
    blocks = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if re.search(pattern, line):
            lo, hi = max(0, i - before), min(len(lines), i + after + 1)
            blocks.append('\n'.join(lines[lo:hi]))
    if len(blocks) != expect:
        raise ValueError(f"{Path(path).name}: {pattern!r} matched {len(blocks)} time(s), expected "
                         f"{expect}. The program layout has changed, the wrong file is configured, "
                         f"or the pattern is not specific enough.")
    return redact_people('\n\n'.join(blocks))


def uncommented(excerpt: str) -> str:
    """Drop the comment part of every line of a logger-program excerpt.

    Notebook 03 did not need this and this notebook does. Both program languages keep dead code in
    comments, and the CR1000 keeps some here: two lines above the live pressure instruction sits a
    commented-out single-ended version of it, carrying a DIFFERENT multiplier. A parser reading the
    raw excerpt finds that one first and reports constants the logger has never applied. CR10X
    comments begin with `;`, CRBasic comments with `'`.
    """
    out = []
    for line in excerpt.splitlines():
        stripped = re.split(r"[;']", line, maxsplit=1)[0].rstrip()
        if stripped.strip():
            out.append(stripped)
    return '\n'.join(out)


def calibration_constants(excerpt: str, consts: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """The multiplier and offset of one measurement instruction, parsed from its own text.

    Two shapes occur across the two program languages and both are matched on their own terms: the
    CR10X lists the two numbers as numbered parameters, while the CR1000 passes them as the last
    two arguments of a `VoltSe(...)` or `VoltDiff(...)` call. Copied from notebook 03, including
    the `consts` path, which this variable does not use - the CR1000 writes its pressure constants
    as literals.

    Raises if either number cannot be found. A silently empty result would make the comparison
    below pass by having nothing to disagree about.
    """
    if 'Mult' in excerpt:                                    # CR10X parameter listing
        _m = re.search(r'^\s*\d+:\s*([\d.]+)\s+Mult', excerpt, re.M)
        _o = re.search(r'^\s*\d+:\s*([\d.]+)\s+Offset', excerpt, re.M)
        tokens = [_m.group(1) if _m else None, _o.group(1) if _o else None]
    else:                                                    # CR1000 VoltSe/VoltDiff call
        _call = re.search(r'Volt(?:Se|Diff)\s*\(([^)]*)\)', excerpt)
        _args = [a.strip() for a in _call.group(1).split(',')] if _call else []
        tokens = _args[-2:] if len(_args) >= 2 else [None, None]

    values = []
    for _tok in tokens:
        if _tok is None:
            raise ValueError("could not parse a multiplier and an offset from the instruction - "
                             "the program language or the layout has changed")
        try:
            values.append(float(_tok))
        except ValueError:
            if not consts or _tok not in consts:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"the instruction gives its constant as the name {_tok!r}, which is not among "
                    f"the declarations passed in.")
            values.append(consts[_tok])
    return {'multiplier': values[0], 'offset': values[1]}

3️⃣ The absolute level, against the barometric formula
Pressure falls with height by a law with no free parameter, so a barometer’s elevation can be read back from its readings: an absolute test that a unit or offset error fails by orders of magnitude. The scale height uses the virtual temperature of the column (humid air is lighter; ignoring this overstates the predicted difference) from Lägern’s temperature and vapour pressure, with the layer mean half a lapse rate below the station. The test covers the level and the seasonal shape of the difference, which follows temperature; a formula right about the mean by accident will not also match the cycle.

📋 Table: barometer elevation from the barometric formula

# Constants of the hypsometric equation. None of them is fitted.
G_ACCEL = 9.80665     # m s-2
R_DRY = 287.05        # J kg-1 K-1, specific gas constant of dry air
LAPSE_RATE = 0.0065   # K m-1, standard atmosphere; used only to put the layer mean temperature
                      # between the two sensors rather than at the upper one
NOMINAL_ELEVATION = SITE_BASE_ELEVATION + SENSOR_HEIGHT
KPA_PER_METRE = 93.3 / (R_DRY * 283.0 / G_ACCEL)   # for reporting a pressure as metres of air


def scale_height(t_degc, vp_hpa, p_kpa, dz):
    """Scale height R*Tv/g of the layer, from the reference station's own temperature and humidity."""
    t_layer = t_degc + 273.15 + LAPSE_RATE * dz / 2
    return R_DRY * (t_layer / (1 - 0.378 * vp_hpa / (p_kpa * 10))) / G_ACCEL


def predicted_pressure(p_ref_kpa, t_ref_degc, vp_ref_hpa, dz):
    """Pressure `dz` metres below a station, from that station's own pressure, temperature and humidity."""
    return p_ref_kpa * np.exp(dz / scale_height(t_ref_degc, vp_ref_hpa, p_ref_kpa, dz))


def implied_elevation(here: pd.Series, there: pd.Series, elevation_there: float,
                      t_there: pd.Series, vp_there: pd.Series,
                      min_records: int = 10_000) -> dict:
    """Where the hypsometric equation puts `here`'s barometer, given a station of known elevation.

    Raises if either series is not plausible surface pressure in kPa, or if too few records
    overlap. The unit guard is the point of the helper as much as the answer is: run on a series
    still stored in Pa this has to stop, not return a number.
    """
    both = pd.concat([here.rename('p'), there.rename('pref'), t_there.rename('t'),
                      vp_there.rename('e')], axis=1, sort=False).dropna()
    if len(both) < min_records:
        raise ValueError(f"only {len(both):,} overlapping records, too few for a level check "
                         f"(at least {min_records:,} are wanted).")
    _lo, _hi = PA_PLAUSIBLE_KPA
    for _name, _s in (('the series under test', both['p']), ('the reference', both['pref'])):
        if not (_lo <= float(_s.mean()) <= _hi):
            raise ValueError(f"{_name} has mean {float(_s.mean()):,.2f}, which is not surface "
                             f"pressure in kPa ({_lo}-{_hi}). Convert before comparing levels.")
    _p, _pref = float(both['p'].mean()), float(both['pref'].mean())
    _dz = 0.0
    for _ in range(3):   # the layer mean temperature depends on dz, which depends on it
        _h = scale_height(float(both['t'].mean()), float(both['e'].mean()), _pref, _dz)
        _dz = -_h * np.log(_p / _pref)
    return {'n': len(both), 'measured difference (kPa)': _p - _pref,
            'scale height (m)': _h, 'implied elevation (m)': elevation_there + _dz}

4️⃣ Three barometers, and the pattern that names the one that moved
Each barometer appears in two of the three pairwise differences, so a change at one moves exactly its own two and leaves the third alone (the argument of notebook 02 and RADIATION_SENSOR_CONTINUITY.ipynb). Pressure errors are additive: differences, not ratios.
The differences carry a physical seasonal cycle of about 0.09 kPa (step 3️⃣), so monthly medians are averaged over calendar months and a year missing a month is dropped. This drops 2026, which ends in September; the yearly statistics stop at LAST_FULL_YEAR. Changes are read year on year, against what the same instruments do in an ordinary year.

📋 Table: pairwise differences by year

TOWER, HUT, LAEGERN = 'tower 47 m', 'NABEL hut 2 m', 'MeteoSwiss Lägern'
BAROMETERS = {TOWER: pa_2005_2026[TARGET], HUT: pa_2005_2026[REFERENCE], LAEGERN: pa_lae}
PAIRS = [(TOWER, LAEGERN), (TOWER, HUT), (HUT, LAEGERN)]


def difference_by_year(a: str, b: str, min_records: int = 200) -> pd.Series:
    """Month-matched yearly mean of `a` - `b`, in kPa.

    Monthly medians first, then the mean over calendar months; a year not covering all twelve is
    dropped rather than compared against one that does, and nothing after LAST_FULL_YEAR enters.
    Raises rather than returning a thin
    result: a difference built from a handful of half-hours reads exactly like one built from
    thousands.
    """
    _d = (BAROMETERS[a] - BAROMETERS[b]).dropna()
    _m = _d.groupby([_d.index.year, _d.index.month]).median()
    _m.index.names = ['year', 'month']
    _m = _m[_d.groupby([_d.index.year, _d.index.month]).count() >= min_records]
    if _m.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"{a} - {b}: no calendar month reaches {min_records} records")
    _months = _m.groupby(level=0).count()
    # The twelve-month rule already drops the partial 2026; the cut at LAST_FULL_YEAR states it.
    return _m.groupby(level=0).mean()[_months == 12].loc[:LAST_FULL_YEAR]


DIFFS = {_pair: difference_by_year(*_pair) for _pair in PAIRS}

diff_table.index.name = 'YEAR'

             and _y - 1 in diff_table.index and diff_table.loc[_y - 1].notna().all()]

      f"{DECIDABLE[0]}-{DECIDABLE[-1]}")


def moved(changes: dict, threshold: float):
    """Which barometer a set of pairwise changes identifies, or None.

    Returns None when the pattern does not identify one - two instruments moving at once looks
    exactly like a row with several large entries, and a rule that guessed in that case would be
    worse than no rule. A difference says two barometers separated, never which of them left.
    """
    _big = {_p for _p, _v in changes.items() if pd.notna(_v) and abs(_v) >= threshold}
    if not _big:
        return None
    for _b in BAROMETERS:
        _own = {_p for _p in changes if _b in _p}
        if _big == _own:
            return _b
    return None

The scan finds three events, one at this tower:

2011: both differences containing MeteoSwiss move and the site pair does not. That is Lägern’s instrumentation rebuild of 6 October 2010, dated in the radiation notebooks, so tower-minus-Lägern is no evidence about the tower across that date.
2016: both differences containing the tower move by the same amount and the reference pair does not. That is the tower barometer (step 5️⃣).
2017: both differences containing the hut barometer move, in that instrument’s last years before it stopped in July 2018.

Otherwise the differences hold to a few hundredths of a kPa for two decades.



5️⃣ The January 2016 acquisition change: the tower barometer steps
The record before the changeover sits about 0.09 kPa above the record after it. Both references see the same step to within a thousandth of a kPa and do not move against each other.
Three independent files fix the date: a three-week outage ending 21 January 2016 brackets the step and limits its dating to that gap, the logger program on disk is the version of 18 January 2016, and the fieldbook (step 7️⃣) names that file. Against the barometric formula (step 3️⃣) the later era agrees and the earlier does not, for both references. The later era is evaluated to LAST_FULL_YEAR, so the partial 2026 does not weight its months unevenly.
That agreement is an era mean. Against Lägern the yearly departure from the formula moves from +0.017 kPa in 2016 to -0.061 kPa in 2025, and the tower-minus-Lägern difference for January to September 2026 sits 0.023 kPa below the same months of 2025: the largest year-on-year change since 2016, below EVENT_THRESHOLD (0.04 kPa) and above the typical year-to-year change of 0.014 kPa. The formula is computed from Lägern’s own pressure, so it cannot say whether the tower or Lägern drifts. This is the residual drift quantified below.

# The step at a resolution that separates it from a drift. Two things are removed first: the
# 1.7 kPa between the two differences, on which 0.09 kPa is a line thickness, and the annual wave
# of step 3, about as large as the step. Subtracting each pair's own monthly climatology over the
# three years before the changeover does both; the pre-change era then sits at zero by
# construction.
_CLIM_YEARS = slice(f'{BREAK_YEAR - 3}', f'{BREAK_YEAR - 1}')


def seasonal_anomaly(ref: str) -> pd.Series:
    """Tower minus `ref`, with that pair's own pre-change monthly climatology removed."""
    _full = pa_2005_2026[TARGET] - BAROMETERS[ref]
    _clim = _full.loc[_CLIM_YEARS].groupby(_full.loc[_CLIM_YEARS].index.month).median()
    return _full - _full.index.month.map(_clim)

ImportantWhy the step is reported and not corrected



The step is real, dated and attributed, and a correction would be defensible. It is not applied, for three reasons in order of weight:

Size. One part in a thousand of the value, under ten metres of air. Air density, and the fluxes computed from it, change by the same fraction.
Cost. Homogenising means a second, rescaled column and a SOURCE flag, as in 02, 08 and 09. That changes this product and the merged product, a decision about the dataset rather than this variable.
Remainder. The residual drift is of the same order, has no date at which to correct it, and after 2018 cannot be attributed. Homogenising would remove the step and leave the drift.

For one absolute level across the record, lower the records before ACQUISITION_CHANGE by the size of the step printed above; keep the later era.





6️⃣ No step at the December 2021 screening splice
meteoscreening_mst ends on 31 December 2021 and meteoscreening_diive begins the next day, without overlap. This is a screening boundary: no fieldbook work on this sensor, no program change. With the hut barometer gone, only the difference against MeteoSwiss is available, so the pattern rule cannot be applied. The change across the splice is smaller than the median year-to-year change, and the three-year statistic lies between its neighbours’ values: slow drift, not a splice.

📋 Table: change across the 2021/2022 screening splice

SCREENING_YEAR = 2022   # the first year screened by diive; mst ends on 31 Dec 2021
_ms_label = f'{TOWER} - {LAEGERN}'
_ms = diff_table[_ms_label]


def step_at(series: pd.Series, year: int, span: int = 3) -> float:
    """Change of a yearly difference across `year`, over `span` years either side, in kPa.

    The candidate year itself is excluded from both sides. Returns nan rather than a number when
    either side is thin, so a year at the edge of the record cannot win a comparison by having
    almost no data behind it.
    """
    _pre = series.reindex(range(year - span, year)).dropna()
    _post = series.reindex(range(year + 1, year + 1 + span)).dropna()
    if len(_pre) < 2 or len(_post) < 2:
        return float('nan')
    return float(_post.mean() - _pre.mean())


assert np.isnan(step_at(_ms, 1990)), "(!) step_at returned a number for a year off the record"
assert np.isnan(step_at(_ms, int(_ms.index.max()))), \
    "(!) step_at returned a number for the last year of the record"

_adjacent = _ms.diff()
_quiet_adjacent = _adjacent.drop(index=[_y for _y in (2011, 2016, 2017, SCREENING_YEAR)
                                        if _y in _adjacent.index]).abs()
tabcap(f"the tower-minus-Lägern difference at the {SCREENING_YEAR - 1}/{SCREENING_YEAR} screening "
       f"boundary and in the years around it. A step lands entirely in the one-year change; the "
       f"three-year change is dominated by the slow drift of this difference and is shown so the "
       f"two are not confused")
splice_table = pd.DataFrame({
    'one-year change (kPa)': {_y: _adjacent.get(_y, float('nan'))
                              for _y in range(SCREENING_YEAR - 2, SCREENING_YEAR + 3)},
    'three-year change (kPa)': {_y: step_at(_ms, _y)
                                for _y in range(SCREENING_YEAR - 2, SCREENING_YEAR + 3)},
})
splice_table.index.name = 'YEAR'
display(splice_table.round(4))

_here = float(_adjacent.loc[SCREENING_YEAR])
_typical_adj = float(_quiet_adjacent.median())
print(f"\nchange across the splice:            {_here:+.4f} kPa "
      f"({_here / KPA_PER_METRE:+.1f} m of air)")
print(f"median change in an ordinary year:   {_typical_adj:.4f} kPa")
print(f"change across the 2016 hardware date: {change.loc[BREAK_YEAR, _ms_label]:+.4f} kPa")
assert abs(_here) < EVENT_THRESHOLD, (
    f"the tower-Laegern difference now moves by {_here:+.4f} kPa across the screening splice, past "
    f"the {EVENT_THRESHOLD} kPa an event is counted at - the mst/diive splice can no longer be "
    f"reported as clean")
assert abs(_here) < _typical_adj, (
    "the change across the screening splice is no longer smaller than what this difference does in "
    "an ordinary year, which is the statement this step makes")
_neighbours = [step_at(_ms, _y) for _y in (SCREENING_YEAR - 1, SCREENING_YEAR + 1)]
assert min(_neighbours) <= step_at(_ms, SCREENING_YEAR) <= max(_neighbours), (
    "the three-year change at the splice is no longer between the values of its own neighbours, so "
    "it is no longer just the slow drift passing through")

      "two screenings of this measurement can be joined.")

7️⃣ What the maintenance record holds for this barometer
Two questions: what the fieldbook says about the barometer, and about the January 2016 changeover. The barometer search returns one free-text entry, of 3 January 2023, which matches only on the word “Vaisala” and concerns the PWD12 present-weather sensor. It is a false positive.

# The maintenance record, read and filtered here rather than quoted, so a newer export
# re-derives this instead of leaving a stale copy in the prose.
fb = pd.read_csv(FIELDBOOK)
fb['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(fb['Date'], format='%d.%m.%Y', errors='coerce')
fb['text'] = fb['Text'].apply(strip_html)
audit_unmapped_names(fb['text'], 'fieldbook entries')
print(f"fieldbook: {len(fb):,} entries, {fb['Date'].min().date()} -> {fb['Date'].max().date()}")
_dev = fb[['Device Name', 'Device Model']].astype(str).agg(' '.join, axis=1)

# Question 1: does this barometer appear at all? Device columns AND free text, because the entries
# that explain a fault are routinely filed under something else.
BAROMETER = r'PTB\s*-?\s*101|barometer|barometric|Vaisala|Luftdruck'
_by_device = _dev.str.contains(BAROMETER, case=False, regex=True, na=False)
_by_text = fb['text'].str.contains(BAROMETER, case=False, regex=True, na=False)
print(f"\nentries naming a barometer: {int(_by_device.sum())} by device column, "
      f"{int(_by_text.sum())} by free text")


def fragment(text, pattern, width=40) -> str:
    """The part of one entry that matches, rather than its first hundred characters.

    Several of these entries are whole-day visit reports in which the matching word appears once,
    halfway through; truncating from the start shows the drive to the site instead.
    """
    _m = re.search(pattern, str(text), re.I)
    if not _m:
        return str(text)[:2 * width]
    _lo, _hi = max(0, _m.start() - width), min(len(str(text)), _m.end() + width)
    return ('...' if _lo else '') + str(text)[_lo:_hi] + ('...' if _hi < len(str(text)) else '')


for _, _r in fb[_by_device | _by_text].sort_values('Date').iterrows():
    print(f"  {_r['Date'].date()} [{_r['Device Model']}] {fragment(_r['text'], BAROMETER)}")

    "a barometer now appears in the device inventory, so the statement that this instrument is "
    "absent from the maintenance record is out of date")

# The word 'pressure' on its own is about something else here, and saying so is part of the
# answer: a filter that counted those would report maintenance on a sensor that has had none.
_pressure = fb['text'].str.contains(r'\bpressure\b|\bDruck\w*', case=False, regex=True, na=False)

      f"about this instrument. What they are about:")

What this section settles
PA_T1_47_1 is one instrument over the whole record, a Vaisala PTB101B with one conversion, never replaced, calibrated or cleaned according to the fieldbook. Its absolute level is right: the barometric formula, with nothing fitted, places it within a few metres of where it hangs from both references and reproduces the seasonal shape of the difference.
The record is not homogeneous: it steps by about 0.09 kPa at the January 2016 acquisition change, on the tower, and the later era agrees with the physics on average over 2016 to 2025. It is exported as measured (callout above). The December 2021 screening splice is clean.

title: Calculate VPD (2004-2026.09)
text:
ℹ️ About this notebook
Computes vapour pressure deficit VPD from the two products that precede it, and stores it to the external data folder. No download, no gap-filling: 02 and 04 must be run first.
VPD follows from TA and RH by formula. Both inputs are complete, so VPD is computed for every record and no model runs here. Both inputs come from one probe at 47 m, which changed twice: from a Rotronic MP101A to a Campbell CS215 on 21 January 2016, and to a Campbell HygroVUE10 on 5 June 2026. Notebooks 02 and 04 each export the measured series and a homogenised one that puts every probe era onto one level. VPD is computed on both bases and both are exported, on the pattern of 02, 04, 08 and 09:

VPD_T1_47_1 — from the measured pair, TA_T1_47_1_gfXG and RH_T1_47_1. This is the VPD the probe reported. It is the series that matches the measured TA and RH used as biomet input to EddyPro and as drivers in the flux processing chain. It steps where the probe changed.
VPD_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED — from the homogenised pair, TA_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED_gfXG and RH_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED. Use it for anything that crosses January 2016 or June 2026.
FLAG_VPD_T1_47_1_ISFILLED — what each record was computed from; 0 = measured TA and measured RH, >0 = one input was gap-filled or reconstructed (see FLAG_LEGEND). The homogenised inputs are filled at the same records as the measured ones, so this flag describes both value columns.
FLAG_VPD_T1_47_1_SOURCE — which probe, and which state of it, stands behind the record (the SOURCE flag of 02 and 04, carried over unchanged).

Changes against notebook version 3. Version 3 exported one column, computed from the homogenised TA and the measured RH, because 04 exported no homogenised RH at the time. That mixed basis corrected the temperature term and left the humidity term, and its step at 2016 was the largest of the bases scored below. 04 now exports a homogenised RH, so the mixed basis is computed here only as a diagnostic and is not exported. The column name VPD_T1_47_1 now stands for the measured pair, as TA_T1_47_1_gfXG and RH_T1_47_1 do in their products.
The section on the probe changes scores the three bases against MeteoSwiss Lägern, at January 2016 and at June 2026, and says which of the two comparisons is an independent test.

⏱️ Timestamp convention
Every input file already carries a sanitised, continuous 30MIN TIMESTAMP_MID index in local time, produced by the TimestampSanitizer call in the notebook that wrote it. title: Calculate VPD (2004-2026.09)
text:
⚙️ Settings

Data settings

REQUIRED_TIME_RESOLUTION = '30min'  # Expected resolution of the input files; asserted below

TARGET = "VPD_T1_47_1"                    # from the measured TA and RH
TARGET_HOM = "VPD_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED"    # from the homogenised TA and RH

# Last record (TIMESTAMP_MID). The file names say 2026.09; the inputs and the export are asserted
# to end here.
PERIOD_END = '2026-09-30 23:45:00'
# 2026 ends in September, so statistics that compare calendar years use years up to this one only.
LAST_FULL_YEAR = 2025

SITE_LAT = 47.478333  # CH-LAE
SITE_LON = 8.364389   # CH-LAE
TIMEZONE_OFFSET_TO_UTC_HOURS = 1  # local time UTC+01:00 (CET), the convention of every input

# Inputs: products of the earlier notebooks of this stage, in the external data folder.
# There is no database download in this notebook.
TA_FILE = "02_METEO_TA_GAPFILLED_2004-2026.09"
TA_COL = "TA_T1_47_1_gfXG"
TA_HOM_COL = "TA_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED_gfXG"
TA_FLAGCOL = "FLAG_TA_T1_47_1_ISFILLED"
TA_SOURCECOL = "FLAG_TA_T1_47_1_SOURCE"

RH_FILE = "04_METEO_RH_CORRECTED_2004-2026.09"
RH_COL = "RH_T1_47_1"
RH_HOM_COL = "RH_T1_47_1_HOMOGENIZED"
RH_FLAGCOL = "FLAG_RH_T1_47_1_MISSING"
RH_SOURCECOL = "FLAG_RH_T1_47_1_SOURCE"
RH_FLAG_RECONSTRUCTED = 3      # notebook 04: reconstructed from NABEL at 49 m
RH_FLAG_RECONSTRUCTED_LAE = 4  # notebook 04: reconstructed from MeteoSwiss Laegern at 2.5 km

# Reference: MeteoSwiss Laegern, 2.5 km from the tower, stored on TIMESTAMP_END. It carries both
# TA and RH, so a reference VPD follows from the same formula. Addressed by path, so a move breaks
# this read.
REFPATH = (r"<DATA_FOLDER>"
           r"\workflow\10_METEO\10_REFERENCE\MeteoSwiss_LAE_30MIN_2004-2026.09.parquet")
REFCOL_TA = "TA_LAE_MS"
REFCOL_RH = "RH_LAE_MS"

# The two probe changes, from notebooks 02 and 04. The acquisition change of January 2016: the last
# record of the analog era and the first of the SDI-12 era are 20 days apart, and 2016 belongs to
# neither era. The HygroVUE10 sample of 02 and 04 starts on HV_FIT_START, the day after its SDI-12
# configuration change, and is compared with the normal CS215 (code 0) on the same calendar dates of
# HV_CS215_YEARS. Both values are declared in 02 and repeated here, not read from it.
ACQUISITION_CHANGE = '2016-01-21 14:15:00'
BREAK_YEAR = 2016
HV_START = '2026-06-05 11:45:00'
HV_FIT_START = '2026-06-12 00:00:00'
HV_CS215_YEARS = [2022, 2023, 2024]

# Output: data files live in the external (untracked) data folder, with the same
# numeric prefix as this notebook.
OUTNAME = "07_METEO_VPD_2004-2026.09"
OUTPATH = r"<DATA_FOLDER>\workflow\10_METEO\30_PRODUCTS"

# Plausible VPD at this site, in kPa. VPD is zero at saturation and cannot be negative; the upper
# bound is generous (the record maximum is around 4 kPa) and only has to catch a unit or formula
# error, which would be off by a factor of 10 (hPa) or more.
VPD_PLAUSIBLE_KPA = (0.0, 10.0)



Imports

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

Last run: 2026-10-23 14:26:58
